Who do I call about a Hart County, KY tax bill?

Hart County runs its tax work from Main Street in Munfordville. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns each parcel a value, the sheriff takes the money, and the clerk records deeds and inherits bills that nobody paid.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 566, Munfordville, KY 42765, phone (270) 524-2321, weekday hours of 8 until 4.
  • Sheriff: 100 Main Street, phone (270) 524-2341. The county's sheriff page directs owners to hartcountysheriffky.com for online payment.
  • Clerk: 200 Main Street, phone (270) 524-2751, open weekdays 8 until 4 and Saturday mornings from 9 to noon.

State law names the sheriff as collector of state, county, school and special district taxes (KRS 134.119). The sheriff may take part payments, and a relative, tenant or lender can pay on the owner's behalf.

What should a seller know about Hart County's land and people?

Hart County is cave country in south central Kentucky, and nearly nine in ten residents (88.3 percent) were counted as rural in 2020. Hardin and Barren counties gave up land to form it in 1819. It spans 418 square miles and has two cities: Munfordville, the seat, and Horse Cave, the biggest.

Underground features define the west side. Part of Mammoth Cave National Park sits there, and the Fisher Ridge Cave System, charted at roughly 125 miles in 2018, passes beneath Hart County farms. Amish families began settling between Munfordville and Horse Cave in 1989, and 2,486 people, about 12.9 percent of the county, belonged to that community in 2020.

History left a mark on paperwork. The Battle of Munfordville took place in 1862, and a January 1928 courthouse fire consumed some county records. A seller of an older farm who finds holes in the title paperwork can ask the clerk what survives for that parcel.

The 2020 census recorded 7,418 households, of which 27.4 percent were single people living alone. Of 8,816 housing units, 15.9 percent stood vacant. Wikipedia's county profile labels the northern borders with Hardin and LaRue counties as the Eastern time boundary, while Hart County itself keeps Central time, so confirm which clock your closing office follows.

Which counties border Hart County, and how fast has it grown?

Seven counties touch Hart County: Hardin and LaRue to the north, Green to the east, Metcalfe to the southeast, Barren to the south, Edmonson to the southwest and Grayson to the northwest. Each neighbor runs its own PVA and sheriff, so a seller comparing listings across a county line deals with a different office.

Hart County's population climbed from 18,199 in 2010 to 19,288 in 2020, a gain of 6.0 percent, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate of 20,117 continues the trend. With 412.56 square miles of land, density works out to 46.8 people per square mile, up from 44.2 in 2010.

How affordable is housing in Hart County?

Census estimates covering 2020 through 2024 depict modest prices and a strong owner base. Owners occupy about 72 percent of homes, and the middle value sits at $146,000.

Hart County in figures, drawn from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table
ItemHart County

The population rose 4.3 percent from the April 2020 base to the July 2025 estimate. A Hart County household averages 2.62 people, and 89.9 percent of residents stayed in one house through the previous year. Among adults 25 and over, 81.2 percent finished high school and 12.2 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband reaches 83.7 percent of households.

Employers numbered 276 in 2023 and supplied 4,073 jobs. Retail sales came to about $244.8 million in 2022, or $12,492 for every resident, and the average commute runs 28.7 minutes. The poverty rate is 18.0 percent, and 1,002 residents are veterans.

When is a Hart County tax bill late?

Everything is due by the last day of the assessment year, and KRS 134.015 adds a reward for early payers and a surcharge for late ones.

  • On or before Nov. 1: the bill shrinks 2 percent when paid whole.
  • Nov. 2 through Dec. 31: face value.
  • January: face value plus 5 percent.
  • Later: face value plus 10 percent.

The PVA can tell you who is listed as owner on January 1, since that date controls the name printed on the bill. Someone who closes in spring will probably see the first bill arrive addressed to the seller, so decide at the table who covers it.

What can I do if Hart County values my property too high?

Talk to the PVA, and if that fails, petition the county board of assessment appeals. The process sits in KRS 133.120, rewritten by the 2026 General Assembly with an effective date of July 15, 2026.

  1. Ask for a conference with the PVA or a deputy. Phone conferences are allowed on request.
  2. Still unhappy? Put the appeal in writing and deliver it to the clerk's office by the workday after inspection closes. Cover three points: your objections, the parcel's identity, and your own valuation.
  3. Show up at the hearing with documents: listings, comparable sales, insurance records, building cost or loan papers. A petition with no facts behind it is denied.

The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends (KRS 133.030) and visits the property when asked. Meanwhile you owe tax on the number you claimed, and the board's final number may bring a bill for the difference.

Can Hart County homeowners get a homestead exemption?

Yes, for a person over 65 or totally disabled who lives in the house. The Revenue Department's deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100. Against the county's $146,000 Census median, taxable value would fall to $96,900. File with the Hart County PVA, and report a sale so the deduction ends at the old address.

What happens to unpaid taxes when a Hart County house sells?

Back taxes ride along with the land. A lien for delinquency under KRS 134.420 stays attached after a sale, which is why title searches find it.

Ask the sheriff for a payoff before listing. Once claims pass to the clerk, KRS 134.119 piles a collection fee on top (ten percent of the tax plus ten percent of the penalty), and an investor may buy the certificate and add interest. Closing offers the cleanest fix: the title company deducts the payoff from your proceeds.

How does transfer tax work when a Hart County house sells?

The seller pays a Kentucky levy of $0.50 on each $500 of price, or part of $500. The clerk takes the money first and records afterward (KRS 142.050). At $146,000 that is $146. The clerk's office on Main Street in Munfordville holds the county's land records, so call for the current recording charge.

More questions about Hart County, KY Property Tax Guide

Which office mails the Hart County tax bill?

The sheriff, at (270) 524-2341. The PVA supplies the value, and the clerk picks up claims the sheriff could not collect.

How large is the homestead deduction for Hart County owners?

$49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It goes to owners over 65 or totally disabled who apply with the PVA at (270) 524-2321.

Does Hart County reward early payment?

Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 cuts it 2 percent. Missing December 31 adds 5 percent through January and 10 percent after that.

Do I stop paying while my Hart County appeal is pending?

No. Meanwhile you owe tax on the figure you claimed, and a higher ruling brings a second bill with interest.

Can a Hart County house with back taxes be sold?

Yes, with the debt settled at closing. Obtain a payoff from the sheriff and have the title company send it from your proceeds.

Boyd County by the numbers

Which Boyd County offices handle property tax?

Three do. The Property Valuation Administrator sets values. The Sheriff's Office bills and collects for the current year. The County Clerk picks up older delinquent bills.

The county's Property Valuation page says the PVA values all real and personal property in Boyd County, except items the Kentucky Department of Revenue assigns itself, such as public service companies, bank shares and vehicles. The PVA's mailing address is PO Box 434, Catlettsburg, KY 41129. For a house, the PVA's number is the starting point of everything else on the bill.

What is Boyd County's tax base like?

Land area is about 160 square miles, with roughly 300 residents per square mile, and 76.2% of people lived in urban areas at the 2020 count. The estimated 2025 population was 47,751 in about 21,818 housing units.

Boyd County's typical owner-occupied home is valued at $130,700 by the Census Bureau, and the typical household brings in $61,118. Owners live in 70.2% of homes. A house priced near that level carries a smaller assessment than most Bluegrass homes, yet the 911 fee and city levies still show up on the bill.

  • Ashland and Catlettsburg bill their own city property tax, and you call the city, not the county.
  • The county bill lists a 911 service fee, with questions going to Boyd County 911 at 606-329-2191.
  • Three school districts cover different parts of the county: Boyd County Public Schools, Ashland Independent and Fairview Independent.

When are Boyd County property taxes due?

The Sheriff's Office follows the calendar in KRS 134.015: a reward for paying early, a flat middle stretch and two steps of penalty.

Kentucky property tax payment schedule under KRS 134.015, applied by the Boyd County Sheriff
Payment timingResult
By November 12% discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount, no penalty
January 1 to January 315% penalty
After January 3110% penalty

The county's property tax page says online viewing and payment are available through the Sheriff's Office. Dates on a printed bill can run later than the statute's calendar when the state allows an alternative collection schedule, so read the bill and ask the sheriff's office which dates apply to your parcel. When the sheriff's collection period ends, unpaid prior year taxes move to the County Clerk, who handles them at 606-739-5116, option 4.

How do I contest a Boyd County assessment?

Go to the PVA first. The assessment date is January 1. When a property's value goes up from the prior year, the PVA mails the owner a notice of change.

The Boyd County PVA's appeals page explains the order of steps. Your first step is a conference with the PVA or a deputy. The window is six days a week for two weeks, starting the first Monday in May, though dates can shift. When the conference ends without agreement, a written petition to the County Clerk gets you a hearing before the board of assessment appeals, as KRS 133.120 provides.

  • Bring comparable sales, an appraisal, photos of damage or a contractor's repair estimate.
  • You may ask to hold the conference by phone.
  • The petition must give your reasons and your opinion of the property's fair cash value.
  • Keep paying while you appeal, since an appeal does not hold up the tax.

Does Boyd County have a homestead exemption?

Boyd County follows the statewide homestead exemption for owners who reach 65 or are classed as totally disabled. For the two years covering 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100.

File with the Boyd County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability claims need proof of a total-disability classification from a federal or retirement program. They are refiled yearly, except for veterans with service-connected disability and owners found permanently disabled.

What are the key dates in a Boyd County assessment year?

  • January 1: the assessment date for every property.
  • First Monday in May: the roll inspection period normally opens, and the PVA conferences begin.
  • Third Monday in May: the inspection period normally ends, and the written petition follows within a workday.
  • November 1: the last day for the 2% discount.
  • December 31: the last day to pay the plain face amount.
  • January 31: the last day before the 10% penalty.

The county's tax page posts a notice when each year's collection begins. Read the dates printed on your own bill, since the state can set an alternative schedule.

Who can speak for me in a Boyd County assessment appeal?

You can appear yourself, or you can use an agent. Kentucky law limits who may be paid to represent an owner at a PVA conference or a board hearing.

  • An attorney or a certified public accountant.
  • A tax consultant or a Kentucky licensed real estate broker or sales associate.
  • An employee of the property owner.
  • A licensed or certified Kentucky real property appraiser.

An agent carries written authorization from you and discloses any personal stake, such as a contingency fee. Losing at the county board leaves one more stop, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, open only to owners who went to the county board first.

What does a late Boyd County payment cost on a sample bill?

Use a bill of $1,000 for illustration. Paid by November 1 it is $980. Paid from November 2 through December 31 it is $1,000. In January the 5% penalty brings it to $1,050, and after January 31 the 10% statutory penalty brings it to $1,100. Extra charges can attach after a bill moves to the clerk, so get a payoff figure from that office before closing.

These figures show the statute's calendar only. Your own bill carries the county, school and district amounts plus the 911 fee, and the Sheriff's Office can tell you the exact total for your parcel.

What else do Census numbers show about Boyd County owners?

The county's poverty rate was 18.0% in the Census figures, and 17.2% of residents under 65 reported a disability. Owner costs run $1,217 a month with a mortgage and $463 without, and 85.9% of residents stayed put over the past year.

For an owner on a fixed income, the homestead exemption and an on-time payment in the discount window matter more than a small difference in value. Before listing, read the due dates on the bill and ask the PVA whether an exemption application is on file.

What if I sell a Boyd County house with taxes owed?

Delinquent tax attaches to the house as a lien, and the debt itself belongs to the owner as of the assessment date. A title company will want any unpaid bill cleared at closing.

  • This year's bill unpaid: the Sheriff's Office gives the exact amount.
  • An older year unpaid: the County Clerk's office quotes it.
  • City tax questions: City of Ashland, 606-385-3275, or City of Catlettsburg, 606-739-5223.
  • Escrow: ask the lender whether it has already paid.

If you cannot pay beforehand, have the closing agent take it from your proceeds.

More questions about Boyd County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who collects property tax in Boyd County?

The Boyd County Sheriff's Office collects the current year's tax. The County Clerk collects delinquent taxes from prior years.

What is the Boyd County property tax discount?

KRS 134.015 allows 2% off for payment in full by November 1, then the plain amount until December 31. The dates printed on your bill control.

How do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes?

Call the Boyd County Clerk's office at 606-739-5116 and press option 4, or use the clerk's website.

When can I meet with the Boyd County PVA about my assessment?

Before the roll inspection window ends. The Boyd PVA says it normally opens the first Monday in May and closes the third Monday.

Do Ashland and Catlettsburg charge their own property tax?

Yes. Questions about city property tax go to the City of Ashland at 606-385-3275 or the City of Catlettsburg at 606-739-5223.

Where is Breckinridge County, and what is it like for homeowners?

Breckinridge County stretches along the Ohio River in western Kentucky, facing Perry County, Indiana. At 586 square miles, 567 of them land, it is the biggest of the four counties compared here. Hardinsburg is the seat and the largest city, with Cloverport and Irvington as the other two cities. Grayson, Ohio and Hancock counties adjoin it, and Meade and Hardin lie to the east.

The county was split from Hardin County in 1799 and was the 38th formed in Kentucky. Cloverport once shipped coal oil from the Victoria mines, and Rough River Dam State Resort Park opened up the southern edge in the 1950s. A local-option vote on January 29, 2013 ended 105 years of prohibition, making Breckinridge a wet county.

During the Civil War, Confederate cavalry burned the courthouse while Union troops were using it as a barracks, though most records were saved. Breckinridge County Public Library sits at 308 Old Highway 60 in Hardinsburg, and Saint Romuald Interparochial School is the private school.

Breckinridge runs on Central time, and the Meade and Hardin side to the east keeps Eastern time. A seller lining up a closing with offices across that line should confirm each office's clock.

What do the Census numbers show for Breckinridge housing?

The July 2025 estimate is 21,503 residents, 5.2 percent above the 2020 count of 20,432, which edges out Bullitt's 5.1 percent for fastest growth among the four. With 35.9 people per square mile, it is also the thinnest settled.

  • An owner's home has a middle value of $156,700 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owners live in 81.4 percent of housing units, across 8,069 households.
  • Rent in the middle runs $733 a month, and monthly owner costs in the middle are $1,210 with a mortgage and $377 without one.
  • Household income in the middle is $55,843, and 18.3 percent of residents are below the poverty line.
  • Only 14 building permits were issued for 2025, against 10,952 housing units.

At the 2020 count about a quarter of the 10,704 housing units sat vacant, far above Bullitt's share. Few new homes compete with existing ones. Labor force participation among residents 16 and older is 52.6 percent, the average commute is 32.7 minutes, and 283 employers provided 2,480 jobs in 2023, down 0.8 percent from 2022. Retail sales for 2022 were $217.4 million, about $10,370 per resident, and the county counts 1,384 veterans. Broadband reaches 83.9 percent of households, a point to raise when buyers work remotely.

Which Breckinridge County office does what?

The sheriff bills and collects, the PVA values property, and the county clerk takes over unpaid bills. The Sheriff's Office is at 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, open weekdays eight to four Central. The phone is 270-756-2361 and the mailing box is PO Box 127. It collects about $11 million a year on behalf of the state, county, schools and special districts.

Assessment and homestead questions go to the PVA at 270-756-5154. Past-due real estate bills go to the County Clerk (270-756-2246), who quotes payoff amounts.

What are the Breckinridge County tax payment dates?

For the 2026 bills the sheriff said mailing would finish by October 29, and an owner without a bill by November 10 should ask for a duplicate. Online lookup and payment run from November 1 through 4 p.m. Central on April 15. Postmarks count.

Breckinridge County Sheriff's payment stages on the 2026 bills
WindowAmount owed
November 1 to 30Face amount less 2%
December 1 to 31Face amount
January 1 to 31Face amount plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21%
After April 15Pay at the County Clerk's office

Statute and the Revenue Cabinet fix these dates and percentages, and the sheriff cannot bend them.

How does paying a Breckinridge County bill work?

The sheriff takes only the exact amount printed on the bill. A short payment is mailed back, and installments are not offered. One payment may cover several bills.

  • Online: a processing fee of 1.5 percent, minimum $1.50, applies on the first $60, and 2.5 percent on anything over $60. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and eCheck work.
  • Mail or counter: a check or money order with the voucher.
  • Fire dues: a signed opt-out form has to accompany the payment, so owners opting out pay by mail or at the counter.

Your cancelled check is the receipt, or enclose a stamped, addressed envelope for a mailed one.

How are taxes split when a Breckinridge County house sells?

The bill is made out to whoever owned on January 1. Selling after that date still leaves the bill in your name, and you pass it to the new owner. The closing agent usually allocates each side's portion on the settlement statement.

The sheriff will not accept two prorated checks. One party or the other has to pay the full bill, so ask the closing attorney who carries the payment and whether the buyer gets a credit.

How can a Breckinridge County owner dispute a valuation?

Values are set as of January 1, and the PVA's crews revisit every property about once in four years. If a new value seems wrong, schedule a conference with the PVA while the roll is open to inspection, which begins in early May and lasts thirteen days.

Only after that conference can you file with the county clerk, who serves as clerk to the local appeals board. The board meets about a month after inspection closes. Bring photos, a repair bid, an appraisal or comparable sales, since boards decide on paper and an appeal without it is denied.

Is there a senior or disability break in Breckinridge County?

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classed as totally disabled, may claim the homestead exemption on the house they live in, up to $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. About 21.6 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 92.5 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. The sheriff sends every exemption question to the PVA, and says that checking for an exemption is the first move when a bill feels heavy.

What happens to unpaid Breckinridge County property tax?

The sheriff treats a bill as delinquent after April 15, or after the tax day assigned for that year, and extra penalties may apply. After April 15 the sheriff drops the bill and it shows up at the clerk as delinquent, with a lien on the property. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, commissions for the clerk and county attorney follow, and notices and advertising come before any sale. The Department of Revenue posts each county's delinquent list online by June 1, and on a normal schedule a sale can fall between July 14 and August 28. A third party can buy a bill that reaches the sale list. Anyone selling a house here with old tax owing should order the payoff before closing so the title company can pay it from the sale.

More questions about Breckinridge County, KY Property Tax Guide

What is the Breckinridge County sheriff's tax office address?

208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. Payments by mail go to PO Box 127, and the phone is 270-756-2361.

Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax online?

Yes, starting November 1. A convenience fee applies, and the payment must equal the exact bill amount.

Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax in installments?

No. The sheriff accepts the full amount shown on the bill, though one payment can cover several bills.

When does the 21 percent penalty start in Breckinridge County?

On February 1, and it runs through April 15. After that the bill goes to the County Clerk as delinquent.

Who pays the tax on a Breckinridge County house I sold in June?

The January 1 owner is billed. The closing agent usually prorates the year, but the sheriff still needs the whole bill paid at once.

Which Garrard County office answers which tax question?

The PVA owns the value, and the sheriff owns the bill. The county's own site stresses that the PVA neither sets rates nor collects, and the sheriff's page says the sheriff never assesses property, so an argument over the figure goes to one office and a question about paying goes to the other.

Both sit at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster. The PVA answers at (859) 792-3291 on weekdays during the 8 to 4 day, and the sheriff's number is (859) 792-3591. Think of the PVA as a state office with a local address. State revenue officials supervise it, and every parcel is valued at full fair cash value as of January 1.

The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts. The list covers state and county levies, school districts, and special districts for things like fire protection and libraries. Bills go out on October 1 every year with instructions on due dates, penalties, mortgage-company payment and ways to pay. The County Clerk, at 15 Public Square, Suite 5, records deeds and helps notify and collect on delinquent bills.

What should I know about Garrard County before selling?

Garrard County is in east-central Kentucky and has 230 square miles of land. Rolling Bluegrass country fills most of it, and the southeast corner near Cartersville falls in the Knobs. Lancaster, the seat and the only city, started as a cluster of log cabins in 1776, and the county was formed in 1796 from parts of Lincoln, Mercer and Madison counties, making it the 25th in the state.

Lexington is about 28 miles north. Outside Lancaster you find Paint Lick, Bryantsville, Buckeye, Cartersville, Davis Town and Hyattsville, and the 2020 census classed all residents as rural. The Civil War left its mark here: Camp Dick Robinson served as the first Federal base south of the Ohio River. A tobacco heritage festival takes place every September, and voters ended the county's dry status on November 7, 2023.

The county has gained residents quickly, and the average commute is long.

  • Population: 18,207 in the 2025 estimate, up 7.4 percent from 2020.
  • Home values: $204,900 is the survey median for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owner-occupied share: 79.9 percent, the highest among Floyd, Franklin, Gallatin and Garrard.
  • Average commute: 33.1 minutes, the longest among those four.
  • New-home permits in 2025: 0.
  • Median gross rent: $794. Median household income: $63,087.

In 2020 the census counted 7,254 housing units, 9.2 percent of them empty, and 6,584 households. With no permits recorded in 2025, sales are mostly of existing houses and acreage.

The local economy is small and heavily self-employed. The Census Bureau lists 251 employer businesses in 2023 with 1,654 jobs and a $71.4 million payroll, against 1,572 businesses with no employees. Retail sales were about $80.8 million in 2022, or $4,600 per resident, a fraction of the Franklin County figure of $19,603, a much smaller per-person total. Just over half of adults (54.7 percent) are working or looking for work, and the Census Bureau shows 18.7 percent with a four-year degree. The county government is run by a fiscal court of a judge executive and five magistrates, and the courthouse in Lancaster is one of the oldest in continuous use in Kentucky.

When is the Garrard County bill due, and what is the discount?

The sheriff expects payment by December 31, and bills leave on October 1, so the early-payment window is about a month long. Under KRS 134.015, paying the entire bill by November 1 trims 2 percent. A January payment costs an extra 5 percent, and later ones cost 10 percent.

When statewide mailing runs late, Revenue can substitute a short calendar: a month with the discount, a month at face, then a month with the 5 percent charge. Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's tax personally, so an early-year closing needs a clear agreement on the bill.

How much does a late Garrard County bill cost?

A lot more. Unpaid bills change hands on April 15, moving from the sheriff to the County Clerk with a lien recorded on the parcel. The state illustrates the climb with a $1,000 bill and a sheriff commission assumed at 4 percent, so your own totals will differ.

What one unpaid $1,000 bill costs over the weeks after transfer (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue worked examples)
Payment dateAmount owed
The day the sheriff hands it over, with penalty, add-on and commission$1,254.00
Within a week of the handover$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first letter$1,611.30
In May, a second month of interest$1,627.61
In June, once the newspaper ad has run$1,659.90

Interest is 1 percent per month. A 30-day notice and a second notice come from the county attorney, and the clerk's sale is set 90 to 135 days after transfer. When a certificate sells to an outside buyer, you owe that buyer plus its additional fees.

What should a Garrard County seller do about taxes before closing?

Treat the tax bill as part of the sale paperwork. Because the sheriff mails bills in October and the debt belongs to whoever held the property on January 1, a house that closes in spring or summer may still have a bill outstanding in the seller's name.

  • Phone the sheriff's office at (859) 792-3591 for the amount due on the parcel.
  • Ask the County Clerk at (859) 792-3071 how to record the deed, since the clerk's office archives deeds and mortgages.
  • Tell the PVA at (859) 792-3291 who the new owner is so later notices and any exemption follow the right person.
  • Keep the paid receipt with your closing file, because the buyer's title search will otherwise show the balance as open.

An owner behind on taxes and facing repairs on an older farmhouse may also weigh a direct sale to a buyer that closes as-is, which avoids carrying the bill through a long listing.

How can a Garrard County owner appeal?

Meet with the PVA, then file with the County Clerk. The roll is open for 13 days beginning in early May, and the conference comes first. File by the end of the next business day after viewing closes.

A local board of assessment appeals then meets about four to five weeks later and rules on documented evidence: comparable listings, construction costs, photographs. It must give written reasons for a change. A paid representative must be an attorney, appraiser or another approved professional carrying your written authorization.

Is there a homestead exemption for Garrard County owners?

Seniors and totally disabled owners can subtract $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA on Stanford Street. At the county's typical home value of $204,900, the taxable amount would be $155,800.

To show age, bring a birth certificate, license or passport. A seller who has held the exemption should tell the PVA after closing so it ends at that address.

More questions about Garrard County, KY Property Tax Guide

When do Garrard County tax bills go out?

They are mailed on October 1 each year, according to the Garrard County Sheriff. Payment in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount.

Who should I call if a Garrard County tax value looks wrong?

Call the Garrard County PVA at (859) 792-3291. The sheriff's office says it never assesses value and refers those questions to the PVA.

Where is the Garrard County sheriff's tax office?

It is at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster, KY 40444, with a phone at (859) 792-3591. The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts.

What changes for Garrard County taxes still open on April 15?

The bill moves to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent per month starts, and clerk and attorney commissions follow.

What is the Garrard County homestead exemption worth?

It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, taken off the assessed value of a home owned by a senior or a totally disabled person.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Payments in the 10% penalty period before transfer to clerk carry additional 10% sheriff's fee; delinquent bills transfer to County Clerk at close of business 4/15/2027, then subject to 20% County Attorney fee, 10% clerk fee, 1% per month interest, and possible sale to third party

What we could not confirm

  • Millage rates not researched
  • Online payment not available per sheriff page (confirm)

Which Montgomery County offices deal with property tax?

Setting a parcel's worth and collecting on it are different jobs here. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) answers the first question. The Sheriff's Office prints and collects the bills.

  • PVA, (859) 498-8710: questions about value, the tax roll and exemption forms.
  • Sheriff, (859) 498-8704: amounts due. Checks go to 1 Court Street, Suite 4, Mt. Sterling, KY 40353, with the bill number written on them.
  • County Clerk, (859) 498-8700: recording a deed, and any bill that has gone delinquent.

The sheriff's site lets you view and print bills and receipts but offers no way to pay on the web. Anyone who wants a receipt mailed back should enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope with the check.

What is Montgomery County like beyond the tax office?

Land in the county rises and falls between 707 and 1,447 feet above sea level, across 197 square miles of the Outer Bluegrass. Clark County gave up the territory in 1796. The Census Bureau estimates 28,822 residents for 2025, a gain of 2.5% since the 2020 base.

Mount Sterling, the seat, lies 34 miles east of Lexington. The town received its first courthouse soon after the county's creation, and Wikipedia counts seven courthouses built there since. In June 1864 the Battle of Mount Sterling ended in a Confederate defeat, the last fighting in the county. The Montgomery County School District serves the county and includes Montgomery County High School. Interstate 64 clips the north edge of town at exits 110 and 113, while U.S. 60 and U.S. 460 cross downtown. Workers here report an average commute of 25.7 minutes. Wikipedia describes the area as a micropolitan area inside the Lexington combined statistical area, and notes that Mount Sterling is a wet city in an otherwise dry county for package alcohol.

Zoning is uneven. The fiscal court says there is no countywide planning and zoning, yet subdivisions within five miles of Mt. Sterling must meet the city's zoning and subdivision rules. Anyone planning to split a lot before a sale should call city hall first. Each October, Court Day brings roughly 130,000 visitors to downtown over four days, which is worth knowing before scheduling showings that weekend.

How does Montgomery County housing look in Census data?

QuickFacts gives a picture of a county with a sizable rental segment and moderate prices. The figures below cover 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

  • 12,422 housing units in 2025, and 53 building permits that year.
  • Homeowners live in 68.3% of occupied units, leaving close to a third to renters.
  • Census puts the midpoint of an owned home at $172,200.
  • Monthly ownership costs are $1,242 for mortgage holders and $470 for owners with no loan.
  • Renters pay a midpoint of $830 in gross rent.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $56,396, and 15.5% of people live below the poverty line.

Nearly nine in ten residents (88.3%) stayed put during the previous year. A seller with deferred repairs can expect a slower sale than one with a tidy house.

What are the 2026 Montgomery County due dates?

The sheriff reports that 2026 bills were mailed in the last week of September and became payable October 1, 2026. The calendar below is the one the sheriff approved for this tax year.

Sheriff's approved collection dates, 2026 tax year
DatesWhat the bill becomes
10/01/2026 through 11/01/2026Two percent comes off
11/02/2026 through 12/31/2026Printed total, no adjustment
01/01/2027 through 01/31/2027Five percent is tacked on
02/01/2027 through 04/15/2027Twenty-one percent is tacked on

A sheriff's note says a payment made while the 10% penalty applies, before the bill is handed to the clerk, carries one more 10% sheriff's fee. At close of business on April 15, 2027, delinquent bills transfer to the County Clerk. From then on a 20% County Attorney fee, a 10% clerk fee and 1% interest each month apply, and the clerk may sell a bill still unpaid to a third party in summer 2027.

What would a $1,500 Montgomery County bill cost at each stage?

In the discount window it is $1,470. Through December it is $1,500. January raises it to $1,575, and the February to mid-April stretch lifts it to $1,815. Between the best and worst sheriff dates lies $345.

A past-due bill belongs to the clerk after April 15, and the clerk gives the payoff. A seller who owes an earlier year should ask for that figure before picking a closing date. If your lender pays the tax from escrow, or a prior owner is responsible, the sheriff asks that you pass the bill along so it is paid on time.

How can an owner push back on a Montgomery County valuation?

Values are pinned to January 1. Under KRS 133.120, the first step is a sit-down with the PVA or a deputy, which may be held by phone. KRS 133.045 opens the tax roll for inspection for 13 days from the first Monday of May, unless the Department of Revenue picks other dates.

If that talk fails, put your complaint in writing and deliver it to the County Clerk. Name the parcel, say why the number is wrong and state what you believe it is worth. The hearing is before the county appeals board, and the burden is on you to bring evidence such as an appraisal, listings or a builder's estimate.

Pay on your own figure while the case is open. If the final number rises, you owe the difference plus interest. Skipping the county hearing forfeits the later route to the state Board of Tax Appeals.

Does a Montgomery County owner qualify for homestead relief?

The state exemption is $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026, and it is open to anyone 65 or over or classified as totally disabled. A home appraised at $172,200 would be taxed as if it were worth $123,100.

The PVA takes the form at (859) 498-8710. Age is shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claimants must reapply each year, with carve-outs for service-connected veterans and for people whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has found permanently and totally disabled.

How should a Montgomery County seller treat the tax bill at closing?

Whoever owns the house on January 1 is the taxpayer for that year, and a purchase later in the year leaves the bill under the previous owner's name. KRS 134.015 calls the tax a personal debt of that owner. A lien from unpaid tax can last 11 years under KRS 134.420 and passes to the next buyer along with the land.

  • Ask the sheriff whether this year's bill is settled, and what payoff applies on the day of closing.
  • Decide in the sales contract who bears which months of tax.
  • Enter the buyer's address for later tax mailings on the deed, since KRS 382.135 demands it.
  • Record the signed deed at the County Clerk's office.

Title companies search for old bills, so paying any early prevents a hold-up at closing.

More questions about Montgomery County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who sends the Montgomery County tax bill?

The Sheriff's Office, which can be reached at (859) 498-8704. Call the PVA at (859) 498-8710 only when the assessed value looks wrong.

Is online payment offered by the Montgomery County Sheriff?

No. Bills and receipts can be viewed and printed on the sheriff's site, but payment must be mailed or brought in at 1 Court Street, Suite 4, Mt. Sterling.

What are the penalty periods after December 31 in Montgomery County?

Five percent applies in January, then twenty-one percent runs from February 1 to April 15. Delinquent bills then move to the County Clerk, who adds attorney and clerk fees plus monthly interest.

Is there zoning in Montgomery County outside Mt. Sterling?

There is none countywide. Subdivisions within five miles of Mt. Sterling follow the city's rules, so ask city hall before dividing land.

What does the state homestead exemption take off a Montgomery County home?

Forty-nine thousand one hundred dollars comes off the assessed figure for the 2025 and 2026 years. Applicants need to be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and file at the PVA.

Where are the Edmonson County tax offices?

Three counters matter to a seller in Edmonson County, and all sit in Brownsville. Valuation belongs to the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), whose office is inside the courthouse on Main Cross Street; the phone there is 270-597-2381. Payment belongs to the sheriff at 110 Jackson Street (270-597-2157). Anything late, plus the land records, goes through the county clerk at 108 North Main Street (270-597-2624).

County government keeps weekday hours starting at 7:30 and ending at 4:00, and its welcome page boasts that the county has no stoplight. The PVA's website links a qPublic parcel search, which shows how a particular house is assessed before anyone picks up the phone.

No single office decides the total bill. The PVA supplies the value, while the levy comes from the taxing bodies, among them the fiscal court and the county school system. For the combined rate on one parcel, ask the sheriff.

What is the Edmonson County tax calendar?

Bills leave the sheriff's office on October 30, which is later than the statewide default of September, so the calendar here starts and ends a month behind the usual one. A homeowner with no bill by November 15 should ring the sheriff, who mails a duplicate right away. The slower start fits the alternative schedule in KRS 134.015, which gives each stage one month when bills are delayed.

What the Edmonson County Sheriff charges at each stage of the collection year
When you payWhat you owe
Paid by November 30Bill less 2%
All of DecemberBill as printed
All of JanuaryBill plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Bill plus 21%

That 21 percent is a 10 percent penalty with a 10 percent sheriff fee stacked on it. Whatever remains unpaid when April 15 ends goes to the clerk.

The sheriff takes cash at the counter, plus checks, money orders and cards (processing fees apply to cards, by phone or in the office). The office opens at 7:30 every day it is open, closes at 4:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and closes at noon on Thursday and Saturday.

How does an Edmonson County owner contest a valuation?

Talk to the PVA first; the appeal comes second. Values are struck on January 1; houses can be listed with the PVA through March 1, and business equipment through May 15.

  • The assessment roll lies open for thirteen days starting on the first May Monday, including Saturdays.
  • A conference with the PVA or a deputy unlocks the right to appeal. The appeal form then goes to the clerk's office, due the workday after the inspection window shuts.
  • The local board sits for no more than five days, opening between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends.
  • Evidence decides the outcome: insurance policies, building costs, listings and physical details of the land. An appeal with none is denied.
  • Skipping a scheduled hearing forfeits any further review at the Kentucky Claims Commission.

If bills print while an appeal is pending, they use the owner's stated figure, and a supplemental bill covers any increase the board later sets.

How far does the homestead exemption go in Edmonson County?

The state deducts $49,100 from a qualifying home's value, and that figure applies to the 2025 and 2026 rolls. Owners qualify at 65 or when classified as totally disabled, and the PVA takes the application.

Apply that to a house worth $160,300, the Census typical value in this county, and the taxable figure falls to $111,200, about 31 percent lower. For proof of age, a birth certificate, license or passport will do. A disability claim rests on classification under a federal program or a retirement system, with payments received over the whole year. Disability claims are renewed every year, unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Can I sell an Edmonson County house while taxes are unpaid?

The debt rides with the land. The lien outlives a change of owner: KRS 134.420 keeps it alive for up to 11 years on a parcel whose tax went unpaid, so a title search at closing will turn it up.

After April 15 the clerk holds the bill as a certificate of delinquency, interest builds by 1 percent each month, and the county attorney sends written notice well before a sale. Kentucky puts the sale 90 to 135 days after the handover. In 2025 the clerk ran the list of 2024 bills in The Edmonson News on August 13 and held the sale on September 16 at 11:00 a.m. Buyers registered by September 5 and posted 25 percent of the face value of the certificates they hoped to win.

Paying the clerk in full before the sale date ends the matter, and money that shows up later is sent back. Some bills are pulled from the list under KRS 134.504. Call 270-597-2624 for a payoff figure ahead of listing.

As grantor, the seller owes transfer tax of one dollar per $1,000 of price, which is how the $0.50 per $500 rate works out. At $160,300 that is $160.50. Recording a five-page deed adds $33 under KRS 64.012.

Why does Edmonson County's setting matter when selling a house?

The legislature set Edmonson County apart on January 12, 1825, using land from Grayson, Hart and Warren, and named it for Captain John Edmonson, who died at the Battle of Frenchtown in 1813. It spans 303 square miles of land inside the Bowling Green metro area, with Brownsville serving as seat and sole town. About a quarter of the county falls inside Mammoth Cave National Park, and the Green and Nolin rivers shape the rest, with Nolin Lake State Park in the north. Alcohol sales are prohibited.

Roads are state routes. KY 70 runs across the county from west to east, KY 101 runs north to south, KY 259 crosses the Green River on the county's only bridge over it, and KY 185 ties the west side to Bowling Green. Interstate 65 touches the southeastern corner without an interchange. The five schools of the Edmonson County system include a combined middle and high school complex in Brownsville. Community events include the Lions Club Fair and its parade in early September, Nolin Fest at the lake and the Big Brownsville Bash in June.

Census figures show 12,749 residents in 2025, a gain of 5.1 percent on the 2020 count, along with these details:

  • 80.1 percent of housing is owner-occupied, across 5,099 households.
  • A typical owned home is worth $160,300; a typical monthly rent runs $778.
  • Household income sits around $54,937.
  • Workers face an average drive of nearly 33 minutes.
  • Roughly one adult in ten holds a bachelor's degree.

Because most owners hold their houses long term and drive a long way to work, sales tend to be of older homes. A seller facing back taxes or repairs can compare a listing against a straight as-is sale for cash.

More questions about Edmonson County, KY Property Tax Guide

When does the Edmonson County tax discount end?

The 2 percent discount ends on November 30 under the sheriff's calendar, because bills are mailed October 30. December is face value, and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

Where does an Edmonson County owner send the payment?

Take it to the sheriff's office at 110 Jackson Street in Brownsville, or post a check or money order to that same address. The counter takes cash. Cards go through by phone or in the office and carry a fee.

Who sets my Edmonson County property value?

The PVA sets it, working from January 1 values. Its office is in the courthouse, phone 270-597-2381, and neither the sheriff nor the fiscal court has a say in the value.

Can I appeal my Edmonson County assessment later in the year?

No. Every appeal starts with a PVA conference while the May tax roll is open to inspection, and the clerk's filing window closes one workday after the roll does.

What does Edmonson County do with unpaid property taxes?

Bills left unpaid at the April 15 cutoff pass to the clerk, where 1 percent interest accrues monthly. The clerk advertises them in late summer and holds a tax sale, and payments must reach the clerk in full before the sale date.

Hopkins County by the numbers

Who values and who collects in Hopkins County?

Hopkins County divides the work between its PVA and its Sheriff. The PVA's staff lists every taxable parcel, measures and photographs buildings, puts a value on each and builds the tax roll that the public may inspect. The office is in the Courthouse Annex, 25 East Center Street, Madisonville, KY 42431, telephone (270) 821-3092.

Billing and collection sit with the Sheriff's Office at 261 Responders Lane, phone 270-821-5661, which serves taxpayers on weekdays between eight and four. Bills still open after April 15 belong to the Hopkins County Clerk, reachable at 270-326-2097.

Bills are written to the name on the parcel as of January 1. A spring buyer may find the old owner still receiving it, and that person should forward it. The Sheriff cannot see new deeds, so a buyer who hears nothing can ring the office or print a copy online.

What does the Hopkins County collection calendar look like?

Mailing normally happens about September 30, and the counter opens October 1. The Sheriff posts four stages through April 15.

Stages of the Hopkins County Sheriff's yearly tax collection (source: Hopkins County Sheriff's Office FAQ)
StageWhat changes
October 1 to November 12 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 315 percent added
February 1 to April 1521 percent added

The Sheriff's FAQ prints 21 percent for that final stage. KRS 134.015 itself names only a 10 percent penalty after January, and Revenue's explainer lists a sheriff's add-on fee and commission separately. Call for an exact payoff before paying in February or March.

Sheriff collection stops when business closes on April 15, and whatever is left moves to the Clerk.

Which payment methods does the Hopkins County Sheriff accept?

The office takes online payments and counter payments, and it insists on the whole amount. A partial payment is turned down.

  • Accepted: cash, personal checks, money orders, cashier's checks and cards.
  • An outside processor runs cards and charges 2.5 percent plus 30 cents.
  • Online checks cost $1.50 to process.
  • Write checks to Hopkins County Sheriff.

Escrow does not lift the owner's duty. The Sheriff says the taxpayer must get the bill to the mortgage lender, and a lender cannot pay what it never receives.

How do I estimate and prorate a Hopkins County bill?

The bill math runs as taxable assessment divided by 100, times the rate set for the year. Volunteer fire department fees or watershed taxes, where they apply, are added separately.

The Sheriff's FAQ also gives a sale formula. Divide the last year's bill by 365 for a daily cost, then multiply by the number of days the seller lived in the house. Someone who sells at the end of June would owe 181 days of that daily amount.

Some closing agents wait for the real bill. Compare their number with the Sheriff's method before you sign the settlement statement, and ask which year's bill each of you used.

How do I fight a Hopkins County assessment?

Start with the PVA's office. Under KRS 133.120, a conference with the PVA or a deputy has to come first, ahead of or during the inspection period, and callers can ask to hold it by telephone.

  • The PVA walks through how the number was set and writes up the meeting.
  • If that fails, send the County Clerk a letter or petition no later than one workday after inspection closes.
  • Name the value you think is fair and back it up with land and building descriptions, insurance, cost records, listings, comparable sales or loan papers.
  • Show up for the hearing, personally or through an authorized representative.

The board may reject an appeal if you hold back information it reasonably asks for. Meanwhile, pay on the figure you claimed.

Which Hopkins County owners qualify for a tax reduction?

A homeowner aged 65 or older, or totally disabled, who lives in the property can deduct $49,100 from the assessment for the 2025 and 2026 years.

Applied to the Census middle value of $142,800, that leaves $93,700 to be taxed. The form is completed at the PVA office with proof of age, most often a birth certificate or driver's license. Disability applicants must document benefits received from January through December.

Farmland gets different treatment. The Sheriff's page cites KRS 132.010, which values agricultural land by its production capability, and describes qualifying land as parcels of 10 acres or more used to raise livestock or grow crops, including timber. Nobody can claim more than one exemption on one property within one county and state.

What happens to a Hopkins County tax debt after the Clerk takes over?

Once the Clerk holds the bill, it is a certificate of delinquency, and a lien is entered against the property. A sale of the house does not remove it.

The Clerk's 2025 sale shows the next step. It ran electronically on October 8, 2025, with registration handled at the Clerk's office, 24 Union Street, Madisonville. Buyers paid $5 per priority bill or $10 per current-year bill, capped at $250 in combined fees, and full payment was due by October 10 or the purchase was void.

A buyer of a certificate can load its own fees on the account, so clearing the bill with the Sheriff before the deadline, or with the Clerk afterward, costs less. The Sheriff's website and the Clerk's website do not link, so call the Clerk for current amounts instead of trusting the Sheriff's listing.

How does the local economy shape Hopkins County housing?

Coal and farming shaped the county's history, and the Census figures show retail and health care among its larger sectors. The first coal mine in the county opened in 1869 under the man Earlington is named for, and the Louisville and Nashville Railroad ran a line through Madisonville in 1870. Dawson Springs grew in the 1880s as a health resort.

Census figures show a retail-heavy base. Retail sales came to $1.84 billion in 2022, or $41,062 per resident, and health care and social assistance receipts reached about $414 million. Residents spend a mean 21.3 minutes getting to work, and 53.6 percent of people 16 and older are in the labor force.

  • 18,397 households averaged 2.40 people each.
  • Monthly owner costs came to $1,107 with a mortgage and $436 without.
  • Poverty touched 19.3 percent of residents.
  • Builders took out 201 permits in 2025.
  • Persons 65 or older made up 21.0 percent of the population, which matters for homestead claims.

What should a Madisonville-area seller know about Hopkins County?

Hopkins County sits in western Kentucky with Madisonville as seat and largest city. It was created on December 9, 1806 from Henderson County and has 542 square miles of land. The Pond, Tradewater and Green rivers cross it, with flat river valleys in the north and rolling hills in the south and center.

Coal mines work the southern end and farms fill the north, mostly soybeans, corn and tobacco. The Pennyrile Parkway and Western Kentucky Parkway both pass through. Other incorporated places include Dawson Springs, Earlington, Nortonville, Mortons Gap, Hanson, White Plains, Nebo and St. Charles.

  • 45,127 residents in 2025, down 0.6 percent from 2020.
  • A middle owned-home value of $142,800 in the 2020 to 2024 survey.
  • Owners live in 70.7 percent of homes.
  • $56,815 median household income.
  • $837 median gross rent.

Hopkins County Schools covers most of the county, while Dawson Springs runs its own district. Madisonville Community College sits in the county seat, and the Madisonville Messenger is the local daily.

More questions about Hopkins County, KY Property Tax Guide

What day does the Hopkins County discount period begin?

Collection opens October 1, after bills go out around September 30. Paying through November 1 earns 2 percent off, and face value applies from November 2 to year end.

Will Hopkins County let me split a bill into pieces?

No. The Sheriff takes the whole amount only and refuses part payments. Cards, cash and checks all work, and cards carry a processor fee.

I closed last month and received no bill. Who do I call?

Call the Sheriff at 270-821-5661. Bills are issued to the January 1 owner and the office does not see new deeds, so a copy can be printed from the Sheriff's website.

Whom do I pay once April 15 has gone by?

Pay the Hopkins County Clerk, phone 270-326-2097 per the Sheriff's page, since open bills go there when April 15 ends.

Do older owners get any relief?

Yes: a $49,100 homestead exemption, filed at the PVA's office on East Center Street. Owners 65 and over who live in the house qualify, as do totally disabled owners.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Office 100 South Main St, Greenville KY 42345; 270-338-3345; M-F 8-4

Tax rate

Selling in Muhlenberg County?

Where and how do Muhlenberg County owners pay the Sheriff?

Payment happens at the Sheriff's Office inside the courthouse at 100 South Main Street, Greenville, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. The number is 270-338-3345, and the mailing address is PO Box 227, Greenville, KY 42345.

  • Bills normally go out October 30, and collection opens November 1.
  • Online payment is possible. Telephone payment is not.
  • A drop box behind the courthouse, near the elevator entrance, accepts payments outside office hours.
  • Only full payment is taken, so a part payment does not count.

Value is a different question and belongs to the county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). The sheriff's own site says assessed values may change before they are final.

What shaped Muhlenberg County, and what does it mean for a sale?

The county covers 479 square miles of western Kentucky, 467 of them land. The Green River and Lake Malone are its two main waters. Greenville is the seat, and Central City is the largest community. Logan and Christian counties gave up the land in 1798.

Coal built the local economy. Kentucky's first commercial coal mine opened here in 1820 along the Green River at Paradise, and during most of the 1970s no other county in the country mined more. Surface coal has been stripped out, and what remains lies deep. The north is gentle hill country with river flats and bald cypress swamps along Cypress Creek. The south has higher relief, gorges and sandstone outcrops. Lake Malone State Park, with a 788-acre lake, sits near Dunmor.

Listings therefore range widely, from town lots in Greenville and Central City to ground near the lake and parcels in old mining country. One public school system operates under the Muhlenberg County Board of Education, and a single Muhlenberg County High School has served the county since June 2009.

How do Muhlenberg County Census figures read for housing?

The population estimate for July 2025 is 30,634, which is 1.0% below the 2020 base, and 21.3% of residents are past 65. Home prices are modest, and so are tax bills.

  • 13,640 housing units in 2025, with just 5 building permits that year.
  • Owners occupy 78.8% of homes during 2020 to 2024.
  • The Census midpoint for an owned house is $127,400.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,167 with a mortgage and $396 without.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $718.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $51,927, and 19.1% of people are in poverty.

About 88.7% of residents did not move in the prior year. With so few new permits, a buyer here mostly picks among houses that already exist.

Which Muhlenberg County economy details matter to buyers?

Buyers ask about jobs, schools and commuting. Coal mining in the county and its neighbors began to grow again as the 2000s opened. The Greater Muhlenberg Chamber of Commerce, created in January 2006 when the Central City and Greenville chambers merged, counted over 155 member businesses at the time.

The Census Bureau lists 537 employer establishments for 2023, and employment rose 6.7% between 2022 and 2023. Retail sales for 2022 were $374,858 thousand, or $12,212 per resident. Workers spend a mean of 27.0 minutes getting to their jobs. The schools consolidated in steps, from eight secondary schools to two high schools in 1990 and then to one. A sheriff's receipt showing the year's bill paid is the quickest answer to a buyer's first question about taxes.

What else about Muhlenberg County do buyers and heirs ask?

Many calls come from heirs, so some numbers help. The Census Bureau counts 1,758 veterans in the county, and 16.5% of residents under 65 live with a disability. Some 84.2% of households have a broadband subscription, and 14.7% of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Health care and social assistance brought in $144,467 thousand in 2022, and lodging and food service sales were $39,476 thousand.

Culture and services cluster in the two main towns. Central City has a convention center with an outdoor pool and spray park. Muhlenberg County Public Libraries runs the Thistle Cottage Genealogy and History Annex in Greenville, a useful stop for anyone tracing an old deed chain. The county lies at the southern edge of the Evansville, Indiana television market. John Prine's song 'Paradise' criticized strip mining here and refers to the community where the 1820 mine opened.

What are the Muhlenberg County payment windows?

The sheriff's posted dates follow KRS 134.015, with a discount first, the printed amount next and penalties after.

Muhlenberg County Sheriff, month-by-month bill totals
Month paidResult for the owner
Whole of NovemberSubtract 2 percent
Whole of DecemberPay the printed total
Whole of JanuaryAdd 5 percent
February 1 through April 15Add 21 percent

Whatever the month, the sheriff wants the entire bill in one payment. On a $1,200 bill the figures are $1,176 in November, $1,200 in December, $1,260 in January and $1,452 from February through April 15. Waiting the full season costs $276 more than paying early.

After April 15 the county clerk handles delinquent bills, so a seller with an old unpaid year should call the clerk for the payoff.

What is the route for contesting a Muhlenberg County valuation?

The PVA sets value as of January 1. Under KRS 133.120, the owner first meets the PVA or a deputy during the tax roll's 13-day public inspection in May, which KRS 133.045 schedules. Anyone still dissatisfied files a written petition with the County Clerk naming the parcel, the reasons and the value the owner proposes, within a workday after the inspection ends.

The appeals board will deny a case if the owner refuses to supply reasonable value information the PVA or board requests, so assemble sales comparisons, an appraisal or repair estimates early. Nothing about a filed appeal postpones the due date, because the bill stays payable on the normal schedule while the case proceeds. A taxpayer who never appears before the county board cannot reach the state Board of Tax Appeals afterward. Tax is paid on the owner's claimed value, with any increase billed later plus interest.

What exemption is available to older Muhlenberg County owners?

Owners 65 and up, and those totally disabled, can subtract $49,100 from assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. Applied to the county midpoint of $127,400, that leaves $78,300 subject to tax. The Muhlenberg County PVA takes the application along with proof of age: a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability filers renew annually unless they are service-connected veterans or have been ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

What should a Muhlenberg County seller settle before the deed is signed?

The tax is a personal obligation of whoever owned the property on January 1. A delinquent bill places a lien on the parcel for up to eleven years under KRS 134.420, regardless of owner.

  • Ask the sheriff whether this year's bill has been paid and in which window.
  • Put the proration in writing in the sales contract.
  • Enter the buyer's address for future bills on the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • When a deceased owner's heirs sell, the executor first files an affidavit with the county clerk naming recipients and values.

More questions about Muhlenberg County, KY Property Tax Guide

Is telephone payment accepted by the Muhlenberg County Sheriff?

No. The office takes payment online, by mail to PO Box 227, in person at 100 South Main Street, or in the courthouse drop box.

May an owner send part of a Muhlenberg County bill?

No. The sheriff's FAQ requires payment in full.

How long is the Muhlenberg County discount window?

All of November. The printed amount is due in December, and the penalty starts January 1.

What hours does the Muhlenberg County Sheriff keep?

Weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., at 100 South Main Street in Greenville. The phone is 270-338-3345.

What is the Muhlenberg County deduction for seniors?

The state subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026 once an owner 65 or older, or totally disabled, applies at the PVA.

Henderson County by the numbers

Which Henderson County, KY office does what with a tax bill?

Three county offices take turns with the same bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) fixes what a parcel is worth, the Sheriff's Office sends the bill and takes payment, and the County Clerk's Office keeps whatever is left unpaid.

The county attorney's tax collection FAQ gives the timeline. Real estate notices are mailed in late October or early November, and the sheriff accepts payment from November 1. A bill turns delinquent on January 1 after its due date. The sheriff holds the file until uncollected bills are turned over to the clerk, and from that point the clerk's office maintains them.

The county's own wording ties delinquency to two conditions: the due date has passed and any appeal rights have expired. A seller with an unresolved value dispute should therefore treat the appeal calendar and the payment calendar as running side by side.

What sets Henderson County apart from other Kentucky counties?

Henderson County sits in far western Kentucky on the Ohio River, facing Evansville, Indiana, and it is part of the Evansville, IN-KY metropolitan area. Its seat and largest city is Henderson, which grew from a riverside settlement called Red Banks. The county was carved out of Christian County in December 1798 and named for Richard Henderson of the Transylvania Company.

It measures 466 square miles, about 30 of which are water, and lies in the West Kentucky Coal Field. Corydon and Robards are the other incorporated cities, and Anthoston, Poole and Spottsville are census-designated places. Roughly 45 square miles called Green River Island lie on the Indiana bank yet belong to Henderson County, and Ellis Park Race Course occupies part of that ground.

Tobacco built the early town. Around 1880 Henderson counted 17 stemmeries and was the largest dark tobacco market in the world, and production fell through the twentieth century. The 2020 count of 44,793 residents was 3.2 percent below 2010.

Population density is 102.7 people per square mile, and 63.5 percent of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census. Hart County, by comparison, was 11.7 percent urban, so a Henderson seller is marketing in a far more urban county.

What local resources matter when you sell in Henderson County?

The county's links page lists the agencies a seller or buyer is likely to contact.

  • The Henderson City-County Planning Commission oversees public and private development inside both city and county limits.
  • Henderson GIS offers maps, data and information on the county.
  • Henderson County Schools and Henderson Community College anchor education.
  • The Henderson County Riverport and the Henderson City-County Airport, a general aviation field, serve industry and business users.
  • Audubon State Park, the Tourist Commission and the Downtown Henderson Partnership, begun in 1986 with Main Street program support, cover recreation and downtown life.
  • The Henderson Area Board of Realtors and the Housing Authority of Henderson are listed among community organizations.

If a buyer asks about zoning or development near your parcel, point them to the planning commission, and send questions about the tax bill itself to the sheriff or PVA.

How do Henderson County housing figures read?

The typical Henderson County home is valued above Hart County's $146,000 and below Henry County's $197,900. About 37 percent of occupied homes were rented at the 2020 census, which is a meaningful rental market next to the owner-occupied majority.

Henderson County at a glance, from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts estimates
ItemHenderson County
Residents, July 2025 estimate44,255
Housing units, 202520,295
Homes occupied by their owners64.9%
Middle owner home value$171,900
Middle gross rent$777
Middle household income$58,851
Average commute22.8 minutes
New building permits, 2025112

The county employed 16,375 people at 966 employer establishments in 2023. Retail sales in 2022 were about $763 million and health care and social assistance receipts about $312 million. Of adults 25 and over, 89.7 percent finished high school and 20.1 percent have a bachelor's degree. The poverty rate is 15.7 percent, and 7.2 percent of residents under 65 lack health insurance.

What happens after a Henderson County bill goes delinquent?

Interest and penalties begin, a lien attaches, and an outside buyer may purchase the debt. The county attorney's tax collection FAQ describes each stage.

  • The bill moves to the County Clerk's Office at 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor, Henderson, where interest of 1 percent per month and penalties accumulate.
  • A lien stays on the property until payment in full.
  • Any individual or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 may buy the bill at the clerk's tax sale. The clerk cannot predict or prevent that purchase.
  • The purchaser has 50 days to notify the owner. The owner then pays the purchaser, who sends a release to the clerk for recording.
  • A foreclosure suit by the purchaser becomes possible one year after the certificate of delinquency was created.

You can pay the clerk in person or mail a personal check, cashier's check, money order or certified check. Cards work for an added fee, and the clerk's number for details is 270-827-5753. American Express, Discover and MasterCard are taken, and Visa only as a debit.

Who can contest a Henderson County assessment, and how?

The owner starts with a conference at the PVA's office, a step KRS 133.120 places ahead of any formal appeal. The conference happens during or before the inspection window, and the Department of Revenue may allow up to 25 extra days.

If that fails, a written petition goes to the county clerk, and the appeals board holds a public hearing and fixes fair cash value. The county attorney speaks for the state and county there. Someone who loses may go on to the Board of Tax Appeals, but only after appearing before the county board.

Paid representatives must fall into listed categories such as attorney, accountant, tax consultant, owner's employee, broker or certified appraiser. They carry written authorization and disclose any contingency fee, although attorneys need not state its terms. The board can also raise a value, but it must first send the owner notice and a hearing date.

How should a seller handle taxes at a Henderson County closing?

Ownership on January 1 decides whose name goes on the year's bill, and under KRS 134.015 the debt is personal to that owner while a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 outlasts any sale. Line up both numbers before the closing date: what the sheriff shows for the current year and what the clerk shows for earlier ones.

If a prior year sits with the clerk, the 1 percent monthly interest becomes part of the payoff, so ask for a fresh figure close to the signing. The title agent can pay the total out of your proceeds. For recording charges and the real estate transfer tax on the deed, see the Henderson County Clerk page, which lists the current fee schedule.

More questions about Henderson County, KY Property Tax Guide

When does Henderson County start taking property tax payments?

November 1. Notices go out in late October or early November, and the sheriff accepts payment beginning that day. A bill goes delinquent on the following January 1.

Where is a delinquent Henderson County bill paid?

At the County Clerk's Office, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor Offices, Henderson, KY 42420. Mailed payments must be a check, money order or other certified funds.

How much interest does the clerk charge on a delinquent bill?

One percent per month plus penalties. A buyer of the bill at the tax sale may add charges allowed under Kentucky law.

Can someone else buy my delinquent Henderson County tax bill?

Yes. Any person or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 can buy it at the clerk's sale, and the clerk can neither predict nor stop the purchase.

How long before a bill buyer can foreclose?

One year after the certificate of delinquency is created. Some buyers wait longer while the property's equity covers the debt.
