What we could not confirm

  • No official sheriff tax page opened
  • Discount deadline Oct 31 vs Nov 1 unresolved

Who bills and collects Carter County property tax?

Three courthouse offices split the job in Carter County. The Property Valuation Administration puts a value on each parcel, the county clerk prints the bills and inherits the unpaid ones, and the sheriff takes payments through the autumn and winter. You will find all three at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, so one visit can settle most questions.

The county is a long stretch of northeastern Kentucky with about 412 square miles of land and water. Greenup and Lawrence counties gave up the ground for it in 1838. Grayson is the seat and Olive Hill is the only other city, which means most of the 12,206 housing units counted in 2020 are rural parcels, farm tracts and older frame houses billed as county property.

Where do I go for Carter County tax questions?

Start with the office that matches the question: value goes to the PVA, a bill amount or payment goes to the sheriff, and anything already delinquent goes to the clerk. The county's official directory lists the details below.

Carter County offices that handle property tax (county officials page)
OfficeAddressPhoneHours listed
Property Valuation Administration300 West Main Street, Suite 214, Grayson(606) 474-5663Mon to Fri 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; last Saturday of the month 8:30 am to noon
Sheriff (tax collection)300 West Main Street, Grayson(606) 474-5616Mon to Fri 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; last Saturday of the month 8:30 am to noon
County Clerk (tax bills, delinquent taxes)300 West Main Street, Grayson(606) 474-5188Mon to Fri 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; Grayson office open the last Saturday of each month, Olive Hill office open Saturdays 8:00 am to noon

The county site also lists an Olive Hill clerk location with its own Saturday hours.

What kind of houses and neighborhoods does Carter County have?

Mostly owner-occupied homes outside town limits, many of them decades old. The 2020 census found 10,664 households, with 75.7 percent of occupied units owned and 12.6 percent of all units empty. Only about one resident in five lived in an area the census treats as urban. The county population was 26,627 in 2020 and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 26,149.

The landscape explains the housing. A through rail route between Lexington and Ashland, later the Chesapeake & Ohio line, reached the county in 1881, and fire clay and refractory brick plants at Olive Hill and Hitchins were major industries in the early and mid 1900s. The Olive Hill depot, built in 1910, is on the National Register of Historic Places. Today Interstate 64 and US 60 carry traffic through the county, and the Carter County School District runs the public schools.

  • Carter Caves State Resort Park lies inside the county line.
  • Kentucky Christian University is in Grayson.
  • Adjoining counties are Greenup, Boyd, Lawrence, Elliott, Rowan and Lewis.

What do Carter County owners pay, and when?

The statewide calendar in KRS 134.015 governs. Your bill arrives near the start of October, and the total you owe depends on the day you pay.

  • Through November 1, a full payment earns 2 percent off.
  • From November 2 to year end, the printed amount is due.
  • All of January adds a 5 percent penalty.
  • Once February begins, the penalty becomes 10 percent and the sheriff's add-on fee applies.

The law treats the tax as your personal debt from the assessment date, and a lien on the land lasts eleven years no matter who buys it. Call the sheriff at (606) 474-5616 if a bill does not show up, and ask that office how it accepts mailed or in-person payments.

How can a Carter County owner contest a valuation?

Begin with the PVA, because Kentucky makes a conference there the entry ticket to every later step. The state opens each county's roll to the public for thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and the conference has to take place before or during that window.

If talking to the PVA does not move the number, deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the next workday after the window closes. Say which parcel is involved and what you think it would fetch on the open market. A local board then hears the case roughly a month later. It looks for proof, such as sale listings, construction costs and insurance policies, and it denies petitions that come without any. Owners who skip the board lose the right to go on to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Filing never stops the clock on payment. You owe tax on the figure you claimed until the case ends, and a higher final value brings a supplemental bill.

What happens to Carter County bills still unpaid in mid-April?

They leave the sheriff and land on the county clerk's desk on April 15. Each one becomes a certificate of delinquency, and the clerk reports that totals jump by about 40 percent once the added charges are counted. Personal checks do not work for these bills, while cash, money orders, company checks and cards (with a user fee) do.

The clerk will sometimes arrange a payment plan: a third of the balance up front and the remainder within 90 days. Miss the deadline and the bill returns to the delinquent list, and the money already paid is kept and credited rather than refunded.

  • The clerk places an ad about 30 days ahead of the sale and posts the list online.
  • The sale for 2024 bills took place August 29, 2025, at 10 am in the fiscal courtroom.
  • Bidders sign up at least ten days beforehand, and the lien assignment fee is $46.

A successful bidder gets the right to collect from you, so settling before April 15 is far cheaper.

Which Carter County owners get a homestead break?

Retirees and owners with a total disability who live in the house they own. The state takes a fixed sum off the assessed value before it applies the rate, and the sum stood at $49,100 for the assessment years 2025 and 2026. On a house assessed at $120,000, the taxable portion would shrink to $70,900. Apply at the Carter County PVA, which also knows the current figure, since it is reset every second year.

A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability applicants renew yearly, with exceptions for veterans with a service-connected rating and owners found permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

How do I sell a Carter County house that still owes tax?

Yes, you can, because the title company pays the balance out of your price. First ask the sheriff for a payoff on this year's bill and ask the clerk whether any older year was filed as delinquent. A recorded certificate appears in a title search and must be paid or released for the buyer to receive clear title.

Timing matters. A bill still with the sheriff carries only the 5 or 10 percent penalty, while one at the clerk adds fees and interest. When the house is inherited, vacant or short on repairs, a cash purchaser that takes it as it stands can settle the tax from your proceeds, so you do not have to bring money to the table.

More questions about Carter County, KY Property Tax Guide

Which office takes Carter County property tax payments?

The sheriff, at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, phone (606) 474-5616. Bills that go unpaid past April 15 are handled by the county clerk.

What if my Carter County tax bill never arrives?

Call the sheriff's office and give your name or parcel number. Ask how it takes payments by mail, and confirm the address before you send a check.

How late can I file a Carter County assessment appeal?

The petition goes to the clerk by the next workday after the May inspection window closes. A conference with the PVA must come first.

Will the Carter County clerk accept my personal check on a delinquent bill?

No. The clerk's page says personal checks are refused on delinquent bills and lists cash, money orders, company checks and cards instead. Card payments carry a user fee.

Can I list my Carter County house while back taxes are open?

Yes. The payoff is taken from your proceeds at closing, so get written balances from the sheriff and the clerk before you sign a contract.

Who do I call about a Floyd County tax bill?

Two do. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what a parcel is worth. The sheriff's tax division handles the bill itself. Neither one chooses the rate applied to that value.

The PVA's own site says the office appraises real and personal property at fair market value and stays out of rate setting, tax calculation and collection. Its counter is at 149 S. Value is a PVA question. Money owed is a sheriff question. Sending a value complaint to the sheriff only wastes a trip.

What should a seller know about Floyd County's housing market?

Floyd County lies in the Eastern Kentucky coalfield. It has 393 square miles of land and borders Johnson, Martin, Pike, Knott and Magoffin counties. Lawmakers created it at the end of 1799 as the state's 40th county, and the law took effect on June 1, 1800. The first courthouse burned in April 1808, which is why the earliest surviving government records start after that year.

Coal explains most of the housing map, and the numbers below show how much the market has shrunk since the mines scaled back. Eastern Kentucky's first commercial coal mine opened in 1900 at Betsy Layne, and coal camps such as Wheelwright, Wayland, Garrett, Emma and Bypro grew up around the mines. Floyd County topped 53,000 people in 1950 and has lost residents in almost every census since; the 2020 count was 35,942. By 2016 the county still had 23 working mines producing roughly 640,000 tons.

Prestonsburg is the seat, and Allen, Martin, Wayland and Wheelwright are the other cities. Census-designated places include Auxier, Betsy Layne, Dwale, Maytown and McDowell. Just 21.8 percent of the 2020 population counted as urban, so many sellers own hillside or hollow land instead of a town lot. The Floyd County School District runs the public schools, and Prestonsburg, where the courthouse and county offices stand, is the natural place to bring any paperwork.

How do Floyd County's housing figures read?

They describe a low-priced, owner-heavy market with little new construction.

  • Estimated 2025 population: 34,401, down 4.3 percent since 2020.
  • Typical value of a house its owner lives in (2020 to 2024 survey period): $98,700.
  • Owner-occupied share: 72.2 percent, across 14,700 households that average 2.34 people.
  • Housing units: 17,753 in 2025, with 13.8 percent sitting empty when the 2020 census was taken.
  • Median gross rent: $672. Median household income: $41,279. People in poverty: 27.7 percent.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 2.

Just 43.5 percent of adults are in the labor force, and 22.3 percent of residents younger than 65 report a disability. Health care brought in about $355 million in 2022, more than any other sector listed by the Census Bureau for the county. On a house worth about $98,700, a few thousand dollars of back tax eats a visible slice of the price, so paying it off early counts for more here than in a county with pricier homes.

When does Floyd County expect payment, and what happens if I am late?

KRS 134.015 sets the calendar, and it favors early payers. Pay the whole bill by November 1 and 2 percent comes off. After that the printed amount applies until December 31. January costs an extra 5 percent, and anything later costs 10 percent.

The sheriff's site announced that 2026 bills were payable from October 1 and added an online payment link. If a lender escrows your taxes, check that the servicer actually received the bill.

On April 15 the sheriff hands every open bill over to the county clerk. A lien is recorded, and interest of 1 percent accrues monthly. The clerk adds a 10 percent commission, and once the county attorney has sent a notice, a 20 percent attorney commission follows. A clerk's tax sale follows within roughly three to four and a half months.

How can a Floyd County owner contest a value?

Go to the PVA first. Kentucky requires a conference there before an appeal can be filed, and the PVA must walk you through the valuation method.

  • The roll is posted for public viewing over 13 days that start in early May.
  • The written appeal goes to the county clerk, and the cutoff is the end of the first business day after viewing closes.
  • A local review board hears cases roughly four to five weeks after viewing ends, so spend the wait collecting photos, repair quotes and nearby sale prices.
  • Missing the hearing forfeits the later step to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Hired representatives must come from a short list of professions in KRS 133.120 and carry your written permission.

Does a Floyd County homeowner qualify for the homestead exemption?

Age 65 and up, or total disability, opens the door to a $49,100 reduction in assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. The Floyd County PVA site says nobody receives an exemption without filing a formal application, and that the disability route is meant for people who are 100 percent disabled.

With a median-priced Floyd County house at $98,700, the taxable figure becomes $49,600. To prove age, bring a birth certificate, license or passport. Someone applying on disability grounds needs proof of a total-disability classification and has to reapply annually. Veterans with a service-connected disability and people whose disability is permanent under Social Security rules are spared the yearly paperwork.

How should I handle unpaid taxes when selling a Floyd County house?

Pay them off, or have the closing agent do it. KRS 134.015 keeps a delinquency lien on the parcel whoever holds title, so the buyer's title company will find it.

  • Call the sheriff's tax division at (606) 886-8965 for the exact payoff.
  • Pay before April 15 if you can, because the clerk and attorney commissions only begin after the transfer.
  • Put the current year's bill in the sale contract. The state treats the tax as owed by the person who held the property on January 1.
  • If repairs and arrears are both piling up, a direct buyer that purchases as-is can fold both into one closing.

The county clerk can explain how to record the deed. Afterward, send the PVA the new owner's name and mailing address.

More questions about Floyd County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where do Floyd County residents pay their property tax?

At the Floyd County Sheriff's tax division, 149 S Central Ave. in Prestonsburg, by mail to P.O. Box 152, or online from the sheriff's home page. The tax division's number is (606) 886-8965.

Does the Floyd County PVA set my tax rate?

No. The PVA's website says the office does not determine rates, calculate taxes or collect them. It values property and processes exemption applications at (606) 886-9622.

When does Floyd County's 2 percent discount end?

On November 1. From November 2 through December 31 the bill is due without a discount, and penalties start in January.

How large is the homestead exemption for a Floyd County home?

The reduction is $49,100 for both 2025 and 2026. Eligible owners are seniors and the totally disabled, and the paperwork goes to the Floyd County PVA.

Can a Floyd County house sell while tax is still owed?

Yes, provided the balance is settled by the closing table. Request a payoff from the sheriff first, since an open bill leaves the lien on the parcel.

Who do I deal with on a Gallatin County tax bill?

Three Warsaw offices come into play when a house changes hands. The PVA places the value, the Sheriff's Office takes the money, and the County Clerk files deeds and takes assessment appeals.

  • PVA: 200 Washington Street (mail to PO Box 470), Warsaw, KY 41095, phone (859) 567-5621.
  • Sheriff: 106 North Main (mail to PO Box 1025), Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5751. The county's sheriff page links to a tax bill lookup.
  • County Clerk: 803 East Main Street, Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5411, open weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon.

The City of Warsaw runs its own online payment page for water, sewer and property tax bills, so a house inside the city limits may owe the city as well as the county. Ask both the sheriff and the city which bills attach to an address before you set a closing date, and keep copies of every paid receipt for the buyer's title company. A clean paper trail shortens the closing, because the title search will list any unpaid balance as an exception.

What makes Gallatin County unusual for a home sale?

Size, mostly. Gallatin County covers 105 square miles in all, which makes it the second smallest county in Kentucky. It sits on the Ohio River across from Indiana and counts as part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area. The legislature formed it on December 14, 1798 out of Franklin and Shelby counties, and the later creation of Owen, Trimble and Carroll counties left it about a tenth of its first size.

The county has three communities: Warsaw (the seat), Sparta and Glencoe. Every resident was counted as rural in 2020. Interstate 71 passes through with three exits around Sparta and Glencoe, joined by US 42 and US 127, and Wikipedia reports that by the 1980s more than half of local workers held jobs elsewhere. The commute still averages 29.5 minutes.

River engineering and racing give the county its landmarks. Markland Locks and Dam was built from 1956 to 1964 and a hydroelectric plant was added in 1967. The county's own website pitches the Kentucky Speedway and two river marinas. A county-owned airport one mile north of Sparta, with a 5,000-foot runway, opened in June 2023.

Here is who lives in the county. Population was 1,291 in 1800, 7,870 in 2000, 8,589 in 2010 and 8,690 in 2020, when the median age was 39.5 and 25.2 percent of residents were under 18. Census estimates put the share of residents 65 or over at 17.5 percent, against 20.6 percent in Floyd County, so a smaller slice of Gallatin County owners can claim the age-based homestead reduction. Census estimates put 84.6 percent of adults as high school graduates, 15.0 percent as holding a bachelor's degree, and 87.4 percent of households as having broadband.

How does Gallatin County's housing market measure up?

Prices sit between the mountain counties and the capital region, and the county has grown slowly but steadily.

Gallatin County, Kentucky housing and economy snapshot (source: Census QuickFacts)

About 61.3 percent of adults are in the labor force. Employer-business jobs fell 7.4 percent between 2022 and 2023, to 1,373, and retail sales reached roughly $135 million in 2022. The 2020 census found 3,685 housing units with 13.1 percent unoccupied, so a share of the stock is seasonal, vacant or waiting for a buyer.

When does the sheriff want Gallatin County property tax?

Bills are payable to the sheriff, and the state's collection rules in KRS 134.015 give every owner the same ladder. A 2 percent reduction applies to a bill paid in full by November 1, the printed amount runs through December 31, and late payers owe 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward.

If bill mailing slips, the Department of Revenue can replace the usual dates with a compressed schedule of one month at a discount, one month at face and one month at 5 percent, so read the dates printed on the bill itself. When a house sells, tell the sheriff the new owner's name so later bills reach the right person.

How do Gallatin County owners dispute a value?

Start at 200 Washington Street. The state requires a PVA conference before any appeal, and visits are easiest right after assessment notices arrive. The tax roll then opens to public view for 13 days in early May.

Once you have met the PVA or a deputy, the County Clerk's office takes your written appeal, which is due by the end of the next business day after viewing closes. The local board of assessment appeals sits about four to five weeks later, for up to five days.

  • Bring facts about the land and buildings, construction costs, insurance details and sale listings of similar properties.
  • Expect to explain your evidence in person with the PVA also present.
  • The board must put the reason for any raise or cut in writing, and you are allowed to record the hearing.

An owner who files but does not attend the hearing cannot continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission, so mark the hearing date on a calendar the day it is set.

How much does the homestead exemption save in Gallatin County?

For seniors and totally disabled owners, $49,100 is deducted from assessed value in 2025 and 2026. File with the Gallatin County PVA. Applied to the county's typical home value of $178,200, the taxable figure drops to $129,100.

Disability filers need payments from a federal or retirement-system program covering the whole assessment period, and they renew every year. Service-connected veterans and people ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from that yearly renewal.

What if taxes are unpaid when a Gallatin County house sells?

The balance stays with the property. KRS 134.015 calls the tax a personal debt as of the assessment date, and a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 continues no matter who takes title.

On April 15 the sheriff transfers open bills to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. Within 30 days the county attorney mails a first notice, a second follows within 60 days, and the Department of Revenue says the clerk's tax sale takes place 90 to 135 days after the transfer. A third-party buyer at that sale can pile on substantial fees. Ask the sheriff at (859) 567-5751 for a payoff before you list, and plan to clear it from the sale proceeds.

More questions about Gallatin County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where do I send a Gallatin County property tax payment?

Send it to the Gallatin County Sheriff, 106 North Main in Warsaw, or PO Box 1025, Warsaw, KY 41095. The county's sheriff page links a tax bill lookup.

How do I reach the Gallatin County PVA?

Call (859) 567-5621 or visit 200 Washington Street in Warsaw. The PVA handles value questions, exemption forms and owner records.

Is Gallatin County's early-payment date different from other counties?

No. It follows the statewide date of November 1, when full payment earns 2 percent off. The face amount is owed through December 31.

Does the City of Warsaw send its own tax bill?

Warsaw offers an online page for water, sewer and property tax bills. Owners inside the city should ask the city and the sheriff which bills apply to their address.

Does a tax lien survive a sale in Gallatin County?

Yes. A delinquency lien stays on the property after a sale until the tax is paid or the period in KRS 134.420 runs out, so settle the balance at closing.

Which offices do Green County owners deal with?

Two courthouse-area offices split the job in Green County. The Green County Sheriff collects the bill at 203 W Court Street, Greensburg, KY 42743, phone (270) 932-5641. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assesses every parcel from 103 South 1st Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-7518.

The PVA values property and keeps the records. The sheriff takes payment. Call the PVA for address changes, exemption forms and questions about how a value was reached, and call ahead to either office to confirm its hours.

The Census counts 4,421 households in Green County, so a phone call to either office is the quickest way to confirm a payoff or a parcel record before you list.

What should a seller know about Green County itself?

South central Kentucky holds Green County, whose only incorporated city is the seat, Greensburg. Summersville is a census-designated place, and every resident counted in 2020 lived in a rural area. The county was formed on December 20, 1792, from parts of Lincoln and Nelson counties, and it later gave up land to create Adair, Cumberland and Taylor counties.

The county government places it twenty miles north of Lindsey Wilson College in Adair County and twelve miles west of Campbellsville University in Taylor County. The land covers about 286 square miles, and the Green River runs across it from east to west. The county government describes terrain that ranges from flat and gently rolling to steep and rocky, and it points to Green River Lake, American Legion Park on the river and Wyatt Jeffries Woods as local draws. Greensburg's 1804 brick courthouse, the oldest in the state according to Wikipedia, stands in the Downtown Greensburg Historic District, and the current courthouse dates from 1931. Cow Days brings crowds to town the third weekend of September.

History runs deep here. The Cumberland Trace, an early road from Lincoln County toward Nashville, crosses the county, and an oil boom from 1958 into the early 1960s lifted the local economy enough that temporary air strips were built at Summersville and Pierce. The 445-foot Goose Creek Footbridge, built in the late 1920s, links the town square to the old train depot. Green County was also dry until 2015.

Census QuickFacts gives the housing numbers sellers will meet:

  • July 2025 estimate: 11,644 residents, a 4.8 percent gain on the 2020 base.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 77.6 percent, at 2.54 people per household.
  • Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024: $125,000.
  • Median owner costs: $955 a month with a mortgage and $361 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $610. Median household income: $46,798. Persons in poverty: 17.9 percent.

The county sits on the Central and Eastern time zone line, with LaRue and Taylor counties to the north on Eastern time, so check which clock an appointment uses.

How does the Green County tax year run?

The PVA's online calendar begins with the January 1 assessment date and finishes with the sheriff's settlement the next September. For a homeowner the milestones are mid-September, when the sheriff receives bills, November 1, when the discount ends, and January 1, when penalties begin. The clerk's sale of delinquent certificates is listed for July 14 through August 28.

Green County real estate tax calendar (source: Green County PVA website)
StepDate or window
Public inspection of the roll, with PVA conferences13 days from the first Monday in May, Saturdays included
Assessment appeals board sits5 days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection
Bills handed to the sheriffBy September 15

When bills mail late, the state may switch to a slower schedule with a 30-day stage for each step.

What is the appeal route for a Green County value?

See the Green County PVA, then the county clerk. Kentucky shuts the local board's door on anyone who skipped the conference, and conferences happen during that May inspection window.

  • Have the PVA explain the number, then state your own. The conference record shows the starting value, your claim and any changes both sides accept.
  • File with the clerk before the close of the workday that follows the inspection period.
  • Show up at the hearing with proof: lot and building details, insurance papers, build costs and listings of comparable houses.
  • If the board raises or cuts the value, it owes you a written reason.

A professional paid to speak for you must fit the state's list of qualified representatives and hold your written authorization. Skipping the filing or the hearing ends the path to the Kentucky Claims Commission. A late-finishing case can bring a supplemental bill if the board lands above your claim.

Which Green County property is exempt?

Section 170 of Kentucky's constitution, which the Green County PVA site reproduces, exempts public property in public use, burial grounds, church property, charities, schools not run for gain, public libraries, household goods and crops in the producer's hands. A separate break covers owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who keep the house as a permanent residence.

It is worth $49,100 in assessment years 2025 and 2026. At Green County's Census median of $125,000, a qualifying owner is taxed on $75,900. Apply through the PVA with a birth certificate, license or passport. Disability claims need payments received through the whole assessment period and a yearly renewal, except for service-connected veterans and owners with a permanent total disability finding.

The break matters locally. Green County's median age was 44.6 in 2020, and 21.1 percent of residents had reached 65, so many owners may qualify.

If you move out, give the PVA your new mailing address so assessment notices and tax bills reach you.

What if a Green County house sells with tax still owed?

The debt rides with the land, so it passes to the buyer unless it is cleared first. The owner on January 1 is personally liable, and a delinquent bill's lien can survive 11 years, as KRS 134.015 and 134.420 provide, whoever holds title.

Timing drives the cost. Pay the sheriff before April 15 and you owe only the penalties already earned. After the transfer, the clerk adds 1 percent monthly interest, a 10 percent commission, a county attorney commission and a lien fee. The state's sample shows how fast it grows: $1,000 turns into $1,387.79 almost at once and $1,611.30 once the attorney's first notice goes out.

The county attorney writes at the 30-day and 60-day marks, and a sale follows 90 to 135 days after the transfer. Get both payoffs in writing before listing, and let the closing agent pay them from the sale proceeds.

More questions about Green County, KY Property Tax Guide

When does the Green County discount end?

On November 1. The calendar lets owners pay 2 percent less through then, face amount from the next day to December 31, and adds 5 percent in January.

Who takes tax payments in Green County?

The Green County Sheriff, at 203 W Court Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-5641. The PVA at (270) 932-7518 values property and handles exemptions but takes no payments.

What happens to a Green County bill after January 31?

After January 31 the PVA calendar adds a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent sheriff fee. The clerk takes over on April 15 and charges monthly interest.

How large is the Green County homestead exemption?

Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, get $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. At the $125,000 median, that leaves $75,900 taxable.

When does Green County sell delinquent tax bills?

The standard calendar lists July 14 through August 28, which falls 90 to 135 days after the April 15 handoff to the clerk.

Which offices do Greenup County owners deal with?

The Sheriff's Office collects tax bills, the PVA assesses, and the County Clerk takes over after April 15. All three work out of the Greenup County Courthouse area in the town of Greenup. The Property Valuation Administrator is in Room 209 at 301 Main Street, phone (606) 473-9984, open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Mail to the sheriff goes to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, and the office answers at (606) 473-9833. The sheriff's tax page lets you pay online with your bill number and mailing address, and online payments carry convenience fees that go to the payment processor, not the sheriff. Refunds and account problems are handled in person at the sheriff's office, not by phone.

  • PVA: values, exemptions and appeals conferences, (606) 473-9984.
  • Sheriff: current-year payment, (606) 473-9833.
  • County Clerk: bills transferred after April 15, (606) 473-7394.
  • Circuit Clerk: court matters, (606) 473-9869.
  • County Attorney: questions about the law behind the April 15 transfer, (606) 473-7855.

What should a seller know about Greenup County itself?

Greenup County lies along the Ohio River in the northeast corner of Kentucky, and it belongs to the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area. The General Assembly created it in December 1803 from Mason County. Greenup is the county seat, Flatwoods is the largest city, and the other cities are Bellefonte, Raceland, Russell, South Shore, Worthington and Wurtland.

The river valley is flat and holds most of the industry, shops and housing, while the rest of the county rolls into Appalachian foothills with forest, farms and fishing spots at Greenbo Lake, Tygarts Creek and the Little Sandy River. US 23 follows the river through Russell, Flatwoods, Raceland, Wurtland, Greenup and South Shore and crosses to Portsmouth, Ohio on the U.S. Grant Bridge. The AA Highway, finished in 1995, runs west toward Maysville, and the Industrial Parkway links Wurtland to EastPark and Interstate 64.

The county has had three courthouses, the first of logs and replaced by brick in 1811. Today it is wet by local option: Russell has allowed full retail alcohol sales since 2014, and Greenup, Raceland and South Shore voted in 2020. The 2020 census found a median age of 43.9, with 21.2 percent of residents 65 or older.

Three school systems share the county: Greenup County Schools, Russell Independent and Raceland-Worthington Independent. Census QuickFacts supplies the housing numbers:

  • July 2025 estimate: 35,213 residents, 2.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 80.3 percent.
  • Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024: $134,000.
  • Median owner costs: $1,186 a month with a mortgage, $483 without, across 14,739 households.
  • Median gross rent: $860. Median household income: $60,751. Persons in poverty: 16.7 percent.

What does a Greenup County bill cost after April 15?

It goes from the sheriff to the County Clerk, and the total starts climbing. The sheriff's page says April 15 is the last day to pay at the Sheriff's Office, and that bills turned over to the Clerk pick up fees that the original bill never showed. The sheriff's page cites House Bill 262 as the reason for the April 15 date.

The Department of Revenue prices out the stages for a $1,000 bill. It assumes a 4 percent sheriff commission, so your actual figures depend on the local rate.

Cost of a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill after transfer to the clerk (source: Department of Revenue example)
When paidTotal due
Within 5 business days of transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
After a second month of interest (May)$1,627.61
After newspaper advertising (June)$1,659.90
Bought by a third-party purchaser at the sale$1,704.21

Interest runs at 1 percent per month on the certificate. The sheriff's site also keeps links to earlier bills for tax years 2015 through 2019, which helps when you trace an old balance. The clerk's sale of delinquent bills must fall 90 to 135 days after the transfer, which in a normal year means July 14 to August 28. Ask the Clerk's office for the third-party purchaser rules if you hold a bill that reaches the sale.

How can a Greenup County owner challenge a value?

Start at the PVA, because Kentucky lets only owners who held a conference take a case to the board. The PVA's site explains that every property is revalued each year and physically examined at least once every four years, so a value can move even when your house has not changed.

  • Conferences fall in the May inspection window, which runs 13 days from the first Monday, and staff can meet earlier once notices are mailed.
  • File at the County Clerk's office by closing time on the next business day.
  • The board convenes four to five weeks after inspection ends and sits at most five days unless the state agrees to more.
  • Bring documents the board can weigh: building costs, insurance policies, listings and photos. No documents, no reduction.

The PVA's FAQ gives the formula as taxes equal assessment times rate. If the rate holds, a higher value means a higher bill and a lower value a lower one. It also gives two reminders. Keep your mailing address current with the office, and never treat a missing bill or notice as a reason to skip payment. Rates come from the county, city and school boards, not the PVA.

Does Greenup County have a homestead break?

Greenup County owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and live in the house get $49,100 knocked off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. A house at Greenup County's Census median of $134,000 would be taxed on $84,900.

Bring proof of age to the Greenup County PVA, such as a birth certificate, license or passport. For a disability claim, ask the PVA which papers prove the classification and when to renew.

The PVA's FAQ still quotes a saving of about $280 for 2011, so ask the office for the current figure on your own parcel instead of relying on that old estimate.

What should a Greenup County seller settle before closing?

Ask each office for a payoff, because which office holds the bill depends on the date. Before April 15 it sits with the sheriff. Afterward the Clerk has it, and the Clerk's delinquent tax page links the third-party purchaser information and application.

Taxes are the owner's debt from January 1, and a delinquent lien can follow the house for up to 11 years after a sale, per KRS 134.420. A buyer's title search will find a lien that has not been released, and a recording and release fee comes with clearing it.

The closing agent can tell you how this year's bill is split with the buyer. Any bill still open at the Clerk should be paid from your proceeds, and a written payoff from the Clerk shows the full price of clearing the title on a house with several years behind.

More questions about Greenup County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where is Greenup County property tax paid?

At the Greenup County Sheriff's Office through April 15, in person, by mail to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, or online. Call (606) 473-9833. Processors charge convenience fees on online payments.

Which office explains a Greenup County assessment?

The PVA at (606) 473-9984, in Room 209 of the courthouse, 301 Main Street, with weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

What changes on April 15 in Greenup County?

The sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the County Clerk, which adds fees the original bill never showed. Call (606) 473-7394 for the total.

What is the Greenup County homestead amount?

The 2025 and 2026 figure is $49,100 off assessed value, open to owners 65 or older or totally disabled. A house at the $134,000 county median would be taxed on $84,900.

Will the Greenup County sheriff refund money by phone?

No. The sheriff's page says refunds and account corrections must be requested in person at the office, and staff do not process them by phone.

Which Edmonton offices run Metcalfe County property tax?

In Metcalfe County the PVA appraises, the sheriff mails the bill and takes the payment, and the county clerk inherits any bill left open in the spring. The county's own PVA site, hosted on qpublic.net, publishes the roll and a tax calendar.

Edmonton is the county seat and also its one incorporated city.

Where does Metcalfe County sit, and who buys homes there?

Metcalfe spreads over about 290 square miles of south central Kentucky. It was organized in May 1860 as the 106th Kentucky county and honors Thomas Metcalfe, governor from 1828 to 1832. The Glasgow micropolitan area includes it, and that area belongs to the Bowling Green and Glasgow combined statistical area. Wikipedia lists Summer Shade as a census designated place and Alone as a ghost town.

Edmonton sits on the Louis B. Nunn Cumberland Parkway. The county site puts Interstate 65 about 29 miles away by that road, Glasgow 16 miles west, Louisville 113 miles away, Lexington 124, and Nashville 112. U.S. 68 and Kentucky routes 80 and 163 also serve the town. CSX rail service is near Glasgow, and Moore Field there has a 4,586 foot paved runway.

Neighboring counties are Hart, Green, Adair, Cumberland, Monroe and Barren. Because the county sits inside the Glasgow area, a seller may meet buyers who work toward Glasgow or Bowling Green. The county site gives Edmonton about 1,586 residents in 2010, against 10,099 in the whole county, so most owners live outside the city. The 2020 census put the median age at 41.9 years, with 19.0 percent of residents 65 or older, which is the group that can claim the homestead exemption described below.

What does the Census Bureau report on Metcalfe County homes?

In 2020 the county had 10,286 residents, barely above 10,099 in 2010, and mid-2025 brought an estimate of 10,583. That 2020 tally showed 4,691 housing units with 11.6 percent standing empty, and the whole population lived in rural territory.

The five year survey reports:

  • Homeowners live in 77.7 percent of homes, the top rate among these four counties.
  • Housing costs for owners come to $1,066 a month with a mortgage and $368 with none.
  • Jobs numbered 1,234 in 2023, 7.5 percent fewer than the year before.
  • Commutes average 25.9 minutes, the briefest of the four.
  • Per capita income is $27,314, and 83.3 percent of households have a broadband subscription.

Which Metcalfe County offices handle tax questions?

The elected officials page lists these contacts.

  • Sheriff: bills and collections. P.O. Box 371, Edmonton, KY 42129, phone (270) 432-3041.
  • PVA: values, exemption forms, mailing address changes. P.O. Box 939, phone (270) 432-3162, and the site is www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.
  • Fiscal Court: county government, with a street address of 201 North Main and a mailing box at P.O. Box 149, phone (270) 432-3181.
  • County Attorney: P.O. Box 999, phone (270) 432-0777.

Lien and delinquent bill details come from the county clerk's office. A new owner who never receives a bill should contact the sheriff, the PVA site advises.

Which payment dates apply in Metcalfe County?

KRS 134.015 ends the 2 percent discount on November 1. Yet the PVA's calendar page lists November 30 as the discount deadline, December 1 to 31 for the plain amount, and January 1 as the start of delinquency. Read the dates on your own bill, and confirm with the sheriff before you count on the later one.

The same calendar also shows:

  • September 15: the sheriff has the bills in hand.
  • January: 5 percent added.
  • February onward: 10 percent added, together with a 10 percent sheriff fee.
  • April 15, close of business: the bills pass from sheriff to clerk.
  • July 14 to August 28: window for the clerk's certificate sale, with the sheriff's settlement due September 1.

What steps lead to a Metcalfe County assessment appeal?

Start with the PVA while the roll is on public view, which runs 13 days from the first Monday of May and includes Saturdays. If the conference fails, go to the county clerk, and do it by the next workday after the viewing period closes.

The appeals board has three local members, named by the mayor of the county's largest city, the fiscal court and the judge executive. Since Edmonton is the only city, its mayor makes one of those picks. A change by the board must come with a written explanation, and you may record the hearing.

  • Sale prices and dates of similar homes near yours.
  • A contractor quote for repairs that the PVA record omits.
  • The dollar value you claim, written on the form.

If you file and then skip the hearing, you cannot take the appeal further.

How is rural land valued in Metcalfe County?

State rules send PVAs to every parcel at least every four years and put new buildings on the roll annually. Farm land can be assessed at what it is worth as agriculture instead of its fair cash value, the Department of Revenue says.

On nearly 290 square miles with about 10,500 residents, many Metcalfe County sales include acreage. If any part of a parcel is farmed, ask the PVA about its classification before you list.

Do Metcalfe County seniors get a homestead exemption?

Yes. An owner who turns 65 during the year, or is classified as totally disabled on January 1, applies at the PVA for the home they own and live in. KRS 132.810 allows a single exemption for each residential unit and includes mobile homes and manufactured houses.

A disabled owner under 65 reapplies yearly, except a service connected totally disabled veteran or a person with a permanent disability finding. Applying before payment reduces the bill, and applying afterward earns a refund.

What follows a missed Metcalfe County payment?

Unpaid bills reach the clerk's office at the end of April 15 as certificates of delinquency, each with a lien on record. Interest of 1 percent a month builds up, and clerk and county attorney fees (10 and 20 percent) follow. A public listing is required at least 30 days before the sale.

KRS 134.015 makes the January 1 owner personally liable, and the lien can trail the property for 11 years. A private buyer who gets the certificate collects from the owner and may add fees.

Does back tax stop a Metcalfe County sale?

It does not have to. The sheriff quotes the payoff before April 15 and the clerk afterward, and the amount grows monthly once the clerk has it. Request a written figure dated close to closing.

January 1 settles tax ownership, so a late year sale leaves the bill with the previous owner until next year. Many Metcalfe County sellers hold older houses with repairs put off. To weigh a cash offer against a listing, work out each net after repairs, tax and months of carrying cost.

More questions about Metcalfe County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who takes payment of Metcalfe County property tax?

The county sheriff, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 371 in Edmonton. The listed number is (270) 432-3041.

Is there a city property tax in Edmonton?

Edmonton is the county's only incorporated city. Ask the Fiscal Court at (270) 432-3181 whether a city bill applies to your parcel.

How do I reach the Metcalfe County PVA?

Call (270) 432-3162 or write to P.O. Box 939, Edmonton, KY 42129. The office site is www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.

When can a Metcalfe County owner contest a value?

During the 13 days that begin on the first Monday of May. A PVA conference has to come before any filing.

How long does a delinquent tax lien last?

Up to 11 years under KRS 134.015, through any change of owner.

Which Tompkinsville offices collect and assess Monroe County tax?

Courthouse suites at 200 North Main Street in Tompkinsville hold most of the tax offices. The PVA values the homes, the sheriff takes in the payment, and the county clerk looks after delinquent bills and liens. The county attorney, in a separate office on North Main Street, arranges payment plans.

This is the Kentucky Monroe County, in the Eastern Pennyroyal Plateau.

What is Monroe County like beyond the courthouse?

Monroe spreads across about 329 square miles of land along the Tennessee border. Formed in 1820, it carries the name of President James Monroe, and its seat honors his vice president, Daniel Tompkins. Wikipedia says no other county named for a president has a seat named for that president's vice president. Fountain Run and Gamaliel are the other cities. Neighbors are Barren, Metcalfe, Cumberland and Allen counties, plus Clay and Macon counties in Tennessee.

The county website describes the Upper Cumberland hills, the Cumberland River and the headwaters of the Barren River. History is visible on the ground: the Old Mulkey Meetinghouse State Historic Site holds the oldest log meetinghouse in Kentucky, built in 1804, on a 20 acre park. Confederate raiders under John Hunt Morgan attacked a Union garrison here on July 9, 1862, and captured 30 soldiers, per Wikipedia.

Wikipedia adds that Monroe stayed a dry county until voters approved alcohol sales on November 7, 2023.

Is the Monroe County housing market growing?

Monroe is the only one of these four counties to shrink since 2020. The 2020 count of 11,338 topped the 10,963 recorded in 2010, but the mid-2025 estimate of 11,191 is 1.3 percent lower. Housing units number 5,300.

Five year survey results:

  • The share of owner lived homes is 70.9 percent, the smallest of the four counties, which leaves more room for rentals.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,056 with a mortgage and $397 without one.
  • Broadband is subscribed to by 83.9 percent of households.
  • Workers average 28.4 minutes to reach a job.
  • Jobs counted in 2023 came to 2,649, which is 1.9 percent below 2022.
  • Per capita income is $27,296, and 88.7 percent of households have a computer.

Which Monroe County offices should you call or visit?

The county officials page gives these courthouse suites, all in Tompkinsville, KY 42167.

  • Sheriff: tax collection. 200 North Main Street, Suite E, phone (270) 487-6622.
  • PVA: assessments and exemptions. 200 North Main Street, Suite A, phone (270) 487-6401.
  • County Clerk: delinquent bills and liens. 200 North Main Street, Suite D, phone (270) 487-5471.
  • County Attorney: 215 North Main Street, phone (270) 487-6303.

Before paying anyone, learn from the clerk whether your certificate has been sold, because a buyer can attach costs of its own.

What is the Monroe County delinquent tax sale?

Right after April 15 the clerk issues a certificate of delinquency, a lien of record against the property. According to the clerk, that happens on or about April 16. Interest climbs monthly, so an early payment costs less.

The clerk scheduled the 2026 sale for September 23, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Central, inside the clerk's office, and that date is behind us. A certificate unpaid at the sale may go to a private party who adds heavy administrative costs. The county attorney or a buyer may pursue foreclosure.

  • By mail: money orders only.
  • In person at the clerk's desk: check, cash or credit card, and card fees may apply.
  • Installments: the County Attorney's office offers them, though a sold bill no longer qualifies.

The clerk's page gives a phone number for learning whether a certificate was bought and by whom.

When are regular Monroe County bills due?

Through April 15 you pay the sheriff under the calendar in KRS 134.015. Fall brings the mailed bill, a 2 percent discount holds until November 1, and the printed amount can be paid up to December 31.

January costs an extra 5 percent, and later payments carry 10 percent. The state's property page gives a combined 21 percent penalty for February 1 through April 15. In its example a $1,000 bill becomes a $1,254 certificate, then totals $1,387.79 if the owner pays within five business days of the transfer.

How do you challenge a Monroe County value?

A PVA conference comes first, and the state requires it before anyone can file. The roll opens to the public on the first Monday of May for about two weeks, and the clerk's office accepts filings through the next workday after it closes.

The filing states your own opinion of value. Should bills go out before the appeal ends and the final figure beat your claim, a supplemental bill covers the gap. The board meets between 25 and 35 days after the window and may sit five days. Bring what the Department of Revenue lists as evidence: land and building details, insurance policies, construction costs and sales listings.

How are rural parcels valued in Monroe County?

Across 329 square miles and 34.4 people per square mile, many Monroe County sales come with land. The PVA must visit every parcel at least every four years and add new construction yearly, the Department of Revenue says. Farm land may be assessed at agricultural value instead of fair cash value, so ask the PVA how your acreage is classified before you list it.

Parcels near the Tennessee line, along the river or up in the hills can differ widely. If the roll shows a building that was torn down, or misses a barn you added, raise it at a PVA conference.

How does the homestead exemption work in Monroe County?

Anyone who owns and lives in a house and has turned 65, or carries a total disability classification, may claim it. Apply at the Monroe County PVA with proof, on the state's form.

KRS 132.810 sets one exemption per unit, even if the owner is both elderly and disabled, or several older residents share the unit. The amount follows a federal price index and is rechecked every two years. A sale or the owner's death must be reported to the PVA.

Can you sell a Monroe County house that owes tax?

Yes, and the usual route starts with a written payoff. The sheriff supplies it before April 15, and the clerk does afterward, when the figure rises monthly and carries the clerk and attorney fees.

Under KRS 134.015 the person who owned on January 1 owes that year's tax personally, and a lien can follow the property for 11 years. Houses in Monroe County that need work, or came to heirs, can change hands with a bill still open, so build the payoff into your numbers when you compare a listing with a cash sale.

More questions about Monroe County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who accepts Monroe County property tax payments?

The county sheriff, in Suite E at 200 North Main Street, Tompkinsville. Call (270) 487-6622.

When did the 2026 Monroe County tax sale take place?

The clerk set it for September 23, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Central. Phone (270) 487-5471 to learn whether a certificate was sold.

Is an installment plan available on a late Monroe County bill?

Yes, through the County Attorney's office, provided the certificate was not sold at the tax sale.

Can a delinquent bill be paid to the clerk by check in the mail?

No, mailed payments must be money orders. Checks, cash and credit cards work only at the clerk's office.

Where is the Monroe County PVA?

Suite A, 200 North Main Street, Tompkinsville. The office phone is (270) 487-6401.

What kind of place is Bracken County, Kentucky?

Bracken County is small and entirely rural, running along the Ohio River in the northern part of the state. Brooksville holds the courthouse, Augusta is the biggest town, and Germantown rounds out the three incorporated cities. Across the water lie Clermont and Brown counties in Ohio. On the Kentucky side the neighbors are Mason, Robertson, Harrison and Pendleton. Bracken falls inside the Cincinnati metro area, and it covers 209 square miles.

Kentucky made it the 23rd county in 1796 and named it for Big and Little Bracken creeks. The seat moved from Augusta to Woodward's Crossing, today's Brooksville, in 1833. White burley tobacco was bred from Bracken seed, and farm fields still define the landscape. The 2020 count was 8,400 residents, none of them in an urban area, and the July 2025 estimate stands at 8,511.

The Augusta area holds several Underground Railroad sites, because local abolitionists helped people cross the river to Ripley, Ohio, and Augusta College, founded in 1822, was the first Methodist college in the world.

When a value dispute arises, the sales records held at the PVA are what the county appeals board looks at.

What do Census numbers say about housing in Bracken County?

QuickFacts covers 2020 to 2024 for the figures below. Against Boyle, Breckinridge and Bullitt, Bracken has the cheapest typical home and the longest drive to work.

Bracken County housing and work snapshot from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts
MeasureBracken County
Typical value of an owner's home$125,000
Share of homes lived in by owners78.5%
Typical monthly rent$756
Typical monthly cost for a mortgaged owner$1,144
Households3,364
Average trip to work34.5 minutes
Typical household income$66,319

The 2020 count found 3,839 housing units, with 13.3 percent empty. Employers numbered 98 in 2023, and about 58.3 percent of residents 16 and older were in the labor force. Turnover is low: 95.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, the highest share of the four counties. The county counts 462 veterans, and broadband reaches 89.8 percent of households, and retail sales for 2022 totaled $29.6 million, or $3,506 per resident.

Who do I call about a Bracken County tax bill?

Valuing and collecting happen in separate offices that share the courthouse at 116 West Miami Street in Brooksville. The Property Valuation Administrator, 606-735-2228, owns the assessment, the property address, the name and mailing address on the bill, and exemptions. The Sheriff's Office (606-735-3233, second floor) only collects.

  • Address or name wrong: fix it on the return stub or call the PVA.
  • Disagree with the value: call the PVA before paying.
  • Bills from earlier years: County Clerk, 606-735-2952, on a separate check.

An online portal shows and takes payment for bills. Cards add a 2.50 percent charge that the cardholder pays and the sheriff does not keep. By mail, the check must cover the exact amount due.

When does the Bracken County discount end?

The sheriff gives the 2 percent discount period as October 1 through November 1. Bills go directly to owners. Later cutoffs and penalty steps are printed on the bill itself, and the sheriff's office can read them to you.

Escrow causes most of the grief. The sheriff mails to the owner and never to a mortgage company, so a borrower whose lender pays from escrow should pass the bill along as soon as it lands, or check that the lender has asked the sheriff for it. A check that bounces puts the bill back to unpaid, with the repayment schedule on the bill and a returned-check fee on top.

Why might a Bracken County bill carry the previous owner's name?

Ownership for tax purposes freezes on January 1. If a purchase closes after that, the bill for the year is addressed to the person who sold, and the PVA works from recorded deeds to find new owners. A buyer whose copy never turns up can ask the sheriff for one.

For a seller, that means a bill can show up at an address already left behind. The settlement agent normally divides the year by days of ownership and either pays the sheriff or credits whichever side will. Leave a forwarding address with the closing agent.

How does a Bracken County owner challenge an assessment?

Book a conference at the PVA first, since state rules require one before an appeal. The roll opens to inspection for thirteen days beginning with the first Monday of May, and appeals are filed with the clerk by the next workday after those days end.

If the PVA raises a value above what you listed, KRS 132.450(4) obliges the office to notify you. Anyone paid to speak for you must be an attorney, accountant, broker, appraiser or other qualified professional and must show your written authorization. Hearings may be recorded on audio.

What happens to an unpaid Bracken County bill after April 15?

The sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the County Clerk, who records a lien and files each as a certificate of delinquency. The clerk gives the Department of Revenue a list by May 15, and the Department publishes each county's list by June 1. On the normal schedule a tax sale can fall on any business day between July 14 and August 28.

Before that, the county attorney sends a 30-day letter and a second letter naming the sale date. The list is advertised in the paper with the biggest paid circulation between 30 and 45 days ahead and posted online at least 30 days ahead. An owner who still owes at the sale risks having the lien assigned to an outside buyer, who may add fees.

Interest accrues at 1 percent for every month or fraction. In the state's worked example, a $1,000 bill grows to $1,254 at transfer and to about $1,660 if paid after the June advertising.

Does Bracken County offer homestead relief?

Yes, to owners who turn 65 during the year or are permanently disabled. The Department of Revenue capped the exemption at $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026. The house must be your owned, occupied and maintained residence on January 1, and the application is due at the PVA by December 31.

The sheriff tells eligible owners to phone the PVA before paying a bill that lacks the exemption, because the exemption shrinks the bill. About 20.3 percent of Bracken residents are 65 or older.

How can I sell a Bracken County house that owes tax?

Treat the tax as a closing item. Get the present balance from the sheriff and any older balance from the clerk, and have the closing agent pay both from the proceeds. Inherited houses, houses with tenants and houses that need more work than a retail buyer will take on often sell to cash buyers who accept the property as it stands and pay the tax at the table.

More questions about Bracken County, KY Property Tax Guide

What is the Bracken County PVA's phone number?

606-735-2228, at the courthouse in Brooksville. The office handles assessments, mailing addresses on bills and homestead exemptions.

Where do I pay a Bracken County property tax bill?

At the sheriff's second-floor office in the courthouse, by mail, or through the sheriff's online portal. Card payments add 2.50 percent.

Does my mortgage company get my Bracken County tax bill?

No. The sheriff mails only to the owner. If your lender escrows taxes, forward the bill or ask the lender to request it.

Where do I pay a prior-year Bracken County bill?

At the County Clerk's office, 606-735-2952, with a separate check from the current year's payment.

Who owes tax on a Bracken County house sold in the spring?

The bill goes to whoever owned the house on January 1. Buyer and seller normally split the year at closing, and the agent pays the sheriff.

What should a Princeton seller know about how Caldwell County taxes a house?

The local Property Valuation Administrator values the house, the Caldwell County Sheriff collects the money, and anything unpaid after April 15 goes to the clerk. Values are fixed as of January 1, and the Department of Revenue says the PVA must walk every parcel at least once in four years, as described on its real property assessment page.

Princeton anchors a county of roughly 345 square miles of land. A Caldwell bill adds together several taxing districts, among them the state, the county and the schools, and each of those bodies picks its own rate. The assessor has no say over rates.

The county has long been farm country. Farmland is taxed on what it can produce rather than on market price. The sheriff's site says a parcel of ten or more acres used for livestock or crops, timber included, can qualify, so an owner with acreage should ask the PVA how the land is carried before listing.

Which dates and penalties apply to a Caldwell County tax bill?

The payment year runs on a fixed monthly ladder that starts on November 1 and ends on April 15. The sheriff's tax page lays out the steps, and the statewide framework behind them is KRS 134.015.

Collection for 2026 opened November 2, 2026, after bills were mailed October 30, and the sheriff replaced postcards with letter-style bills. Whatever the phase, a payment is credited if it is postmarked, handed over or dropped in the box before the next phase begins. The ladder looks like this:

  • All of November: the bill less 2%.
  • All of December: the bare face amount.
  • All of January: 5% extra.
  • February 1 through April 15: 21% extra.

The office is the first door to the right off Main Street inside the Princeton courthouse. It takes checks, money orders, cashier's checks, cash and, at the counter, cards with a processing surcharge. A drop box by the east courthouse door handles after-hours payments, with no cash allowed. Hours run 8 am to 4 pm on weekdays, and the sheriff posts a holiday closing list each season.

Which Caldwell County office answers which tax question?

Three numbers cover almost every question: 270-365-2088 for the sheriff, 270-365-7227 for the PVA and 270-365-6754 for the clerk. The PVA is on the courthouse's second floor at 100 East Market Street, and the sheriff takes mail at Room 25 of the same building.

  • Sheriff: mails bills, accepts payment until April 15, and runs a view-only bill search online.
  • PVA: sets values, takes homestead and disability forms, and holds the conference that must come before an appeal.
  • County clerk: takes over delinquent bills and records deeds.

The bill is addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. A buyer whose bill went to the previous owner can print it from the sheriff's site, and the sheriff, who does not receive deed transfers, lists the new name in care-of form the first year.

How can a Princeton owner dispute a Caldwell County value?

Book a conference with the PVA first, then file at the clerk's office no later than the workday after public inspection ends. Inspection lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May, and the local appeals board sits up to five days beginning 25 to 35 days later, as the state property tax calendar explains.

Bring facts, not opinions. Useful evidence includes lot and building descriptions, insurance papers, what the house cost to build and listings of comparable sales. An appeal without that paper is denied. Skipping the local board also closes the door to later review. Because bills can print before a case ends, the value you claim is billed in the meantime, and a supplemental bill arrives if the board lands higher.

Whatever number survives is what a buyer's lender and title company will see. A Princeton owner whose house has gained a new roof or an addition should check that the PVA's record describes the house as it stands.

Which relief programs lower a Caldwell County bill?

Owner-occupants who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can have part of the assessed value removed. The sheriff's page puts the maximum at $46,350 for 2024 and 2025, and KRS 132.810 resets it every two years, so the PVA can quote the current figure.

Applicants must live in the house they own, prove their age and claim no exemption elsewhere. The form is completed at the PVA office, which the sheriff says takes under five minutes. The benefit stays with the owner, so whoever buys from you files separately.

An older seller should confirm the exemption shows on the bill before closing. The sheriff asks owners to sort out a missing exemption with the PVA before paying.

What happens to the Caldwell County bill at closing?

The lien stays with the parcel while the closing agent splits the year between the two sides. According to the sheriff's FAQ, your agent or lender explains the split, since the sheriff is never told how a sale handled it.

Unpaid bills stay alive after a sale. Delinquent bills move to the clerk with penalties and 1% monthly interest, as the Department of Revenue's collection process page shows. A Princeton owner with back taxes should get the clerk's payoff figure before picking a closing date.

Where a lender escrows taxes, the bill still goes to the owner, and the sheriff says forwarding it is the owner's job. Checking in with the servicer now and then keeps a missed forward from becoming a penalty.

Who is buying and selling homes in Caldwell County?

Caldwell County has about 12,600 residents, and its typical owner-occupied home is valued at $118,500 for 2020 to 2024, far under Campbell County in northern Kentucky. Princeton, with 6,270 people in 2020, grew up around railroad junctions. It hosts a University of Kentucky research campus, factories such as Bremner provide jobs, and a December 2021 tornado hit the south side of town.

Caldwell County profile drawn from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page

Residents (2025 estimate)12,609
Homes counted in mid-20256,122
Share lived in by owners70.2%
Typical home value$118,500
Typical monthly rent$767
Typical household income$59,583

Roughly 30 percent of occupied homes here are rentals, and 93.4 percent of residents had not moved in the past year, so few houses change hands. Those that do often belong to estates, older owners or farm families, and an owner facing repairs or a tenant may prefer a direct cash sale to skip showings.

More questions about Caldwell County, KY Property Tax Guide

What dates matter for Caldwell County tax bills?

The bill opens for payment on November 1, and the 2% discount lasts through November 30. December is face value, January adds 5% and February 1 to April 15 adds 21%. Anything still open on April 15 goes to the county clerk.

Where can I pay a tax bill in Princeton?

Go to the sheriff's office in the courthouse, mail to 100 E. Market St., Room 25, or use the drop box at the east door. The website search only displays bills, and phone payments are not taken.

Is there a tax break for homeowners over 65 in Caldwell County?

Yes, the homestead exemption covers owners who live in the home and turn 65 during the year. Apply at the PVA office with proof of age. It trims the assessed value, and a new owner must apply again.

What if my Princeton house sells before the bill comes?

The bill is issued to the January 1 owner, so you may still get it. The closing agent prorates, and a buyer who never receives it can print a copy from the sheriff's site.

Do I need repairs before a cash sale in Caldwell County?

No. A cash buyer can take the house as-is. Back taxes and liens come out of your proceeds, so ask the sheriff and clerk for amounts early.

Which Johnson County offices handle property tax?

In Johnson County the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) puts a number on your parcel, the sheriff takes your money, and the county clerk holds the liens and the appeal paperwork. Calling the wrong desk costs a day, so keep the split straight.

County offices cluster at 230 Court Street in Paintsville. The clerk sits in Suite 124 at (606) 789-2557 and is closed Saturdays. The sheriff's page gives (606) 789-3411, and both offices run on a weekday 8 to 4 clock.

Rates are not the PVA's call. The Fiscal Court sits on the second Monday of the month at 4:45 PM, and the county's two public school systems, Johnson County Schools and Paintsville Independent, are among the bodies that levy tax on a bill.

What are the key tax dates for a Johnson County parcel?

Value is struck on January 1, the roll opens for review on the first Monday of May, and bills arrive in the fall. Those dates come from Kentucky law, so they match every other county, but the offices that act on them are Johnson County's own.

The review window lasts 13 days and includes Saturdays. Anything you want changed has to be raised in that window, and the sheriff's discount for early payment ends November 1. Business equipment and other personal property is listed with the PVA through May 15. Ask the sheriff to confirm each year's collection dates, because the state sometimes shifts them.

What happens to an unpaid Johnson County bill?

On April 15 the sheriff hands any unpaid bill to the Johnson County Clerk. The clerk records a lien, and the bill can end up in the hands of a private buyer.

A tax sale cannot come sooner than 90 days after the handoff, under KRS 134.128, and interest of 1 percent a month runs in the meantime. The county attorney writes to the owner, and the clerk publishes the delinquent list before the sale. A county that also sells overdue oil and gas or unmined mineral bills gets 60 extra days, which suits a coalfield county where those interests are billed apart from the surface.

  • The lien rides with the land, so a buyer inherits it unless it is cleared.
  • Whoever buys the bill at the sale can add fees of their own.
  • Letters go to the address on file, so an outdated address means missed warnings.

What is the appeal route for a Johnson County value?

Ask the PVA for a conference in May. No filing with the board is allowed until that meeting has happened, and the PVA must explain how your number was built.

If the meeting settles nothing, file at the clerk's office in time for the following workday. A panel of local property owners hears the case. It must turn down any appeal that shows up without proof, for instance insurance policies, building costs or sales listings.

  • Ask which sales the PVA relied on for your house.
  • Get repair quotes if damage is missing from the record.
  • A paid representative must be an attorney, CPA, licensed appraiser or another category the state recognizes.

Past the local board, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals is the last stop. With median values near $120,000, even a few thousand dollars off the value shifts a bill, so the call is worth making.

Who can claim a homestead or other exemption in Johnson County?

A homeowner who is 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement plan, can take the homestead and disability deduction. One per household is the limit, and it travels with the owner, so a purchaser has to file fresh.

Kentucky resets the dollar amount every two years. A neighboring-region PVA posts $49,100 for 2025 to 2026, so confirm the Johnson County figure with the PVA. Service-connected totally disabled veterans and people ruled disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement file once, while those classed disabled by an out-of-state agency refile every year.

Churches, schools and charities apply on Revenue Form 62A023. Farmland is taxed on use value, a break the state says can be large where market prices run well above farm prices. Separately from property tax, the county charges an occupational tax of 0.5 percent on wages and net profit earned inside Johnson County.

How does Johnson County housing compare with other Kentucky counties?

Homes cost far less here than in the state's metro counties. Census survey figures for 2020 to 2024 put Johnson County's median home value at $120,200, a number that shapes how much any one assessment change matters to a bill.

Johnson County beside two metro-area Kentucky counties

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, 2020 to 2024.

Johnson County counted 22,680 people in 2020 and an estimated 22,051 in July 2025, a drop of 2.8 percent. Its population peaked at 25,771 in 1940. The 2020 census found 12.0 percent of the county's 10,493 housing units vacant, against 5.8 percent in Jessamine County and 6.9 percent in Kenton County.

Floodplain rules touch some parcels. Building in a Special Flood Hazard Area needs both a state and a local permit, and the county asks owners to call (606) 789-2550 before any development.

What does the Johnson County landscape look like?

Johnson County covers 264 square miles in the Eastern Coalfield and borders Lawrence, Martin, Floyd, Magoffin and Morgan counties. The highest point is Stuffley Knob at 1,496 feet, and the lowest is the Levisa Fork on the Lawrence County line at roughly 550 feet.

Paintsville is the only city and the seat. Van Lear and West Van Lear are census-designated places, and Paintsville Lake State Park, with a 1,140 acre lake, lies near Staffordsville. Big Sandy Community and Technical College runs two campuses in the county, at Mayo and Hager Hill.

On a rural parcel here, check the access road, the exact acreage and any flood zone before you set a price.

How did Johnson County's coal and oil history shape its parcels?

The railroad reached Paintsville in 1904 and opened the coal era, which lasted more than a century. Consolidation Coal and North East Coal built the towns of Van Lear and Thealka, and by the 1940s as many as 1,500 men worked the county's mines.

Oil and gas followed from 1917, and in 1922 the Johnson-Magoffin field produced over 2,000,000 barrels. Coal output peaked in 2008 at 2,713,196 tons. Wikipedia adds that many residents sold their mineral rights cheaply during the coal boom.

For a seller, that history is practical. Ask the title company whether minerals were severed from the surface on your parcel, and ask the sheriff whether a separately billed mineral or oil and gas tax bill is tied to it.

What should a Johnson County seller confirm before closing?

Three calls cover nearly every surprise: the sheriff for the bill and a payoff, the clerk for any certificate of delinquency, and the PVA for exemption status.

The county lists separate fire and rescue units for Paintsville, Van Lear, West Van Lear and others, and a Kentucky bill can stack school, city, county and fire levies. Ask the sheriff for a line-by-line breakdown. One Kentucky sheriff's FAQ explains that the seller's share is settled with the buyer at closing while the owner of record pays the full bill.

Which office collects Johnson County property tax?

The Johnson County Sheriff, whose office lists (606) 789-3411.

Where is a Johnson County assessment appeal filed?

At the county clerk, 230 Court Street, Suite 124, Paintsville, once the PVA conference is done. The filing falls due the workday after the May review window shuts.

When does an unpaid Johnson County bill move to the clerk?

After April 15. The clerk then carries it as a certificate of delinquency with a lien on record.

Does a Johnson County homeowner get the 65 exemption automatically?

No. The owner applies through the PVA, and the home must be a primary residence.

Who decides Johnson County tax rates?

The taxing bodies on your bill, such as the Fiscal Court and the school districts. The PVA values property and the sheriff collects.

How does property tax work in Bell County, Kentucky?

Bell County is a small, low priced market in the southeast corner of Kentucky, and its tax bills move through the same chain of offices as any Kentucky county: the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets value, the sheriff bills and collects, and the county clerk takes appeals and unpaid bills.

The county touches Tennessee and Virginia at the Cumberland Gap, where the Wilderness Road ran in 1775. Pineville is the seat, Middlesboro is the largest city, and Arjay is a census designated place. The legislature formed the county in 1867 from parts of Knox and Harlan counties and first called it Josh Bell County, after a congressman, before shortening the name in 1873. Bell is the only Kentucky county holding both a state resort park, Pine Mountain, and a national park unit, Cumberland Gap National Historical Park. Steep ground and protected land govern where houses can go and how far a buyer must drive to reach one.

How has Bell County's population changed, and why does it matter to a sale?

Bell County lost about 5.3 percent of its people between the 2020 census count of 24,097 and the 2025 estimate of 22,829. Wikipedia's historical table shows 47,602 residents in 1950, so the county now holds roughly half the population it had seventy years ago.

That history shows in the housing stock. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates put the middle owned home at $89,000 and the middle household income at $31,354, with 31.8 percent of residents in poverty and rent at $592 a month. The 2020 census found 11,517 housing units with 13.8 percent vacant, and only 41 building permits were issued in 2025.
