At prices this low, a tax lien plus clerk fees and interest can swallow a bigger slice of a sale than in a high value county, so check the tax status first.

Which offices handle property tax in Bell County?

Three offices cover most questions, and a fourth takes over once a bill goes delinquent.

  • The Bell County PVA values real estate, takes age and disability exemption forms, and schedules appeal conferences.
  • The Bell County Sheriff sends the bills each fall and collects the money.
  • The Bell County Clerk, whose office keeps weekday hours, files deeds, mortgages and liens and takes in bills that go delinquent.
  • The county attorney mails the warning letters that follow a transfer and can set up payment plans.

The City of Pineville posts its own property tax page. The sheriff has collected Pineville's tax on the county bill since tax year 2020. The city's page shows 27.6 cents for each $100 of assessed real property value, but call city hall for the rate on your bill.

The clerk's recording room matters to sellers for another reason. The Bell County courthouse burned in 1914 and 1918, and a 1977 flood damaged it and destroyed stored documents. If an old deed or probate record looks incomplete, ask the clerk what the recorded chain shows.

When are Bell County property tax bills due?

KRS 134.015 sets the cycle. In a year when collection starts after November 1, the state grants 30 days per stage instead of the usual dates.

On the usual calendar, paying by November 1 saves 2 percent, the bill stands at face value through December, January adds 5 percent, and February 1 to April 15 carries a combined 21 percent. Payment is made to the sheriff.

The tax belongs to the person on title each January 1. A Bell County seller closing in spring therefore owes that year's bill unless the sales contract shifts it. If no bill reaches you, the sheriff can provide a duplicate.

How is a Bell County assessment challenged?

Phone the Bell County PVA and request a conference during the May inspection period. Kentucky requires that meeting before any filing, and the period lasts roughly two weeks.

If the two of you stay apart, the paperwork goes to the clerk on the next business day after inspection closes. Revenue's own example: an inspection ending May 20 means a May 21 filing. Write your claimed value on the form.

  • A three member local board hears the case roughly a month later.
  • Bring evidence: comparable sales, a contractor's estimate or an appraisal.
  • The PVA defends the assessed figure.
  • A certified letter reports the outcome and what to do next.

With typical values near $89,000, small gaps matter. A house with a failing roof or foundation can be valued like a sound neighbor unless you document the problem.

Which Bell County owners get a homestead break?

Yes. An owner who has reached 65, or who is totally disabled, can claim it on a residence. Apply at the Bell County PVA, and approval trims the assessed value by a fixed amount.

The figure began at $6,500 in 1972 and has been indexed to inflation since. Boone County's PVA lists $49,100 for 2026, and the Bell County PVA can confirm what your bill uses. A household receives a single exemption, even when both spouses qualify.

  • Approval carries forward as long as the applicant stays in the house.
  • A buyer starts over with a new application.
  • Disabled owners under 65 refile yearly, except veterans with a service rating and owners with a permanent finding.

After a death, an heir who sells should notify the PVA so the address loses the exemption.

How should a Bell County seller handle unpaid taxes?

A seller can pay ahead of closing or have the closing agent pay out of proceeds. Either way, ask the sheriff or clerk for a written payoff, since the total grows month by month after April 15.

After that the clerk holds a delinquency certificate and a lien. Interest grows at 1 percent a month, clerk and attorney commissions of 10 and 20 percent arrive, and a summer sale can pass the certificate to a private investor. KRS 134.015 lets the lien last 11 years even if the house changes hands.

Bell County has three public school districts: Bell County, Middlesboro Independent and Pineville Independent. The sheriff can say which school district and city rate appear on your parcel's bill. Heirs and owners of vacant houses who want to skip repairs and carrying costs may favor a cash sale, which clears liens at closing against a written payoff.

More questions about Bell County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who takes Bell County tax payments?

Pay the Bell County Sheriff. City of Pineville tax appears on the same bill as county tax, so one payment covers both.

How late can a Bell County appeal be filed?

File with the county clerk by the next business day after the May inspection period ends. A conference with the PVA must come first, and the period opens on the first Monday in May.

What does a typical Bell County house cost?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 data gives $89,000 for owned homes. Median household income for the same years is $31,354.

What do late Bell County payments cost?

On the usual calendar, 5 percent is added in January and a combined 21 percent applies from February 1 to April 15. After April 15 the clerk adds interest and fees.

Does a lien stop a Bell County sale?

Yes. The lien stays with the property until paid, so the payoff is usually taken from the seller's proceeds at closing. Get the figure in writing from the sheriff or clerk first.

  • Page had no schedule or payment methods

Which Clay County offices deal with property tax?

Clay County splits the job three ways. The Property Valuation Administrator decides what a parcel is worth, the Sheriff prints and collects the bills, and the County Clerk takes appeal papers and later inherits any bill the sheriff could not collect. Knowing which desk owns which question saves a seller several wrong-number calls.

All three share one building, 102 Richmond Road in Manchester. The PVA sets no tax rate and accepts no payments. Its work ends at the number on the roll.

Clay County property tax contacts (source: Clay County Fiscal Court department pages and county clerk site)
OfficeHandlesReach it
Property Valuation AdministratorValuation, exemptions, ownership changesSuite 200, 606-598-3832, Monday to Friday, closing at 4:30
SheriffTax bills and collectionSuite 100, 606-598-3471
County ClerkAppeal filings, unpaid-bill certificates, deed recordingSuite 101, 606-598-2544

What is Clay County like for someone selling a house?

Clay County sprawls across 471 square miles of Appalachian hills with Manchester at its center. Kentucky created it in 1807 from land that belonged to Floyd, Knox and Madison, and named it for Green Clay. A fire took the courthouse in January 1936. Seven counties touch its borders: Owsley, Perry, Leslie, Bell, Knox, Laurel and Jackson. The Census Bureau groups Clay with the Corbin micropolitan area.

The 2020 count was 20,345 people. The July 2025 estimate is 19,465, which is 4.3 percent fewer, so a listing draws from a shrinking local pool. Census QuickFacts add this detail:

  • 7,288 households living in 8,781 housing units
  • 76.4 percent of households own their home
  • Typical home value: $90,700
  • Typical rent: $724 a month
  • Typical monthly owner cost: $978 with a mortgage, $367 without

A seller pricing near $90,700 will notice any unpaid tax in the final settlement figure.

How does the Clay County PVA decide what a house is worth?

Valuation is pegged to January 1. Kentucky wants fair cash value, which means the price a voluntary sale between informed parties would produce. Staff walk every parcel at least once in each four-year stretch, and new buildings join the roll every year.

A purchase can simplify things. When you bought in the previous year, the deed price may serve as next January's value, so long as nothing about the building changed. Frankfort values four categories itself: public service companies, bank shares, omitted tangible property and vehicles. Everything else, real and personal, belongs to the local PVA.

What else does the Clay County PVA keep track of?

Beyond the annual value, the office follows ownership changes, maintains parcel maps, updates building details and administers exemptions on real estate. A seller can ask the staff whether the map shows the correct acreage, whether the building record lists a finished basement or an outbuilding that no longer stands, and whether the exemption on file still matches the owner.

Errors in those records flow straight into the bill. Suppose a garage came down years ago but still sits on the record: it keeps lifting the value until someone asks for a correction. Visit during open hours, 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, or write to the office at 102 Richmond Road, Suite 200, Manchester, KY 40962.

When does a Clay County tax bill come due?

Collection follows Kentucky's fall-to-spring pattern, and the sheriff runs it. The Sheriff's page on the Fiscal Court website carries a View Property Tax Bill button for parcel lookups. The sheriff's office, at 606-598-3471, can confirm the exact opening date, since the state lets a county use 30-day phases when a different calendar is needed.

The state's typical pattern:

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent off
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount
  • January: 5 percent added
  • February 1 to April 15: 21 percent added

Because value is fixed on January 1, a bill may carry a previous owner's name after a sale made later in the year.

What is the route for contesting a Clay County valuation?

The sequence is fixed, and missing one step closes the door.

  • Look for the notice the PVA mails after raising a value.
  • Request a conference with the PVA or a deputy while the tax roll is open for inspection. That window starts the first Monday of May and covers two weeks, Monday through Saturday.
  • If talks fail, file the appeal paper with the County Clerk by close of business the next workday after the window ends.
  • Attend the local board hearing, held 25 to 35 days after inspection. The board gets five sitting days unless the state grants more.
  • Bring proof: sales of similar houses, an appraisal, or building costs. With no facts, the board has to deny you.

Filing and then failing to appear forfeits the right to continue. A dissatisfied owner can carry the case to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Does Clay County give a homestead exemption?

It does, to people who live in the house and are at least 65 or are classified as totally disabled. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the amount is $49,100, taken off the valuation before tax is figured. A home worth the county's typical $90,700 would be taxed on $41,600.

Apply at the PVA office in Manchester, 606-598-3832. Age is shown with a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. A disability claim needs paperwork from the federal agency or retirement system that made the classification. Most disability claims renew annually. Exceptions cover veterans with a service-connected disability and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

What happens to an unpaid Clay County bill?

When business closes on April 15, the sheriff hands the bill to the County Clerk. It becomes a certificate of delinquency and a lien on the parcel. Interest of 1 percent per month begins, and the clerk adds 10 percent while the county attorney adds 20 percent.

The county attorney writes to owners in May and, if necessary, June, and can arrange installments. From mid-July, certificates may be sold to outside buyers through late October. After a sale you owe the buyer, and more fees follow. The Clay County Clerk's website posts a delinquent tax page for each year.

Where can a Clay County seller look up records online?

The Fiscal Court website, claycountyky.com, has a page for each department with contact details and hours. The sheriff's page holds the bill lookup. The County Clerk's own site lists Recordings, Fees, Forms and an Open Records Request page, along with a delinquent tax page for each year, which is the place to check whether a parcel was advertised for sale.

How do I handle the tax bill when I sell in Clay County?

The closing agent normally pays the current bill out of your proceeds and splits it with the buyer. An open delinquency has to be settled first, because the lien stays with the parcel. Get a payoff amount from the sheriff before signing a contract, and ask the PVA whether an exemption on the parcel ends when ownership changes.

The deed adds a separate charge. Kentucky taxes the seller $0.50 for every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts in full. The clerk takes it at the recording counter. A $90,700 price makes 182 slices, so the charge is $91. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers, correction deeds and nominal gifts between parent and child fall outside the tax.

More questions about Clay County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who mails the Clay County tax bill?

The Sheriff does. If nothing arrives, call 606-598-3471 or use the bill lookup on the sheriff's page of the Fiscal Court site.

Can a Clay County owner contest a value in summer?

Generally no. Both the conference and the clerk filing must land in the May inspection window, with the filing due the next workday after it ends. Phone the PVA at 606-598-3832 in spring.

Does the Clay County PVA take tax payments?

No. That office only values property and processes exemptions. Money goes to the sheriff, then to the County Clerk after mid-April.

Is transfer tax owed on a Clay County sale?

Usually yes. The seller owes $0.50 per $500 of price, and the clerk collects it before recording. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers and correction deeds are exempt.

Can a Clay County house with a delinquent bill still be sold?

Yes. The delinquency gets paid at or before closing. Ask the County Clerk for the total with interest and fees so the title company can build it into the payoff.

Who do Fleming County owners deal with on property tax?

Two courthouse-square offices carry most of the load, and a third takes over when a bill goes bad. The PVA answers value questions at 606-845-1401, and the county's PVA page lists weekday opening from 8 until 4:30. The sheriff bills and collects at 201 Court Square in Flemingsburg, with phones answered at 606-845-4701 (press 1) from 8 until 4:30 Monday to Friday. Once a bill is delinquent, the county clerk handles it.

It helps to know what the PVA will not do. By its own description, the office appraises property at fair cash value, maintains tax maps and ownership records and processes exemptions, but it neither writes laws nor sets rates. Rates come from the fiscal court, city councils, the school board and other districts. The fiscal court itself meets at the courthouse, 100 Court Square, on the second Tuesday of every month at 9 a.m. Eastern.

A PVA or deputy walks each property at least once in four years and may measure the outside of a building whether or not the owner is in. Send the PVA any new mailing address in writing so notices do not go astray.

What does the Fleming County tax year look like?

Fleming runs the standard Kentucky calendar, which opens October 1. Statements usually leave the sheriff's office near the end of September. A missing bill changes nothing about the debt, so owners without one phone 606-845-4701 and ask for the balance, or use the sheriff's online tax record search.

Fleming County Sheriff, 2026 collection periods and the share of the bill each one asks for
DatesPay this much

The 2026 discount window closed on November 1, 2026, and the face amount applies through December 31. The sheriff's example makes the stakes plain: a $1,000 bill costs $980 inside the discount window, $1,000 afterward, and $1,210 by February.

  • Counter payments are cash, a check payable to the Fleming County Sheriff, or a money order.
  • Cards work at the counter or by phone and add a 2.5 percent service charge.
  • Mail must carry a postmark on or before the deadline.
  • A drop box at the sheriff's door stays open at all hours and is emptied at 8 each morning under camera watch.

How does a Fleming County owner dispute an assessment?

Start with the PVA, because the board will not hear anyone who skipped that step. Kentucky opens the tax roll for inspection for thirteen days beginning the first Monday of May. A conference during that stretch keeps the right to file with the county clerk alive until the next business day after the stretch ends. The Department of Revenue's illustration: inspection from May 3 to May 17 means the clerk must have the paper by the close of May 18.

After that, the local board of assessment appeals convenes 25 to 35 days later. Bring paper. The board turns down any appeal lacking insurance policies, building costs, sale listings or similar proof.

  • At the conference the PVA must walk you through how the value was reached and record the result.
  • A paid agent must hold one of the credentials the state lists, such as attorney, CPA or licensed appraiser, and show your signed authorization.
  • Hearings may be audio-recorded by the taxpayer.

The sheriff will redirect any value complaint to the PVA. Filing and then missing the hearing closes the door to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Is a homestead exemption worth claiming in Fleming County?

For a qualifying owner it is worth claiming. The state deducts $49,100 from the assessed value of the home on the 2025 and 2026 rolls, and the tax is figured on what remains. Fleming County's typical owner-occupied house is valued at $134,700 by the Census Bureau, which would leave $85,600 taxable.

The PVA takes the form. Owners show their age with a birth certificate, license, passport or comparable record. Total disability must be certified by a federal agency or a retirement system, with benefits paid across the entire year, and most such claims have to be re-filed each year; veterans with service-connected disabilities and people found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from that requirement.

If a lender pays the tax from escrow, the sheriff still expects the owner to confirm that it was paid on time. Check the sheriff's record search after the discount period closes.

What happens with Fleming County taxes when a house sells?

The tax follows ownership, and the sheriff will talk through proration for any buyer or seller who calls with a closing date. Under KRS 134.015 the tax is the owner's own debt from the assessment date, and under KRS 134.420 a lien on an unpaid parcel can stay for 11 years after a sale. A sensible order of events: get the balance from the sheriff before listing, then have the closing agent settle the year's bill.

When the sheriff's office closes on April 15, whatever is unpaid goes to the Fleming County Clerk under KRS 134.122. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, commissions and a lien fee follow, and the county attorney writes the owner twice. The clerk then holds a sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer.

The deed also carries a state transfer tax, which the seller pays. It equals $0.50 per $500 of price, so a sale at the county's median value of $134,700 costs $135.00; the 270th block of $500 is only partly filled but counts in full.

Ask the clerk's office in Flemingsburg for any payoff on a transferred bill, and tell the PVA about a new mailing address after closing.

What is the setting for a Fleming County house sale?

Fleming County was cut from Mason County in 1798 and named for Colonel John Fleming. Flemingsburg is the seat, Ewing is the second city and Elizaville is a census-designated place. The county measures 351 square miles, 349 of them land, and borders Mason, Lewis, Rowan, Bath, Nicholas and Robertson counties. The General Assembly gave it the title Covered Bridge Capital of Kentucky in 1998, and the county's courthouse was replaced in 1830 and again in 1952. The 2020 count classed every resident as rural.

Census QuickFacts adds some numbers sellers can use:

  • 15,787 residents in 2025, up 4.7 percent from 2020.
  • 74.8 percent of housing occupied by its owner, across 5,859 households.
  • Typical home value of $134,700 and typical monthly rent of $715.
  • Household income of $49,307 at the median.
  • A commute of 33.1 minutes on average.
  • No building permits issued in 2025.

Without new construction, nearly every buyer is shopping among older houses, so condition matters. A seller who owes taxes or faces repairs can weigh the cost of fixing up a listing against an as-is cash offer.

More questions about Fleming County, KY Property Tax Guide

When do Fleming County tax bills arrive?

Statements typically go out at the end of September. In 2026 the 2 percent discount period began October 1, and an owner who has no bill by then can call 606-845-4701 and press 1.

What does a late payment cost in Fleming County?

January adds 5 percent. From February 1 to April 15 the total reaches 121 percent of the bill, and anything unpaid after that goes to the county clerk.

Where is the Fleming County Sheriff's tax counter?

201 Court Square in Flemingsburg, open weekdays from 8 until 4:30. A drop box at the entrance takes payments around the clock.

Who changes a Fleming County property value?

Only the PVA can, at 606-845-1401. The sheriff cannot alter an assessment, and a PVA conference has to come before any appeal.

Who gets the Fleming County homestead exemption?

Homeowners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and live in the house. It removes $49,100 from the value on the 2025 and 2026 rolls.

Which McKee offices touch a Jackson County tax bill?

Property tax in this rural county runs through three McKee offices. One values the land, one collects the money and one keeps the deed books, and the county's officials page lists them all.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7634, fax (606) 287-7079. Its listed role is keeping property records and assessing property.
  • Sheriff: P.O. Box 426, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7121. Collecting taxes heads the duties the county lists.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 339, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7800. Land records, meaning deeds and mortgages, plus transfers, are filed here.

The county site gives phone numbers and not a payment portal, so call the Sheriff to learn which payment methods and counter hours apply.

What dates matter for a Jackson County bill?

No local calendar overrides the statewide one. Under KRS 134.015 the bill is due by December 31, and paying everything by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount.

The regular Kentucky collection stages that Jackson County follows (source: KRS 134.015)
When paidResult
By November 12 percent off
November 2 through December 31Printed amount
January5 percent added
February onward10 percent added

A late mailing can lead Revenue to set an alternative schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff's collecting ends April 15, after which the Clerk holds whatever is unpaid. If your bill never arrives, phone the Sheriff, because a lost bill does not cancel a penalty.

How can a Jackson County owner dispute a value?

The first move is a conference with the PVA. KRS 133.120 treats it as a required first step, scheduled before or during the inspection period, and a telephone conference is available on request.

Still unsatisfied afterward? Mail or deliver a written petition to the County Clerk, naming your reasons and the parcel and stating what you think fair cash value is. It must arrive one workday after the inspection period closes. Rural owners should plan ahead, since the bill itself comes too late to contest.

A public hearing before the board of assessment appeals comes next. Collect the following beforehand:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

A petition without supporting facts can be denied. During the case, tax stays payable on your claimed value.

How much of a Jackson County house does the homestead exemption cover?

Nearly half. The $49,100 deduction for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, set against the Census middle home value of $111,500, leaves $62,400 to tax. That trims the base by about 44 percent.

Applicants need to be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and live in the house. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shown at the PVA proves age. Disability claims renew yearly, with exceptions for veterans with service-connected disabilities and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The deduction attaches to the owner's own residence. After moving, a seller should tell the PVA and file again for the new address.

Who pays when a Jackson County parcel sells with tax unpaid?

The seller should plan to settle it from proceeds. The tax is a personal debt dating from the assessment date, the lien on the land can last 11 years, and at the April 15 cutoff the Clerk files the bill as a certificate of delinquency.

Revenue's explainer gives the timeline. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, with a second within 60 if needed. KRS 134.128 sets the tax sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the Clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days before it.

Revenue's worked example shows the price of waiting: a $1,000 bill becomes a $1,254 certificate at transfer and costs $1,659.90 if paid after the June advertisement. Those totals assume a commission, so ask the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for the real number.

Where does a Jackson County deed get recorded, and what tax applies?

The County Clerk in McKee handles it. The same office issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and gathers the state transfer tax before taking a deed.

KRS 142.050 bills the grantor 50 cents per $500 of value. At $111,500, the Census middle value, the count is exactly 223 units, so the tax is $111.50. Gifts with nominal value, divorcing spouses and foreclosure transfers are among the exempt cases.

Ask the Clerk for the current recording fee before closing, since the statute sets that amount and lawmakers can change it.

What do household numbers say about Jackson County housing?

Jackson County's middle home value of $111,500 is less than half of Jefferson County's $248,400. The county counted 5,122 households in 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.53 people each, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

  • Monthly owner costs: $1,101 with a mortgage and $355 without.
  • Poverty rate: 22.0 percent.
  • Adults 25 or older with a high school diploma: 75.1 percent, and with a bachelor's degree: 8.8 percent.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 83.1 percent.
  • Veterans: 583.
  • Building permits in 2025: zero.

The Census recorded zero building permits for 2025, so new construction added no supply that year. Sellers here are almost always dealing with an existing house, and the assessment on it traces back to the PVA's January 1 value.

What is the Jackson County landscape like for a seller?

Jackson County sits where the Cumberland Plateau meets the Bluegrass, with ground from about 600 to 1,600 feet above sea level. It was formed in 1858 from parts of Madison, Estill, Owsley, Clay, Laurel and Rockcastle counties. McKee is the seat, and Annville is the largest community.

Karst ground in the north produces caves such as Wind Cave near the Turkey Foot campground, and the Middle Fork of the Rockcastle River rises in the south. Some 56,000 acres, about a quarter of the county, belong to the Daniel Boone National Forest, and the Sheltowee Trace trail has a trailhead in McKee. US 421 runs north toward Berea and Richmond and south toward Manchester. KY 30 links the county to I-75 and the Mountain Parkway. There is no hospital in the county, so residents drive to Berea, Richmond, London or Manchester.

  • 13,325 people lived here in 2025, a 2.8 percent gain on 2020.
  • 345.2 square miles of land, with 37.5 people per square mile.
  • Owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes.
  • $665 median gross rent and $40,000 median household income.
  • A mean commute of 37.7 minutes.

Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs, and the Jackson County Fair and Homecoming runs the weekend before Labor Day. Jackson Energy supplies power, and the Jackson County Water Association serves homes outside McKee.

More questions about Jackson County, KY Property Tax Guide

How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?

Write to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, or call (606) 287-7634. Fax goes to (606) 287-7079.

What is the discount for paying early?

Two percent off, provided the full bill is paid by November 1 as KRS 134.015 allows. Afterward the amount on the bill applies until the year ends.

What does a late payment cost?

The statute adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent after that. A bill unpaid at the April 15 cutoff moves to the Clerk, where monthly interest of 1 percent and commissions begin.

Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?

No. The exemption covers the home the owner lives in, so after closing the seller tells the PVA and files again for the new residence.

Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?

Yes. The County Clerk there files deeds and mortgages and collects the transfer tax of 50 cents per $500. Phone (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.

Who to contact in Lewis County

  • Lewis County Sheriff's Office

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Sheriff collects state, county and school property taxes; bill shows a schedule with 2% discount if received by earliest date; later payment costs more (exact dates not on page)
  • Bills go to owner of record as of January 1; homestead/disability exemption questions go to PVA (606) 796-2622

Tax rate

Selling in Lewis County?
We buy Lewis County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Where do Lewis County, Kentucky owners go about a property tax bill?

Two offices share one address in Vanceburg. Both sit at 112 Second Street, one in Suite 101 and the other in Suite 102, which makes it easy to settle a question about value and a question about payment in the same trip.

Lewis County tax offices in Vanceburg
OfficeWhat it doesLocationPhone
Property Valuation AdministratorAppraises real property, handles exemptions and address changes112 Second Street, Suite 101606-796-2622
Lewis County SheriffMails and collects the current-year bill for the state, county and school districts112 Second Street, Suite 102606-796-2912
Lewis County ClerkTakes over delinquent bills and hosts the appeal filingVanceburg, the county seatListed on the clerk's website

Some bills also carry charges for fire protection or library districts, which the sheriff collects too. The PVA's office page stresses what it does not do: it writes no laws and sets no rates. Those belong to the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, and the PVA only assigns value. Under state rules the office walks every parcel at least once each four years, and since 1992 it may measure the outside of a building with no one home.

What is Lewis County like beyond the tax office?

Up in Kentucky's northeast, Lewis County follows the Ohio River for more miles than any other county in the state. Across the water are Adams and Scioto counties in Ohio, and Greenup, Carter, Rowan, Fleming and Mason counties fill in the Kentucky side. Elevation climbs from 485 feet to 1,400, and oak cut from its wooded hills once ranked among the nation's best lumber.

Mason County gave up the land on December 2, 1806, and the new county took the name of the explorer Meriwether Lewis. The seat has moved twice: Poplar Flat held it first, Clarksburg from 1809 to 1863, and Vanceburg since. Vanceburg and Concord are the only cities, Garrison is the one census-designated place, and Tollesboro, Kinniconick and Laurel are among the many small communities. The 2020 count placed all residents in rural territory.

One school district serves the county, with four elementaries, in Vanceburg, Garrison, Tollesboro and Laurel, plus a middle school and a high school beside KY 10, the AA Highway. Tollesboro's own high school closed in 1994, a closure that stirred real controversy at the time. The county profile counts 814 jobs in health care and social assistance, 680 in construction and 600 in manufacturing, so lumber is no longer the lead.

  • Mean travel time to work: 38.6 minutes.
  • A typical owned home is worth $96,000, and 79.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.
  • Median rent: $751, and median household income: $46,838.
  • Headcount estimated at 12,901 in mid-2025, off 1.4 percent from the 2020 base.

How does the Lewis County sheriff want the bill paid?

The sheriff's page gives three routes. Mail the stub and a check to 112 Second Street, Suite 102, Vanceburg, KY 41179, pay in person at the office, or pay by debit or credit card over the phone or at the counter. Card payments add a fee tied to the bill's amount. Make checks out to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office, write the property ID from the bill on the check, and never mail cash.

Pay only the single figure in the "If Paid By" box at the bottom right of the bill. The subtotals for each taxing jurisdiction are shown for information, and separate payments for each would only cause confusion. A bounced check draws a $25 charge, and the late-payment tiers keep running while you replace it. If you overpaid, phone the sheriff, who may ask for paperwork before refunding. A single payment can cover several parcels as long as each stub is enclosed.

Statute sets the calendar. The state ladder is simple: a 2 percent reward for settling early in the fall, no adjustment during the last two months of the year, then a 5 percent charge in January and 10 percent beyond that. Your own statement prints the exact dollar figure for each window, so trust it over any summary.

What happens when a Lewis County tax bill goes unpaid past April?

Mid-April is the handoff. Whatever the sheriff has not collected by then goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a lien recorded against the house. After that the debt grows by a percent each month, plus commissions for the clerk and the county attorney.

The state's own illustration starts with a $1,000 bill. Clear it within five business days of the handoff and the total is $1,387.79, with the attorney's cut waived. Let the first attorney letter go out and it becomes $1,611.30. Investors can buy these debts at a clerk's sale, which in a usual year lands somewhere between July 14 and August 28.

One exception to the calendar: a bill covering property missing from the roll, or a value that went up on appeal, is payable the day it is drafted, and another 10 percent attaches after a month of silence.

How can I contest a Lewis County valuation?

Ask the PVA's staff for a face-to-face review first. No appeal is accepted without one, and it has to be held ahead of or during the public viewing period.

Viewing runs thirteen days from the opening Monday of May. Having met with the PVA, you can lodge the appeal at the clerk's office until the following workday ends. State law seats the review panel in the county seat, which puts Lewis County hearings in Vanceburg about four to five weeks after viewing wraps up.

  • The board hears only evidence presented with both you and the PVA present, so plan to attend or send an authorized representative.
  • Useful evidence includes photos, insurance policies, construction costs, an appraisal, and nearby listings or sales.
  • Audio recording is your right. The PVA may record only if it gives you written notice.
  • Skipping the board forfeits any later appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Who qualifies for the Lewis County homestead exemption?

The break is for people who live in the house and are either 65 or older or rated totally disabled. The statewide figure for assessment years 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before any rate is multiplied.

The sheriff's page points applicants to the PVA at 606-796-2622. A household gets one, even when both spouses qualify, and a manufactured house or a mobile home taxed as real estate can serve as the residence. After a sale the buyer files fresh, and the seller tells the PVA that title has moved.

What happens to the tax when a Lewis County house sells?

According to the sheriff, sellers typically cover a share at the closing table that matches their months of ownership, and the buyer writes the check for the whole bill when it comes. The closing paperwork shows how your deal split it. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow still lets the owner see the bill, and the owner stays legally responsible for it.

The bill is sent to whoever owned the property on January 1, unless a deed filed afterward carries specific tax bill instructions for the current year. Recording the deed also triggers Kentucky's transfer levy under KRS 142.050, half a dollar for each $500 of price, which the clerk collects. Foreclosures, divorce settlements and gifts from parent to child are among the exemptions. If a tax bill is delinquent, expect the title agent to require a payoff from the sheriff or the clerk before funds are released.

More questions about Lewis County, KY Property Tax Guide

Which phone line answers Lewis County tax questions?

Call the sheriff at 606-796-2912 about payment, and the PVA at 606-796-2622 about value or exemptions. Both offices are at 112 Second Street in Vanceburg.

Can I pay my Lewis County tax with a card?

Yes. The sheriff takes debit and credit cards over the phone or at the office and charges a convenience fee based on the bill's size. Checks go to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office with the property ID written on them.

What does a bounced check cost in Lewis County?

The fee is $25, and the late-payment schedule printed on the bill still applies when you send a replacement payment. Pay the amount for the date your funds actually arrive.

Does my mortgage lender handle the Lewis County bill?

Often, but you still receive a copy and remain legally responsible. If you think escrow covers it and you are unsure, ask the lender, and ask the sheriff if the bill is missing.

Who covers the tax when a Lewis County house is sold?

The settlement statement decides, and sellers usually cover a prorated share for the months they owned the house. The buyer pays the full bill when it comes, and unpaid back taxes must be cleared before the title is clean.

Ballard County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Ballard County, KY Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Ballard County, KY Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Ballard County, KY Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Ballard County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Ballard County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Ballard County

  • Ballard County Sheriff

Tax rate

Selling in Ballard County?
We buy Ballard County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where does Ballard County sit, and where did it come from?

Ballard County fills the far western tip of Kentucky where the Ohio River meets the Mississippi, in the Jackson Purchase. The county's own site calls it the ninety-third county formed, established February 15, 1842, from parts of Hickman and McCracken, and says it covers 254 square miles. Wikipedia's Census-based total is 274 square miles, including 27 of water.

The first seat was Blandville. A courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 burned most early records, and Wickliffe took over as seat in 1882. A buyer or heir tracing an old parcel can ask the County Clerk which books survive from before 1880.

Which towns and neighborhoods share the same tax offices?

Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are the four cities, and La Center is the largest. Bandana and Lovelaceville are census-designated places. All of the 2020 population was classed as rural, and a single school system, Ballard County Schools, covers the county. Axe Lake Swamp State Nature Preserve, 458 acres in the Barlow Bottoms, is part of a 3,000-acre wetland complex.

Across the Ohio River lie Pulaski and Alexander counties in Illinois, and across the Mississippi lies Mississippi County, Missouri. McCracken County, with the Paducah area, lies east of Ballard and Carlisle County lies south. Ballard is counted in the Paducah, Kentucky and Illinois metropolitan area.

Every one of these places pays through the same three courthouse-area offices:

  • Sheriff, 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe: bills and payments, (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: assessments and exemptions, (270) 335-3400.
  • County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: appeals and, later, unpaid bills, (270) 335-5168.

Is the Ballard County population rising or falling?

It is falling slowly. The population peaked at 14,378 in 1880, fell 41.6 percent to 8,390 by 1890, stayed between 7,900 and 8,800 from 1950 through 2010. By 2020 the count had slipped 6.3 percent to 7,728, and the 2025 estimate is lower again at 7,594. In 2020 there were 3,228 households. Single-person households made up 29.3 percent, and 14.8 percent were someone 65 or older living alone.

When does a Ballard County bill become late?

KRS 134.015 supplies one schedule for every Kentucky county, and Ballard County follows it unless the state allows a delay. Pay in full by November 1 and 2 percent comes off the bill. After that and through December 31 you pay the figure printed. In January 5 percent is added; after January, 10 percent.

The state revenue agency describes the aftermath. A bill unpaid at the end of the day on April 15 is passed to the County Clerk, which records a lien against the parcel. From then, interest accrues at 1 percent for each month, and clerk and county attorney fees are added. Under a delayed schedule each stage lasts a month, so confirm the dates with the sheriff's office.

How does a Ballard County owner's year run?

The Kentucky property tax year as it applies to a Ballard County parcel (revenue.ky.gov)
Month or windowWhat occurs
January 1Value date for real estate
January 1 to March 1Real property listing window
First Monday in May, 13 daysPublic inspection of the tax roll
Day after inspection endsLast day to file an appeal with the clerk
25 to 35 days laterLocal board hears appeals for up to five days
December 31Bills due without penalty

No new listing is needed when last year's roll described a property fully and correctly and nothing major changed. A buyer's deed price can serve as the listed value for the next January 1.

How does a Ballard County appeal work?

An appeal opens with a PVA conference at 132 North 4th Street; the clerk cannot take a filing otherwise. Then you have until the workday after the roll's inspection period closes to file at the County Clerk. State your own opinion of value on the form, because the bill relies on it if it is printed before a decision.

  • Evidence to bring: descriptions of the land and structures, insurance policies, construction costs, nearby sales listings.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you needs recognized credentials and your written authority.
  • You may audio-record the hearing.
  • A higher value set by the board produces a supplemental bill for the difference.

An owner who never files with the local board, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot take the case to a later stage.

Do older residents in Ballard County get a discount?

Owners 65 and over, or classified as totally disabled, claim Kentucky's homestead exemption through the Ballard County PVA. For 2025 and 2026 it subtracts $49,100 from the assessed value; the amount changes every other year. Plenty of residents might qualify: the 2020 census counted 21.4 percent of residents at 65 or above, with a median age of 44.8, and the 2025 estimate of 7,594 people sits 1.8 percent below the April 2020 base.

An owner who never applied might be paying tax on value the state would exempt. A call to the PVA at (270) 335-3400 settles it.

What does a Ballard County house cost, and who lives in them?

Census survey data for 2020 to 2024 show a middle owner-occupied home value of $145,800 and owners in 76.0 percent of occupied homes. Gross rent at the midpoint was $817 and household income at the midpoint was $66,164. The county had 3,209 households and 3,730 housing units in 2025. The 2020 count put the vacancy rate at 12.4 percent of units and a rental vacancy rate of 12.0 percent.

Employers are few: 155 establishments with 1,617 workers in 2023, up 19.2 percent in a year, paying $87.0 million. Commutes average 26.5 minutes, 15.9 percent of residents live in poverty, and 354 are veterans.

Retail sales were $56.7 million in 2022, about $7,415 per resident, and accommodation and food sales were $3.3 million. Among adults, 93.9 percent finished high school and 18.4 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more. Computers are in 95.0 percent of households and broadband in 87.6 percent, which helps owners who want to research a parcel or an appeal online.

Of 195 employer firms in 2023, 5 were minority-owned, the county has 510 nonemployer businesses, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Households average 2.35 people, 12.3 percent of residents under 65 report a disability, and 6.0 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance. No building-permit total was reported for 2025.

How do taxes work when a Ballard County house is sold?

Kentucky treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien, once recorded, can stay on the land for as long as eleven years whoever owns it. A closing agent therefore tends to pay the year's bill from the seller's proceeds. Ask how that year is divided with the buyer.

  • Sheriff: what is owed this year and in past years.
  • Clerk: whether a lien is on record.
  • Deed: add the next bill's mailing address, which KRS 382.135 requires.

Owners who inherited a river-county house or moved away and now owe back taxes can request a written cash offer. Any lien balance is paid out of the price.

More questions about Ballard County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay in Ballard County?

Payments go to the Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe. The county's page for elected offices lists (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

How much do I save by paying early?

Two percent of the bill, provided the sheriff has the full amount by November 1 (KRS 134.015). After that date the printed amount stands through December 31.

What if December 31 passes?

The bill picks up 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward. Once April 15 passes, the County Clerk holds it and interest of 1 percent a month runs.

Where is an assessment appeal filed?

File with the County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, after your PVA conference. Filing closes the workday after inspection ends.

Is the homestead exemption a county program?

No, the state runs it. The Ballard County PVA, (270) 335-3400, takes applications from owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and the 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100.

What is Hancock County, Kentucky like for someone selling a house?

Hancock County hugs the Ohio River on Kentucky's northwest side. Hawesville is the seat, Lewisport is the biggest town, and the river separates the county from Spencer and Perry counties in Indiana. The county was carved out in 1829 from slices of Breckinridge, Daviess and Ohio counties and carries the name of John Hancock. Its courthouse dates to 1868 and was renovated in 1978, and the county sits inside the Owensboro metro area.

Industry lines the riverbank. The county industrial foundation describes three aluminum plants and a paper mill, with over 2,000 workers between them, plus smaller manufacturers. Hawesville's 1902 railroad depot, where Harry Truman stopped during his 1948 campaign, is now the county museum and opens on Sundays from April through October. Vastwood Park covers nearly 400 acres on US 60 between Hawesville and Lewisport, with a 19 acre lake and a paved 1.1 mile trail.

The Census Bureau counted 15 building permits for 2025. A Hancock County seller is usually offering a resale house in a small market, where new construction rarely sets the price.

Which offices handle a Hancock County property tax bill?

Three offices share the Hancock County Administration Building at 225 Main Cross Street in Hawesville, and each has a separate job.

  • Sheriff, first floor: takes payment. Phone 270-927-6247, mail to P.O. Box 427. The posted hours are 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.
  • PVA: values property, and has no say over rates or payments. It reads the market each January 1 and aims for what a willing buyer would pay. Phone 270-927-6846, mail to P.O. Box 523.
  • County Clerk, second floor: keeps land records and processes delinquent real estate taxes. Phone 270-927-6117, mail to P.O. Box 146.

The state's Department of Revenue supervises the PVA's work and runs yearly studies in every county to check that assessments meet constitutional standards.

When do Hancock County tax bills fall due?

Bills reach the sheriff by mid September. Until then the PVA mails the current year bill to whatever in care of address appears in the deed. KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount for full payment on or before November 1 and sets face value for the rest of the year.

Miss that and January adds 5 percent. Past January 31 the penalty doubles to 10 percent and the sheriff tacks on another 10 percent, which the state describes as 21 percent combined. When the state delays mailing, an alternative schedule gives 30 days per stage instead. The bill in your hand carries the dates that apply.

Whoever owned the house on January 1 is the taxpayer of record for that year, so a closing in October or November is the moment to ask the sheriff for the exact discount cutoff.

What do the Census Bureau's numbers show for Hancock County?

Homeowners dominate and prices are modest, as the snapshot below shows.

About 20.6 percent of residents are past their 65th birthday, so a good share of Hancock County owners are old enough for the homestead exemption described below. With a typical home near $141,200, a few years of missed bills plus penalties can take a visible bite out of a sale price.

Do Hancock County rental owners owe an occupational fee?

Yes. The county's occupational tax page says every person or business with activity in Hancock County pays on net profits, and it names rental property owners, farmers and home based businesses in that group. The rate on business profits has been 1.60 percent since January 1, 2020, and an annual business license costs $10.

Employees working inside the county pay 1.60 percent of gross wages, withheld by the employer. Two exceptions apply: a company employing more than 100 people in manufacturing in the county does not owe the net profits fee, and neither does a business that pays the county a franchise tax.

A landlord selling a Hancock County rental should expect a net profits return for the year of the sale. The Occupational Tax Office, upstairs on the third floor, answers at 270-927-8788.

How can I contest a Hancock County assessment?

Meet the PVA first. Call 270-927-6846 to book a conference in the spring inspection window, which no appeal can skip. If the talk ends without a deal, you have one workday after the window closes to file with the clerk upstairs, along with the value you claim.

The local appeals board, three people, hears the case about five weeks later and expects evidence from you. The Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals hears anything further. Ask the PVA which sales it relied on, then bring your own comparable sales.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Hancock County?

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled, can ask the PVA to lower the taxable value of their own residence. KRS 132.810 allows one exemption per household unit and treats a manufactured house as a unit. After a sale, the old owner reports the transfer and the new owner applies separately. Ask the PVA for the dollar figure in force.

What should a Hancock County seller check before closing?

A short checklist keeps surprises away from the table.

  • Confirm the deed carries a mailing address for the new owner's tax bill, which KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Ask the sheriff whether a current year bill is open and who will pay it, since the bill covers a full calendar year.
  • Search the parcel through the clerk's website, which links a delinquent tax tool (DTax) and eCCLIX, a viewer for filed land records that helps when a house came through an estate.
  • Pull permits for any addition. Planning and Zoning is at 200 Court Square, P.O. Box 692, open Monday, Wednesday and Friday from 8 a.m. to noon at 270-927-8169.

The Hancock County Urban Planning Commission holds evening meetings every other month, starting the first Monday of February.

What happens to an unpaid Hancock County bill?

A bill still open when April 15 ends leaves the sheriff and lands with the clerk as a certificate of delinquency. The clerk's DTax tool shows what the county believes is owed on a parcel, with a warning that the clerk fixes the true figure at payment or sale. Interest, a clerk commission and later an attorney commission pile on, and a buyer of the certificate adds more. A seller who plans to list in summer should pay or collect a written payoff before certificate sales begin in July.

Back taxes do not block a sale. The settlement agent pays the payoff from the proceeds, the same way it works with a cash buyer who purchases as is.

More questions about Hancock County, KY Property Tax Guide

Do rental owners in Hancock County pay occupational tax?

Yes. Rental property owners pay on net profits at 1.60 percent, plus a $10 annual business license. The Occupational Tax Office at 270-927-8788 takes the forms.

When does the Hancock County Urban Planning Commission meet?

Every other month, starting with the first Monday of February. Meetings begin at 7 p.m. on the third floor of the Administration Building, 225 Main Cross Street.

How can I view recorded deeds for a Hancock County house?

Through eCCLIX on the County Clerk's website, which lets you view or print filed documents. Questions go to 270-927-6117.

I bought a Hancock County home and never got a tax bill. Who do I call?

The sheriff at 270-927-6247 can provide a copy. The PVA mails the bill to the address in the deed until preparation begins in mid September, which is why that address matters.

Is the PVA or the sheriff the office that takes the payment?

The sheriff. The PVA's role ends at valuation, and payments go to the Hancock County Sheriff's Office downstairs on the first floor.

Where can Nicholas County owners get answers on property tax?

Everything runs through the courthouse at 125 East Main Street, Carlisle. The PVA works from the basement, answers at 859-289-3735 and keeps hours from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays. The Sheriff's Office, at 859-289-3740, collects what is owed.

Mail to the PVA goes to P.O. Box 2, Carlisle, KY 40311. Its website carries the certified tax roll, a tax estimator, forms and a fee schedule, and the office says its goal is to help owners understand how assessments are built. The county's own sheriff page describes the job as public safety plus tax collection. Because the sheriff only collects, a dispute about a figure starts with the PVA.

How rural is Nicholas County for a homeowner?

Nicholas is among Kentucky's smallest and most rural counties. Carlisle is the seat and the only incorporated community, and the 2020 Census classed every resident as rural. Bourbon and Mason counties supplied the land in 1799, and 195 square miles of it are dry ground, with Bluegrass-style farms, wooded hollows and small villages.

History is close at hand. Forest Retreat, built in 1814, is a historic district on the National Register. A marker on U.S. 68 identifies the cabin Daniel Boone built in 1795 as his last Kentucky home. Blue Licks Battlefield State Resort Park, 148 acres shared with Robertson County near Mount Olivet, marks an August 1782 fight often called the last battle of the Revolution.

Jobs lie mostly elsewhere. Workers average 35.6 minutes to reach work, longer than in Montgomery, Muhlenberg or Nelson County. Only 82 employer establishments operate inside the county, with total employment of 415 in 2023, and retail sales for 2022 were $23,532 thousand, or $3,022 per resident. A buyer here is rarely tied to a local employer.

What does Census data show about Nicholas County housing?

The estimate for July 2025 is 7,949 people, up 5.5% from the 2020 base. In so small a county, a few sales can move the averages.

  • 3,355 housing units in 2025, and only 3 building permits that year.
  • Owners occupy 74.5% of homes in 2020 to 2024.
  • The Census midpoint for an owned house is $123,000.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,143 with a mortgage and $426 without.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $728.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $59,531, with 16.2% of people in poverty.

Only 9.8% of adults past 25 have a four-year degree, and 10.3% of people under 65 have no health insurance. About 92.6% of residents stayed in place last year, the highest share of the four counties in the Census comparison used for this guide.

Who lives in Nicholas County households?

The county has 2,776 households averaging 2.74 people, larger than in the other three counties compared here. Children under 18 make up 24.9% of residents and people 65 and over 18.2%. Census Bureau data show 237 veterans, 17.1% of residents under 65 with a disability and 81.6% of households with a broadband subscription.

Self-employment matters. The Census Bureau lists 611 nonemployer establishments for 2024, many times the count of employer firms, so a seller may be dealing with a farm, a trade or a home-based business that shares the property. Horse farming also shapes the landscape: the 1954 Kentucky Derby winner Determine was bred on Forest Retreat Farm in the county. A seller with acreage should ask the PVA how land, barns and the house are classed on the roll before comparing values.

What does Nicholas County charge by date paid?

The PVA site announced that 2026 bills would be mailed on or about October 1, 2026. Payment steps follow KRS 134.015.

Nicholas County bill totals under the state due-date statute
Date paidConsequence
No later than November 1Two percent off the total
November 2 through year endThe total printed on the bill
During JanuaryFive percent added
Past January 31Ten percent added

The statute stops at 10%, though the Montgomery, Muhlenberg and Nelson County sheriffs each post 21% for the stretch between February and mid-April. Call 859-289-3740 for the figure that applies on your payment date.

Take an $800 bill. It costs $784 with the discount, $800 through December and $840 in January. At a 21% penalty it would be $968. The same statute describes the tax, fees, penalties and interest as a personal debt of the taxpayer from the assessment date until paid.

What steps lead to an assessment appeal in Nicholas County?

Ask the Nicholas County PVA or a deputy for a conference. KRS 133.120 requires it first, before or during the inspection window or any extension. The PVA must explain the constitutional and statutory rules and how the value was reached, and the office logs what was discussed.

KRS 133.045 keeps the tax roll open 13 days beginning the first Monday that falls in May. An owner who stays dissatisfied delivers a letter or petition to the County Clerk with the parcel, the reasons and an opinion of fair cash value, by the workday after the window closes. At the county hearing, an owner may record the audio. Filing never postpones payment. You pay on your stated value, and the final value decides what else is owed, with interest.

What homestead relief can Nicholas County seniors claim?

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, may claim the state deduction of $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026. Applied to the county midpoint of $123,000, it leaves $73,900 to be taxed. The PVA takes the application in the courthouse basement. Disability claims renew yearly, except for service-connected veterans and for owners found permanently and totally disabled by the federal Social Security Administration or the state retirement system.

Who receives the bill after a Nicholas County purchase?

According to the PVA, both value and ownership are pinned to the first day of January. A house bought afterward is billed to the previous owner until the next calendar year. The PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer using information from a tax agreement signed by buyer or seller. A buyer who receives none can get a copy from the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

  • Seller: confirm the current bill is paid and keep the receipt.
  • Buyer: have a mailing address entered on the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Both: put the year's tax split into the contract.
  • Estate sales: the executor lists heirs and estimated values in an affidavit at the County Clerk's office.

Unpaid tax can outlast a sale. KRS 134.015 says the lien from a delinquent bill runs up to eleven years under KRS 134.420, whoever holds title. A seller who suspects an old year is open should ask the sheriff before listing, and a buyer's title agent will want the answer anyway. With only three building permits issued in 2025, most buyers here are weighing older houses, so a clean tax record is one less thing to negotiate.

More questions about Nicholas County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where does Nicholas County keep its PVA?

The PVA works from the courthouse basement at 125 East Main Street in Carlisle, with weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 and a phone at 859-289-3735.

Who gets a Nicholas County bill after the house sells?

The previous owner is billed until the next calendar year, and the PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer. A buyer with none can call the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

How much does paying early save in Nicholas County?

Two percent, if the whole bill is paid by November 1. After that the printed total is due through December 31.

What penalty follows January in Nicholas County?

KRS 134.015 sets 5% for January and 10% after January 31. Ask the sheriff for the exact payoff, since sheriffs elsewhere in Kentucky post 21% for the late winter and spring stretch.

What does the homestead exemption remove in Nicholas County?

The state takes $49,100 off assessed value once a qualifying owner applies at the PVA. Qualifying means 65 or over, or totally disabled, and the figure covers tax years 2025 and 2026.

What makes Carroll County, Kentucky, different for a house seller?

Carroll County is a small river county where the Kentucky River meets the Ohio, and its seat, Carrollton, sits at that confluence. At 128.68 square miles of land it is the third-smallest county in Kentucky by area, and the 2020 Census counted 10,810 residents. Carrollton lies about 54 miles from Cincinnati and 55 from Louisville along U.S. 42, with Interstate 71 about four miles south of town.

That location shapes who buys here. The county's own website lists employers such as North American Stainless, CertainTeed and Kentucky Utilities, and describes General Butler State Resort Park, a 791-acre park, as a local draw. Jefferson Community College serves the county. A house in Carrollton is often sold to a worker commuting along the river or I-71 corridor, and Carrollton itself was laid out in 1792 under the name Port William.

The city itself is compact, about two square miles with 3,890 residents in 2020. Prestonville lies across the Kentucky River to the west, and Switzerland County, Indiana, sits across the Ohio to the north. The county's own site adds that the Kentucky Veterans Memorial is in Carrollton and that boats launch from Point Park.

Carrollton's worst recorded flood was the Ohio River flood of 1937, with a crest of 79.9 feet, according to Wikipedia. Sellers of low-lying homes near the river should ask the city planning office for floodplain information.

Which Carroll County office does what with a tax bill?

A parcel is valued by the PVA, billed by the Sheriff's Office, and handed to the County Clerk if it goes delinquent. The county's clerk page lists those delinquent collections beside recording deeds and mortgages and filing wills and probate orders.

  • Sheriff: first floor of the courthouse at 440 Main Street, (502) 732-7010, with online tax lookup and payment through the sheriff's page.
  • County Clerk: same building, (502) 732-7005, for delinquent taxes and deeds.
  • County administration: (502) 732-5448, the office that edits or exonerates county tax amounts when a bill looks wrong.

Carroll's FAQ puts the annual due date at December 31 and expects bills in October or November. An owner who has seen nothing should look the bill up on the sheriff's page. In the state's description, most counties begin collecting on October 1 or November 1. The exact discount cutoff is printed on the bill, and the sheriff's office can confirm it.

Can Carroll County owners split payments or get a late fee waived?

Neither. The county FAQ rules out a payment plan and requires the whole bill in one transaction. It also says that a bill that never arrived is not a permitted ground for waiving late fees under the state's administrative regulations.

Mixing tender is fine, such as part check and part cash or card. The penalty ladder comes from KRS 134.015:

  • On or before the discount date: 2% off.
  • Until December 31: the printed amount.
  • During January: 5% on the unpaid tax.
  • Past January 31: 10%.

The debt also becomes a lien. A Carrollton house with a past-due bill will be flagged by the buyer's title company, so line up the clerk's payoff figure early.

How does a Carroll County tax sale work?

After April 15 the sheriff hands unpaid bills to the County Clerk, and a sale comes at least 90 days afterward. KRS 134.128, summarized on the state's collection page, puts the sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, with notices to the owner at 30 and 60 days.

The clerk sold Carroll's 2025 delinquent taxes on July 24, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. on the courthouse's second floor, with third-party purchasers registering by July 14, 2026. Questions go to the clerk at (502) 732-7005. A buyer who purchases a certificate may add substantial fees, which is why owners fare better paying before the sale.

In the state's first example, a $1,000 bill paid within five business days of reaching the clerk costs about $1,388 once interest, a clerk commission and a recording fee are added. Waiting brings in the county attorney's commission, postage and advertising costs.

How can a Carrollton owner appeal a value?

Ask the PVA for a conference, then file with the clerk once the roll closes. The roll stays open 13 days after the first Monday in May, and an appeal is valid only after a conference with the PVA or a deputy, as the state calendar sets out.

The PVA must send notice whenever it assesses above the value you listed. A deed price can also serve as the listed value for the next January 1 if the property has not changed. For a Carroll County seller who bought recently, that means the purchase price may be the PVA's starting point, so keep your closing statement.

The local board owes a written explanation for any increase or decrease, and you may record the hearing. Do not skip it, since not filing or not appearing ends your right to further review.

Which exemptions are open to Carroll County homeowners?

The homestead exemption is available on a primary residence to owners aged 65 or more and to owners who are totally disabled. One state form, 62A350, covers both, and the PVA keeps it on file.

It deducts a set dollar amount from the assessed value, not the entire value, and the amount is reset every two years. A buyer cannot inherit it. Veterans with a total service-connected disability file once, as do owners found disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement System.

Ask the PVA for the current dollar amount, because the dollar figure published on the state's page covers a past assessment period. A seller who is 65 should confirm the exemption was applied before closing.

What do the numbers say about Carroll County homes?

A typical owner-occupied house in Carroll County is valued at $140,900 for 2020 to 2024, between Caldwell's $118,500 and Calloway's $183,200. Owners live in 65.7 percent of homes, the second-lowest share of the four counties, and the 2025 estimate of 11,141 residents is 3.1 percent above 2020.

Employers in Carroll County reported 6,600 jobs in 2023, with total payroll near $497 million, and employment rose 4.7 percent from 2022. Only 11.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 17.3 percent of residents live in poverty, figures that sit beside the county's $140,900 median home value. Sellers who cannot wait for financing, or who are managing an estate or a rental with tenants, can sell as-is for cash and pay the tax payoff from the proceeds.

What is the Carroll County tax deadline?

December 31 is the annual due date, with a discount for bills paid by the early cutoff printed on your bill. January adds 5% and anything later adds 10%.

Does Carroll County allow a payment plan?

No. The county requires the full amount in a single transaction, though check, cash and card can be combined.

Whom do I call about delinquent Carroll County taxes?

The County Clerk, at (502) 732-7005, collects delinquent real estate taxes and runs the sale.

Is a late fee waived if my bill never came?

No. The county FAQ lists a missing bill as an impermissible reason for a waiver. Look the bill up on the sheriff's page each fall.

Can a Carrollton house with back taxes be sold?

Yes. A buyer can take it as-is and the payoff is paid from your proceeds at closing. Get the figure from the County Clerk before you sign.

What shapes the housing market in Harlan County, Kentucky?

Harlan County lies in southeastern Kentucky against the Virginia line. Harlan is the county seat, Cumberland is the largest city, and Benham, Evarts, Loyall and Lynch complete the six incorporated places. Black Mountain, east of Lynch, rises 4,145 feet and is the state's highest point. Three streams, Poor Fork, Clover Fork and Martins Fork, meet at Baxter to start the Cumberland River. It dates to 1819 and carries the name of Silas Harlan, a frontier soldier.

Coal built the economy. The first coal left by rail in 1911, and the population rose from 10,566 in 1910 to 75,275 in 1940. Every count since 1980 has been lower, down to 26,831 in 2020 and an estimated 24,725 in July 2025. Mining jobs dropped from 13,619 in 1950 to 764 by June 2016.

A seller here is entering a market that has shrunk for decades. That affects the price more than it affects the tax bill, but it decides how much cushion a house has when unpaid taxes or repairs come out of the proceeds.

How low are Harlan County home values?

The 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey figures from Census put the typical owned home at $73,700, roughly half of Hancock County's figure and a third of Hardin County's. Owners live in 71.6 percent of the housing, typical rent is $678 a month, typical household income is $41,693, and 29.4 percent of residents live below the poverty line.

The county has 13,136 housing units against 10,731 households, which is about 2,400 more units than households, and the Census recorded zero building permits for 2025. Around one resident in five is past 65, and 21.4 percent of residents under 65 report a disability. Both groups are the ones the Kentucky homestead exemption is written for.

On a $73,700 house the yearly tax bill is small in dollars. The real risk is a string of unpaid years in which interest and fees grow faster than the home's value.

Which Harlan County offices do I deal with?

Each office keeps its own schedule, so call before you drive in.

  • Sheriff: collects the bill. The sheriff's website links to an online public tax lookup. Call for the discount and penalty dates printed on your bill.
  • Property Valuation Administrator: write to P.O. Box 209 in Harlan (ZIP 40831) or call (606) 573-1990 between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.
  • County Clerk: phone (606) 573-3636. Monday it stays open until 6 p.m.; Tuesday through Friday it closes at 4:30; and on the last Saturday of the month, holiday weekends excepted, it opens 9 a.m. to noon.

The clerk's website has a delinquent taxes page and a third party purchaser application. The PVA's website carries the tax roll and a property search showing assessments and owners. Harlan County's fiscal court is led by the county judge executive and five magistrates, one for each of five districts that run from Bledsoe and Pine Mountain to Pathfork.

What is the real estate tax calendar in Harlan County?

The PVA's website posts the state's cycle in a single chart.

How the Kentucky tax year runs for real estate, from the Harlan County PVA chart
StepWhen
Assessment dateJanuary 1
Listing periodJanuary 1 through March 1
Tax roll open for review, conferences with the PVA13 days beginning on the first Monday of May
Appeals board hearingsFive days, beginning 25 to 35 days after review closes
Bills delivered to the sheriffNo later than September 15
Discount paymentsBy November 1
Payments at face valueNovember 2 through December 31
Bills turn delinquentJanuary 1, with 5 percent through January 31
10 percent penalty and 10 percent sheriff add onAfter January 31
Sheriff passes bills to clerkApril 15
Clerk's certificate salesJuly 14 through August 28

A state ordered delay can move a county to a slower plan with 30 days for each stage, so the dates on your own bill control.

How do I question a Harlan County assessment?

Start with the PVA. A conference in the May inspection window is mandatory, and when it produces agreement the new value flows into the fall bill.

Without agreement you have until one workday after the window shuts to file at the clerk's office. A three member local board, appointed by the largest city's mayor, the fiscal court and the county judge executive, meets about five weeks after inspection. It must reject a claim that comes with no facts, so gather sales of similar houses and repair estimates beforehand.

At these values an appeal pays off mostly when the PVA's record is wrong about something concrete, such as a bedroom count, a shed that no longer exists, or a fire damaged building still carried at full value.

Does the buyer get the Harlan County bill after closing?

Not automatically. The bill for a year goes to the January 1 owner, so a later sale leaves it in the seller's name for that year. According to the PVA, staff read the recorded deed and mail the bill to the new owner when they can. A buyer without a copy should call the sheriff.

List a mailing address the buyer will check in the deed, since the clerk cannot take a deed without an in care of address for that year's bill. A seller on the homestead exemption should also tell the PVA, since the exemption does not go to the buyer.

What does a Harlan County bill cost once it is delinquent?

A bill still open when April 15 closes passes to the County Clerk, and a monthly 1 percent interest charge starts. The Department of Revenue's example uses a $1,000 bill.

  • On transfer, with the penalty, sheriff add on and an assumed commission: $1,254.00.
  • Paid within five business days: $1,387.79.
  • Paid after the county attorney's first notice: $1,611.30.
  • Paid after the June advertisement: $1,659.90.

Notices come by mail, and installment plans can be requested before a certificate is sold. If a third party buys it, the owner pays that buyer, who can add substantial fees.

An owner with unpaid years can still sell. The closing agent gets the payoff from the clerk and pays it from the proceeds. A cash offer on an older house can be weighed against a listing by comparing what is left after the payoff.

Which schools and nearby places affect a Harlan County sale?

Two public districts operate here. Harlan Independent Schools serves the city of Harlan, and Harlan County Public Schools covers the rest, with Harlan County High School in the Rosspoint area east of Harlan. Southeast Kentucky Community and Technical College has its main campus in Cumberland.

Part of Cumberland Gap National Historical Park and the Blanton Forest preserve lie in the county, so a house near them may draw outdoor minded buyers. School district boundaries, city limits and fire protection can change the taxes on a bill, so ask the sheriff which districts appear on yours.

More questions about Harlan County, KY Property Tax Guide

What is the last day for the Harlan County discount?

November 1. After that, the chart lists face value through the end of December and a 5 percent penalty in January.

How much extra does a February payment cost in Harlan County?

Ten percent in penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff add on, both of which start once January ends. The state describes the total as 21 percent.

Who answers questions about my Harlan County assessed value?

The PVA at (606) 573-1990 handles the conference that must come before any appeal.

Where do I check for delinquent Harlan County taxes?

The County Clerk's website has a delinquent taxes page, and the clerk's office answers at (606) 573-3636. The sheriff hands over bills after April 15.

Can a Harlan County owner under 65 get the homestead exemption?

Yes, if totally disabled. The statute, KRS 132.810, opens the exemption to age 65 and up, or total disability, for owners living in the home, filed with the PVA.

Selling in Letcher County?
