Which offices value, bill and collect Letcher County property tax?

Letcher County runs its tax through a valuation office, the sheriff and the clerk. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's value. The Letcher County Sheriff sends out the bill and receives the payment. The Letcher County Clerk inherits anything still unpaid in mid-April.

The PVA sits at 156 Main Street, Suite 105, in Whitesburg, with a phone line at 606-633-2182 and a fax at 606-633-3995. Its page on the statewide PVA portal explains that ownership, like value, is fixed on January 1, so a house bought in March still shows the seller on that year's bill. A new owner who never sees a copy can phone the sheriff at 606-633-2293.

The county government site gives the sheriff's weekday hours as 8:30 to 4 and links to a web page for paying the bill. The clerk, at 606-633-2432, keeps the same hours and runs a delinquent tax section. Phone the clerk to learn when the current year's tax sale is scheduled.

What kind of place is Letcher County for a seller?

It is a mountain county where the land shapes everything, including how a house is priced and how long it sits. Letcher County is tucked into Kentucky's southeastern tip. Pine Mountain stretches 125 miles and runs down the county's center, Black Mountain tops out near 3,700 feet along the Virginia line, and national forest covers a big slice of the acreage.

The first permanent settlement dates to 1803, at the mouth of Pert Creek where Whitesburg now stands. Lawmakers created it in 1842 from pieces of three older counties, Harlan, Perry and Pike, and gave it the name of the sitting governor. Courthouse history tells the story in miniature: a log building finished in 1844, a brick one in 1898, a modern one dedicated in 1965 and remodeled in 1998. Whitesburg is the seat, Jenkins is the biggest city, and Fleming-Neon makes three. Blackey, Mayking, McRoberts, Millstone and Payne Gap are unincorporated.

Coal drove the boom. Before mining the county never topped 10,000 people, and by 1940 it had passed 40,000. The Scotia mine explosions of March 1976 killed 26 miners and led to the federal mine safety act the next year. More recently the July and August 2022 floods killed three people here and left others homeless. If a building was damaged, ask the PVA how that damage shows up in the assessment.

  • Letcher County Public Schools covers most addresses, with its high school in Whitesburg.
  • Jenkins Independent Schools covers the Jenkins area, with an elementary school in Burdine and a combined middle and high school.
  • US 119 climbs Pine Mountain between Jenkins and Whitesburg, and US 23 skirts the eastern edge.
  • Fishpond Lake near Jenkins, the Pioneer Horse Trail and the recreation center draw weekend visitors, and the Mountain Heritage Festival has run since 1983.

How inexpensive are Letcher County homes, by the federal numbers?

Homes here are inexpensive, mostly owner-occupied and rarely new. The federal QuickFacts table for the county shows a population that has slid while households stay fairly stable.

Letcher County snapshot from the federal QuickFacts table
ItemFigure
People counted in 202021,548
People estimated for July 202519,952 (down 7.4% from the 2020 base)
Households, 2020-20248,463
Share of homes occupied by owners74.1%
Typical value of an owned home$67,400
Middle monthly rent$669
Residents 65 or older21.9%
Building permits in 20251
Land area337.93 square miles

With so few permits, nearly every sale is a resale, and buyers compare each house against a small set of older homes. A tax bill on a $67,400 home is small in dollars, which is why a few years of neglect can feel manageable until the penalties compound.

When is the Letcher County bill due, and what happens after the deadline?

Kentucky's collection statute, KRS 134.015, sets one calendar for every county, and the sheriff here follows it. Anyone who settles the full amount by November 1 gets 2 percent off. Between early November and year end the bill is payable at face value. January adds 5 percent, and February onward adds 10 percent plus the sheriff's fee. If the state delays a county's bills, it can swap in a schedule that allows a month per stage.

Closing time on April 15 is the cliff. The sheriff passes the unpaid list along, every item turns into a certificate of delinquency, and a lien goes on record against the house. Monthly interest of one percent starts, and the clerk and county attorney each earn commissions that climb as notices go out.

The Revenue Department's own sample shows the pace of growth. A $1,000 bill reaches the clerk at $1,254 once the penalty, fee and commission are added. If it is still open after the June newspaper ad, the sample total is $1,659.90. Investors can then buy the debt at a public sale three to four and a half months after the handoff, and the lien can last eleven years whoever owns the house.

How can I appeal a Letcher County assessment?

Begin with a sit-down at the PVA's office. The appeals panel refuses any case that skipped that meeting, and the meeting must happen before or during the viewing window.

The roll opens for public viewing on May's first Monday and stays open thirteen days. Once you have held your conference, you must file with the Letcher County Clerk by the end of the workday that follows the window. The local appeals panel then sits in Whitesburg, the county seat, roughly a month later, within 25 to 35 days of the window closing.

  • Bring proof: building and land details, insurance policies, what construction cost, and listings of similar houses. An appeal with no evidence is denied.
  • A paid advocate has to be a lawyer, accountant, consultant, broker, appraiser, your own employee or a holder of a state-recognized designation, and needs your authorization in writing.
  • Audio recording is allowed, and the panel must explain any change in writing.
  • If bills were printed before the ruling and the value rises, a supplemental bill follows.

Can a Letcher County senior or disabled owner cut the tax bill?

Yes, through the homestead exemption. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100 off a home's taxable value. A house assessed at $120,000 would be taxed as though it were worth $70,900.

The home must be the applicant's residence, and the applicant must either reach 65 during the tax year or hold a total disability rating from a federal program or a retirement system. About 22 percent of residents are past 65, so plenty of owners may qualify. Apply at the Letcher County PVA. Disabled owners under 65 generally renew every year, except service-connected veterans and people ruled permanently disabled by the Social Security Administration or the state retirement system, who document it once. A buyer cannot inherit the break, since the exemption belongs to the person.

What does a Letcher County seller owe at closing?

The bill follows the January 1 titleholder, and the settlement statement decides who reimburses whom. A common Kentucky practice is for the seller to credit the buyer for the months of ownership, with the buyer paying the full bill when it arrives.

Kentucky also charges a transfer tax under KRS 142.050: a rate of $0.50 on every $500, or fraction, of the price stated in the deed, billed to the grantor and collected by the clerk at recording. Foreclosure transfers, spouses splitting in a divorce and nominal parent-child transfers are exempt. Because delinquent tax is a lien, closing agents insist on paying it out of the proceeds. Request a payoff figure from the sheriff before closing, and ask the clerk whether any parcel has been certified as delinquent.

More questions about Letcher County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who gets the Letcher County tax payment?

Send it to the Letcher County Sheriff, who answers at 606-633-2293 on weekdays from 8:30 to 4. The county website also links to an online payment page. Anything unpaid after April 15 shifts to the county clerk.

Is there an early-payment discount in Letcher County?

Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 of the tax year takes 2 percent off. After that the printed amount is due until December 31, and penalties of 5 and then 10 percent follow.

I bought in Letcher County and no bill came. What now?

Phone the sheriff at 606-633-2293 and ask for a copy. The bill is written to whoever owned the parcel at the start of the year, so it may carry the seller's name, and a missing bill leaves the debt in place.

Who hears a property tax appeal in Letcher County?

A local board of assessment appeals hears it in Whitesburg, after you have met with the PVA at 156 Main Street, Suite 105 and filed with the clerk. The filing deadline is the workday after the thirteen-day roll inspection ends.

Who pays the year's tax when a Letcher County house changes hands?

The settlement statement decides. The sheriff bills the January 1 owner, and sellers commonly credit the buyer for their months of ownership. Delinquent amounts are a lien that has to be cleared for the title to pass clean.

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky

Who to contact in Livingston County

Tax rate

Selling in Livingston County?
We buy Livingston County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Which Smithland offices deal with Livingston County property tax?

Livingston County splits the job three ways, and every office is in or near the courthouse square in Smithland. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) fixes each parcel's value. The Livingston County Sheriff, who also handles court security and civil papers, collects the bill. The Livingston County Clerk steps in once a bill is certified as delinquent.

The sheriff's office is at 321 Court Street (PO Box 340, Smithland, KY 42081), answers at 270-928-2122, and opens its doors from 8 to 4 on weekdays. The clerk, at the same street address with a separate box (PO Box 400), takes calls at 270-928-2162 and runs a slightly longer Monday, 8 to 5, and 8 to 4 Tuesday through Friday. The PVA mails from PO Box 77 and lists 270-928-2524 in the state's directory of valuation offices.

Because the PVA does not set rates or take payments, each question has a natural first call. Dispute a value or ask about an exemption with the PVA. Ask about the amount owed or a payoff with the sheriff. Ask about a recorded lien or a tax sale with the clerk.

How do the Census numbers describe a Livingston County house?

Livingston is a small rural market with settled households. The federal QuickFacts table reports the following for 2020-2024 unless noted.

  • The middle owner-occupied home is worth $125,600, and owners live in 81.2 percent of the county's homes.
  • Median gross rent is $926, and median household income is $58,984.
  • One resident in four, 25.1 percent, is 65 or older.
  • The 2020 census counted 8,888 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 8,863 is almost flat.
  • Few people move in a given year, since 93.8 percent stayed at the same address.

Stability like that means listings are few, and buyers often come from nearby Paducah. The county is part of the Paducah metropolitan area, and the Ledbetter community sits directly across the Tennessee River from that city.

What is Livingston County's setting, and how did Smithland start?

The county touches rivers on almost every side. The Ohio River forms its border with Illinois, and the county seat of Smithland sits at the confluence of the Ohio and Cumberland, which is why water covers 8.5 percent of the total area of 342 square miles. Kentucky formed the county in 1798 from Christian County and named it for Robert R. Livingston, a member of the committee that drafted the Declaration of Independence. The county keeps Central time.

Smithland takes its name from John Smith, sent in the late 1790s to scout the river junction for a land company. A plat laid out in 1805 was not recorded until 1837, and the county says that same plat still locates lots in town. The earthquake of December 16, 1811 along the New Madrid Fault shook the river town, and the county's own history page recounts how residents fled into the streets as chimneys fell.

Livingston County communities and what the county government says about them
CommunityStatusPopulation noted
SmithlandCounty seat, city301 in 2010
SalemSixth-class city752, down from 769 in 2000
CarrsvilleSixth-class city on the Ohio River50 in 2010
Grand RiversCity between the Cumberland and Tennessee riversNot listed
LedbetterCensus-designated place, largest community1,683 in 2010
BurnaUnincorporated, home to North Livingston Elementary and the middle schoolNot listed

Grand Rivers is the one place in the county that voted to allow alcohol sales, in 2016. The rest of Livingston County is dry.

When is the Livingston County tax bill due?

State law gives owners until December 31 of the assessment year, with a discount for early birds. The discount is 2 percent for a full payment made by the first of November. The next two months carry the plain amount, January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies after that. If the state approves a late schedule for a county, each stage lasts about a month instead.

The sheriff turns over what remains on April 15. At that point the clerk records the lien, and the debt picks up 1 percent monthly interest. The Department of Revenue's walk-through of a $1,000 bill shows $1,254 at the handoff. Pay in May after a second month of interest and the sample reaches $1,627.61. A buyer at the clerk's sale pays $1,704.21 in the same example, and that figure becomes the base on which the buyer later charges interest and fees.

Before any sale the clerk must run the delinquent list in a newspaper and on a county-sponsored site, and the county attorney mails a 30-day warning to each owner, with a second warning if needed. Ask the Livingston County Clerk for the date of the current sale and for the list of bills certified as delinquent.

How does the PVA arrive at a value, and can a farm owner pay less?

Kentucky recognizes three main methods. For homes the PVA leans on the sales comparison approach, adjusting nearby sales up or down for differences such as a basement. Barns, fences and commercial buildings are valued at replacement cost minus depreciation. Rental properties are valued by the income they produce.

Rural parcels get special treatment. Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, farmland is assessed at agricultural value, not market value, so the state's own example taxes an acre that would sell for $50,000 on an agricultural value of $750. The Revenue Department builds per-acre values for cropland, pasture, woodland and waste ground. Ask the PVA whether a parcel is classed as farm use before assuming a market-based figure.

  • Federal, state, county and city property is exempt, as are schools run by nonprofits and religious institutions' buildings and personal property.
  • A nonprofit or religious group applies on Revenue Form 62A023 through the PVA, and a denial can go to the local board.
  • Every parcel gets a physical look from the PVA's staff at least every four years.

How can I appeal a Livingston County assessment?

You have to talk to the PVA first, and the talk has to happen before the inspection period ends. Public viewing of the roll starts the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. After your conference, the clerk needs the paperwork by the end of the next workday. The board then sits at the county seat, Smithland, 25 to 35 days later.

Evidence wins or loses these cases. The board considers only what is presented while both sides are in the room, and it denies an appeal that arrives without documents. Photographs of the building, its construction cost, insurance policies, nearby listings and sales all help. A paid representative must hold one of the credentials Kentucky lists, such as attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, and present your written authorization. If the board changes a value, it must explain why in writing, and a value that rises after bills have printed produces a supplemental bill.

Can Livingston County seniors cut their bill, and what happens at a sale?

Yes. With a quarter of residents past 65, the homestead exemption matters here. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 it removes $49,100 from the assessed value of the owner's home, so a house assessed at $175,000 is taxed on $125,900. Apply through the PVA, bringing a license, birth certificate or passport that proves your age. A buyer cannot inherit the exemption and must file separately.

The year's bill belongs to the person who held title when January 1 arrived, and the closing statement divides the cost. The seller also owes Kentucky's transfer tax under KRS 142.050, $0.50 on each $500 of price, which is collected as the deed is filed in Smithland. Foreclosure transfers and transfers between divorcing spouses are among the exemptions. A delinquent amount stays attached to the property as a lien for up to eleven years, so expect the title agent to want it paid first.

More questions about Livingston County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where is the Livingston County sheriff's tax office?

Find it at 321 Court Street in Smithland; mail goes to PO Box 340. Call 270-928-2122 on a weekday between 8 and 4.

What phone number reaches the Livingston County PVA?

The state directory lists 270-928-2524 for the Livingston County PVA, whose mailing address is PO Box 77, Smithland, KY 42081. Call it about values, exemptions and ownership records.

Does Livingston County give a discount for paying early?

Yes. Pay the full bill by November 1 and it drops by 2 percent. Past that date you owe the printed amount until year end, and then penalties begin.

What happens to a Livingston County tax bill I never pay?

The sheriff sends it to the clerk after April 15, and a lien goes on record with interest and commissions piling up. Investors may buy the debt at a sale a few months later.

Is farmland taxed differently in Livingston County?

Yes. Kentucky assesses farmland at agricultural value rather than market value, using per-acre figures for cropland, pasture and woodland. Ask the PVA whether your acreage qualifies as farm use.

Selling in Menifee County? Get a Cash Offer

Who to contact in Menifee County

  • Menifee County Sheriff

Tax rate

Who handles property tax for a Menifee County house?

Three Frenchburg offices share the chores here. An elected appraiser, known as the PVA, values each house. The sheriff mails and takes in the bill. The clerk receives whatever remains unpaid when April 15 closes. Match your question to the right desk and a payoff figure or a corrected value comes faster.

The PVA, clerk and county attorney all list 12 Main Street on the county website, while the sheriff keeps a post office box of its own.

What is Menifee County like for someone selling a house?

Menifee is mountain country, with roughly 204 square miles of land carved out on May 29, 1869 from Bath, Montgomery, Morgan, Powell and Wolfe counties. Frenchburg is both seat and sole city, and its charter dates to 1871 according to the county. Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge flank the county, and Lexington is under 70 miles away via the Mountain Parkway.

National forest land takes up much of Menifee, and cultivated farms cover about a tenth of it. Sellers here mostly offer hillside lots, small tracts and cabins. The county website names tourism, forestry, small business, farming and public service as the economy. Menifee belongs to the Mount Sterling micropolitan area, and the school district office is on Wynn Flat Road in Frenchburg.

A March 2, 2012 EF3 tornado cut through Menifee and neighboring counties, and three people were killed in the region. A lender may ask about storm repairs on an older house, so keep permits and receipts together.

What do Census figures say about Menifee County housing?

Menifee counted 6,113 residents in 2020, a dip from 6,306 a decade earlier, and a mid-2025 estimate of 6,430 would be a 5.2 percent bounce. The 2020 count tallied 3,277 housing units, 24.3 percent of them empty, and classed the entire county as rural.

The five year survey adds these points:

  • Owners live in 75.5 percent of the homes.
  • Monthly owner costs run $996 with a mortgage and $299 without one.
  • Broadband reaches 81.2 percent of households, so ask what internet a remote address can get.
  • A worker's average trip to the job takes 29.8 minutes.
  • Per capita income is $25,879, and covered employment was just 454 jobs in 2023, up 3.9 percent from a year earlier.
Menifee County snapshot from the Census Bureau's five year survey (2020 to 2024)

Which Menifee County offices should you contact?

Every office keeps its own mailing box, so double check the address before anything goes in the mail.

  • Sheriff: collects the bills. P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, (606) 768-3875.
  • PVA: values, exemption forms and conferences. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 36, (606) 768-3514.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and the desk where appeals are filed. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 123, (606) 768-3512.
  • County Attorney: delinquent bill notices and payment plans. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 545, (606) 768-2606.

Call ahead for office hours before you drive in.

What are the Menifee County payment deadlines?

The sheriff runs the statewide calendar found in KRS 134.015. Bills arrive in the fall and follow whoever held title on January 1.

  • Through November 1: pay 2 percent less.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the bill as printed.
  • During January: 5 percent extra.
  • February 1 to April 15: the state shows a 21 percent combined penalty.
  • After April 15: the clerk holds it.

A house sold later in the year still carries the earlier owner's name on that year's bill. Settle the split in the contract and ask the sheriff for the balance.

How do you contest a Menifee County property value?

Sit down with the PVA first, and go to the clerk only if the two of you cannot agree. Inspection starts on the first Monday in May and lasts two weeks, and filing closes one workday later.

A local board then hears the case within 25 to 35 days and gets five sitting days without state permission. Revenue officials say a claim without evidence must be denied, so bring paper.

  • Photos and contractor quotes for a worn roof or a shifting foundation on a slope.
  • Prices that comparable houses nearby fetched this past year.
  • Insurance policies or construction costs.

Audio recording of the hearing is allowed. A paid representative must belong to a group listed in KRS 133.120 and carry your signed authorization.

Is there a homestead break for Menifee County seniors?

Yes, for owners aged 65 or older and for those classified as totally disabled. File at the Menifee County PVA for the house you occupy. Each residential unit gets just one exemption under KRS 132.810, and manufactured homes qualify as units.

The exempt amount tracks a federal price index, so ask the PVA for the current figure. An approval granted after you paid brings a refund on the exempt slice. A sale or a death must be reported, and whoever takes the house files anew.

What happens when a Menifee County bill is not paid?

When April 15 ends, the sheriff passes the bill to the clerk and a lien goes on record. Interest starts at 1 percent each month, with a 10 percent clerk charge and a 20 percent county attorney charge on top. The clerk may sell the certificate to an outside investor from mid-July onward.

The county attorney can arrange installments before a sale. Afterward you answer to the investor, who may add large fees. Under the statute the January 1 owner owes the tax personally, and the lien can ride with the parcel for 11 years.

How are cabins and short-term rentals taxed in Menifee County?

A 4 percent transient tax applies to short-term rentals, and the county's Departments page links the registration form and the monthly return. With Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge nearby, plenty of cabins fit that description.

A buyer who plans to rent will want those filings in order. If you hosted guests, gather your returns and tell the buyer what you filed. The county tourism office on that page can explain how a new owner registers.

Can a Menifee County house with tax owing still be sold?

Yes. An open bill, or one already at the clerk, turns into a payoff number that the sheriff or clerk will quote. Once the bill is at the clerk the number climbs monthly, so it is worth getting a fresh quote close to closing.

Homes here are often inherited, remote or in need of work. The median household income of $45,096 is the lowest among the four counties in the Census table, and 23.6 percent of residents live below the poverty line. To compare a listing with a cash offer, subtract repairs, carrying costs and back tax from each. Get the payoff in writing before you accept anything.

More questions about Menifee County, KY Property Tax Guide

Whom do I pay for Menifee County property tax?

Pay the Menifee County Sheriff at P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, phone (606) 768-3875. Write the bill number on a mailed payment.

Which date ends the penalty-free window in Menifee County?

December 31. A bill paid by then costs its printed amount, and January adds 5 percent.

Where is an assessment appeal filed in Menifee County?

At the county clerk's office, after a conference with the PVA. The filing is due one workday after the May inspection period ends.

Does Menifee County give older owners a tax break?

Yes, through the Kentucky homestead exemption for owners 65 or older who live in the house. Apply at the PVA, 12 Main Street in Frenchburg.

Can the county take a house over a small unpaid bill?

After April 15 a lien is recorded, and collection may include selling the certificate to a private buyer. Speak with the county attorney early about installments.

What we confirmed on official pages

Who does what on a Mercer County tax bill?

Three offices on West Lexington Street in Harrodsburg handle Mercer County tax. The PVA appraises each parcel, the sheriff takes in the payment, and the county clerk files liens and picks up any bill still open once April 15 passes.

By the sheriff's own account the office collects more than $8,000,000 a year, so tax is a big share of its workload. Houses inside Harrodsburg also get a city bill, explained below.

What kind of place is Mercer County for a home seller?

Mercer sits in the Bluegrass of central Kentucky on roughly 249 square miles of land. The county was cut from Lincoln County, Virginia in 1785 and carries the name of General Hugh Mercer. Harrodsburg, the seat, was the first city formally chartered in what was then Kentucky County, according to Wikipedia. Burgin is the second city, and Salvisa is counted as a census designated place.

Visitors come for Old Fort Harrod State Park, the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill with its 30 or more historic buildings, and Herrington Lake. The Louisville Southern Railroad reached Harrodsburg in 1888. Neighbors are Anderson, Woodford, Jessamine, Garrard, Boyle and Washington counties.

The Census Bureau lists 132 building permits for Mercer County in 2025, so some buyers will compare an older house with a new build.

How big is the Mercer County housing market?

The 2020 count came to 22,641 people, up from 21,331 in 2010, and the Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 23,733. Housing units number 10,824.

The 2020 through 2024 survey adds:

  • Owner occupancy is 75.9 percent.
  • Owners paying a mortgage spend a median $1,373 a month on housing, against $497 for owners with none.
  • Broadband reaches 86.8 percent of households.
  • Workers travel 27.2 minutes on average to reach a job.
  • Density is 90.9 people per square mile, well above the 30.0 to 35.5 seen in Menifee and Metcalfe.

Where do you go in Mercer County to pay, appraise or record?

Contact details from the county pages and the PVA site:

  • Sheriff: bills and payments, at 207 W. Lexington St., with a mailing box at P.O. Box 126, Harrodsburg, KY 40330. Phone (859) 734-4221. Doors are open 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, and a box at the entrance accepts payments left after hours.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption forms. Same street address, P.O. Box 244, phone (859) 734-6330, same weekday schedule.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and delinquent bills. Courthouse address, P.O. Box 426, phone (859) 734-6310.

The PVA site has a public property search with limited detail, and a paid subscription opens the full database.

Why do Harrodsburg homeowners get two tax bills?

A house within Harrodsburg pays two governments. The city sends its own bill, and the county sheriff bundles the county, state, library, extension, soil conservation, health and school taxes. City Hall says mailings go out at the end of September.

Harrodsburg publishes its 2025 levies, quoted per $100 of assessed value:

  • City of Harrodsburg: 0.063
  • Kentucky state: 0.106
  • Mercer County: 0.116
  • Library: 0.064
  • Extension office: 0.042
  • Soil conservation: 0.010
  • Health department: 0.050
  • Mercer County schools: 0.705

The city works a sample: a $200,000 assessment produces $126 of city tax. Levies are revisited annually, so rely on the figures printed on your bill.

When must a Mercer County tax bill be paid?

The sheriff's page lays out this calendar for 2026 bills. It mirrors KRS 134.015, with the county's own wording for the later penalty.

  • Oct. 1 to Nov. 1, 2026: 2 percent comes off.
  • Nov. 2 to Dec. 31, 2026: pay what is printed.
  • January 2027: a 5 percent penalty.
  • Later: a 10 percent penalty, with a further 10 percent sheriff fee on payments made between Feb. 1 and April 15.

Whatever is still open moves to the county clerk when business closes on April 15, 2027. The sheriff asks anyone who gets no bill to phone the office. Bills arrive on a white postcard with a yellow strip, which is easy to mistake for junk mail.

What is the route for disputing a Mercer County value?

Ask for a PVA conference during the inspection window, a 13 day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A conference that ends in disagreement leads to a filing at the county clerk's office, where you state your own figure.

A three person board takes up appeals about a month after the window ends and opens by examining recent sales of similar homes. If you hire someone to speak for you, KRS 133.120 limits the choice to lawyers, CPAs, licensed brokers or appraisers and similar professionals, plus your own employees, and that person needs your written authorization.

Mercer County mixes town lots, farms and acreage on one roll, so choose sales of homes like yours. A farm house on acreage and a town lot do not compare well.

Which Mercer County owners qualify for the homestead exemption?

Age 65 or older, or a total disability classification, opens the door, and the exemption covers your own residence. The sheriff's page tells them to call the PVA at (859) 734-6330 if they have not signed up.

KRS 132.810 allows one exemption for each residential unit and treats a mobile home as a unit. Your assessment cannot go up because of the value you write on the application. Disabled owners under 65 reapply yearly, except service connected totally disabled veterans and people found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

What happens if Mercer County tax goes unpaid?

Once April 15 passes, the clerk issues a certificate of delinquency and a lien attaches. Interest builds at 1 percent monthly, and the clerk (10 percent) and county attorney (20 percent) add their fees. The Department of Revenue's sample turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 at transfer and roughly $1,611 after the attorney's first notice.

Outside buyers may purchase certificates beginning in mid-July. After a sale you pay that buyer, and added fees are possible. Before a sale, payment plans run through the county attorney.

How does the January 1 rule affect a Mercer County sale?

January 1 fixes tax ownership. The Mercer County PVA explains that a buyer who closes later in the year still sees the bill issued to the former owner until the next calendar year, though the office tries to send the new owner a copy based on the recorded deed.

That shapes every closing. A buyer without a bill can ask the sheriff for one, and the contract should name who covers the year's tax. For an older bill at the clerk, ask for a payoff figure before picking a closing date.

More questions about Mercer County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where is a Mercer County tax bill paid?

At the sheriff's office, 207 W. Lexington St. in Harrodsburg, or by mail to P.O. Box 126. Payments can also go in the box at the entrance after closing time.

Does the sheriff also collect Harrodsburg city tax?

No. City Hall bills its own levy, and the sheriff's bill covers county, state and school taxes plus the library, extension, soil and health districts.

When does the early payment discount end?

For 2026 bills the 2 percent discount ends November 1, 2026. After that, the printed amount is due through December 31.

Is there a refund if I qualify for the homestead exemption after paying?

Yes. KRS 132.810 entitles a person who qualifies after paying to a refund on the exempt portion.

Whose name is on the bill if I closed after January 1?

The prior owner's, until the next calendar year. A new owner can call the sheriff at (859) 734-4221 for a copy.
